These improvements also persist with a stronger backbone, demonstrating the effectiveness of visual marking across different model capabilities. Overall, SelfMark provides a unified approach to visual reasoning by integrating spatially grounded marks directly into the visual feature space of MLLMs.

papers.title: A Bleichenbacher bit-by-bit oracle attack from partial message knowledge
papers.abstract: Oracle attacks show the importance of a correct implementation of cryptographic standards when translated into code. A notable example is the Bleichenbacher attack on RSA with PKCS#1 v1.5 padding and all the improvements that have been suggested over the decades. This paper shows how an attacker knowing a few least significant bytes of an RSA message can take advantage of a server with an oracle side-channel to decrypt the full message bit by bit. We will consider two oracles that can be tested with chosen ciphertexts: one revealing whether the decrypted message starts with the 00 02 bytes and a second one revealing if the decrypted message is fully PKCS compliant. For an attacker knowing the three least significant bytes of the message, the first oracle provides an attack where one oracle call gives the next least significant bit of the message and the second an attack which requires, with high probability, a small constant number of oracle calls to the oracle, with a constant which depends on the length of the message and the desired probability of success. The attack divides the message bits into two sections, one with the known part and one with the unknown part, and then chooses transformations that will keep the unknown part, except for the last unknown bit, orders of magnitude below the integer coming from the known part. The resulting string either gives a valid padding or not depending on the value of the unknown bit. The attacker can minimize the number of oracle calls at the cost of some local computation. Finally, the same method is adapted to show how it can also be used to extract the few least significant bytes of the message with an increased cost where the main complexity is finding a second valid message with a correct padding starting from the original captured ciphertext.

papers.title: Medicaid Quality Disparities: Domain-Specific Performance Analysis and Approaches for State-Level Improvement
The Manifold-Index Model: provably and efficiently avoiding the statistical and computational curse of dimensionality
papers.abstract: We study vector-valued regression with predictors filling a tube around an unknown $m$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal{M}$ in $\mathbb{R}^D$. In the Manifold-Index Model, the mean response is $F=f\circ\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$, where $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is the nearest-point projection onto $\mathcal{M}$ and $f:\mathcal{M}\to\mathbb{R}^p$ is a possibly non-injective link function. Multiscale ANisotropic lOcal Regression (MANOR) estimates tangent planes by multiscale PCA of predictors with similar responses, then refines them by pooling outer products of local slopes. The neighborhoods narrow tangentially while retaining complete normal fibers. We assume a Lipschitz link differential and bounded response noise. For $p\ge m$, under our geometric and sampling conditions, $n$ independent observations give mean tangent-space error of order $n^{-2/(m+4)}$ and integrated squared prediction error at the $m$-dimensional nonparametric rate $n^{-4/(m+4)}$, up to logarithmic factors. In a scaling regime with fixed intrinsic dimension, model and scale parameters, and ratio of manifold volume to the $m$-th power of its reach, the required sample size grows polynomially in $D+p$, and computation is polynomial in $n$, $D$ and $p$. Numerical experiments on curves with non-monotone links and surfaces with vector-valued responses compare observed convergence rates with the theoretical bounds; a Langevin dynamics example tests prediction of hitting probabilities under an approximate manifold-index model.

papers.title: Beyond AUC: Do Mammography Risk Models Predict When Cancer Occurs?
papers.abstract: Longitudinal deep learning models for mammography-based breast cancer risk prediction output either per-year cumulative risks or a discrete distribution over the year of diagnosis, from which cumulative risks F1,...,F5 are derived. These models are evaluated almost exclusively with year-wise AUCs and the concordance index. We show that these metrics are largely insensitive to when cancer occurs: they can be high even for a model that carries no information about the year of diagnosis. We re-evaluate two recent longitudinal models (OA-BreaCR, LMV-Net) on CSAW-CC with a 5-year horizon using timing metrics computed on cancer cases only. Despite C-indices up to 0.75, neither orders cancer cases by time to diagnosis significantly better than chance (c_time 0.51 and 0.55, both 95% CIs covering 0.5). Weighted absolute timing error favours a constant "year 3" prediction over both models, so we use c_time as the primary timing metric. For Mirai's additive-hazard head, also used by LMV-Net, we analyse how per-year increments passed through a ReLU can collapse under severe class imbalance. We also propose a breast-level, two-stage model that separates whether from when. It matches LMV-Net in discrimination (C-index 0.745 vs. 0.746) but orders cancer cases better (c_time 0.58 vs. 0.51, paired 95% CI of the difference 0.01-0.13), on par with Mirai's published weights (0.57).

papers.title: DexFormer 2.0: Towards a Cross-Embodiment Foundation Policy for Dexterous Grasping
papers.abstract: Dexterous grasping policies are usually trained for one arm paired with one hand. Every new pairing then needs its own policy, and the number of policies grows with every arm and hand added. We ask whether a single policy can control many arm-hand combinations and transfer to pairings and hands it has never seen. This is hard because robots differ in the number, layout, and dynamics of their joints, so their observations and actions share no common interface. We present DexFormer 2.0, a single reinforcement learning policy for cross-embodiment dexterous grasping. It maps every robot to a canonical joint interface with validity masks, encodes each joint's morphology with attention biased by the kinematic tree, and uses a Transformer-XL memory to infer embodiment-dependent dynamics from recent interaction. Trained on 18 combinations of four arms and six hands, it reaches 89% stable success on seen combinations and 51% on six held-out arm-hand pairs, outperforming GRU and DexFormer 1.0 baselines. Without fine-tuning, it also grasps with four new hand types and, through retargeting, with parallel grippers. Ablations show that memory, the kinematic-tree bias, and broader pairing coverage each matter for transfer. On a physical Flexiv arm, distilled students transfer zero-shot from simulation with two hands, including a held-out pair. Project website: this https URL .

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, I: the mass matrix and the polygon model
ANNA: Attention-Free Neural Neighborhood Aggregation for Channel Estimation on Regenerative NTN Payloads
papers.abstract: Accurate deep learning (DL)-based channel estimation (CE) for non-terrestrial network (NTN) uplinks must meet the processing, power, and latency constraints of regenerative payloads. We propose Attention-free Neural Neighborhood Aggregation (ANNA), a lightweight architecture combining per-resource block (RB) pilot projection, convolutional neighborhood aggregation, and shared reconstruction, with dense-grid expansion only at the output. Evaluation against learned and classical estimators uses paired waveform-generated datasets with receiver frequency correction enabled and disabled. With correction enabled, 16-bit floating point (FP16) deployment on a 10 W Jetson Orin NX achieves 0.372 ms 99th-percentile (P99) latency and 2.15 dB lower mean normalized mean-squared error (NMSE) than the fastest learned baseline at 29.6% higher latency. Relative to the most accurate learned baseline, ANNA is 4.08 times as fast and consumes 80.5% less module energy per sample, with a 1.14 dB accuracy penalty. It meets the adopted 0.5 ms P99 target in all 100 benchmark runs, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-latency-energy trade-off for embedded uplink CE.

papers.title: Ramsey sets are canonically Ramsey
Self-supervised learning for zebrafish embryo phenotype evaluation: Systematic comparison of algorithms, label-efficient classification, and transfer learning
papers.abstract: Zebrafish embryos are a prominent model organism for image-based phenotyping and especially suited for large-scale imaging studies, for which machine learning (ML) models can automate evaluation. However, training ML models usually requires large labeled datasets, and differences in imaging conditions often impede reuse across laboratories. Self-supervised learning (SSL) addresses both constraints by learning transferable representations from unlabeled images. Yet central aspects like the choice of algorithm remain underexplored for domain-specific applications. To close this gap, we benchmark popular SSL algorithms on the public EmbryoNet dataset, explore label-efficient learning, and test transfer to an unseen setting. Using representations from our strongest model, a ResNet50 network trained with SwAV, a simple linear classifier reaches 86.4% accuracy and a non-linear classifier 87.1%, rivaling the fully supervised EmbryoNet model (87.1%). The SwAV model decisively outperforms supervised training from scratch when labels are scarce (70.2% vs. 45.7% accuracy with 5% of labels). On a three-class problem (normal, dead, falsely cropped) with a small, previously unseen zebrafish toxicity dataset, recorded in a different setting, our model reaches 81.3% accuracy without retraining, while EmbryoNet achieves 75.9%. Overall, self-supervised models for zebrafish embryos seem to mostly facilitate label-efficiency and transfer to new settings rather than improving supervised results.

papers.title: GNN-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Coastal Emergency Response under Extreme Water Levels
papers.abstract: When a storm surge approaches a coastal town, the emergency plan must be put into action quickly using water-level forecasts, flood extent, road access, vulnerable residents and shelters. Bringing this information together under time pressure is slow and depends on the duty officer's expertise. This paper is one step in a wider research line from data to safe decisions: machine learning to understand the hazard, reinforcement learning and planning to choose actions, large language models (LLMs) to explain and cross-check them, and an assurance layer that keeps people in charge. Here we address the action step on a real place. We ask whether a policy can learn the timing of emergency actions from decades of real events. Lido di Venezia is represented as a heterogeneous graph built from public elevation, road, building and census data and driven by hourly tide-gauge records from 1983 to 2024, with seven actions taken from the municipal emergency plan. A PPO policy is trained on this graph and compared, on storm windows unseen in training, with a rule-based system simulating the officer's discretionary decisions. On 18 historical test scenarios, PPO achieves a similar reduction in population exposure to the rule. With uncertain forecasts and limited protection it again performs similarly but does not outperform the tuned rule, and removing graph message passing does not substantially reduce performance. PPO therefore learns an effective protective response from an outcome-based reward alone: it is given the plan's actions and when each is allowed, but not the thresholds that tell the comparator when to act. Next steps test harder edge cases, move closer to a digital twin of the territory, and replace the simulated officer with assessment by emergency-management stakeholders, supported by LLM-based interpretation of each recommendation.

papers.title: Borel combinatorics of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$-shift actions and hypersmooth equivalence relations
Three-Dimensional Impact Angle Control Guidance Law with Field-of-View Constraint
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel impact angle control guidance law to address the challenge of achieving any desired impact angle while satisfying the seeker's Field Of View (FOV) limit and maintaining acceleration continuity. The guidance problem is decomposed into two two-dimensional (2D) engagement planes. In the first plane, a pure proportional navigation guidance (PNG) law is employed toward a virtual target to align the missile velocity vector with the line-of-sight (LOS) to the target. In the second plane, a two-stage time-varying biased PNG (TVBPN) strategy is utilized to accurately shape the trajectory and achieve the desired terminal impact angle while maintaining compliance with FOV limitations. The position of the virtual target point ensures a smooth and continuous lateral acceleration at the transition between the first and second stages. The effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed law were validated through numerical simulations.

papers.title: Geometry-Derived Capacitance Dyadics with Floquet Sideband Correction for Anisotropic Periodic Patch Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Homogenised sheet models describe periodic metallic patch layers using a scalar sheet capacitance, which is only valid when the effective response is isotropic. An isotropic response exists for unit cells with patch geometries that have rotational symmetry of order three or higher. Lower-symmetry unit cells with irregular or random geometries generically require a full 2 x 2 surface-capacitance dyadic. We present a framework that computes this dyadic directly from the arbitrary gap-connected patch geometry on a unit cell of a hexagonal lattice. The two-dimensional Bravais periodicity fixes the two independent macroscopic loading directions, the connectivity of the gap ensures a full-rank response for the geometries considered here, and the point-group symmetry of the patch constrains the form of the dyadic. A quasi-static boundary value problem on a single periodic cell then determines its independent entries. We use the surface-capacitance dyadic in the anisotropic surface- wave dispersion relation, which includes the leading spatially-dispersive first shell Floquet-sideband correction. For each new patch geometry, the dyadic and the first-shell correction are obtained from a single quasi-static cell problem and from the reconstructed boundary. So anisotropic surface- wave dispersion follows without a per-geometry full-wave eigenmode band sweep or sheet-tensor retrieval. We validate this geometry-to-dispersion chain against full-wave eigenmode simulations across six representative symmetry classes, showing that the correction captures band flattening near the Brillouin-zone boundary and improves agreement relative to the local dyadic model.

papers.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
Self-doped correlated adatom lattices on cubic boron nitride
papers.abstract: We survey triangular adatom lattices on the (111) surfaces of cubic boron nitride (cBN) for strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems. Using density functional theory combined with the constrained random phase approximation and charge self-consistent dynamical mean-field theory, we identify twelve promising candidates. Group-III (group-V) adatoms on the N- (B-)termination realize clean one-band Hubbard systems, while group-III and transition-metal (V, Cr, Mn) adatoms on the B-termination realize two-band Hubbard systems. Importantly, the polar III-V character of cBN induces self-doping by $\pm 1/4$ electron away from integer filling. With strong Hubbard (and Hund's) interactions and small hoppings, most systems are doped Mott insulators. Heavy quasielectrons with mass renormalizations up to 4 and strong local moments up to 2.5 $\mu_B$ put our systems into a regime where unconventional superconductivity on the triangular lattice has been predicted.

papers.title: A counterexample to the subgraphings approximate the cost problem
Estimating Outpatient Visit Prices from Hospital Price Transparency Data using Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Objective: Hospital care prices in the United States have increased substantially, yet patients lack effective tools to access and compare costs. We aimed to develop and evaluate an LLM-based approach for improving access to and use of hospital price transparency (PT) data. Materials and Methods: To estimate visit prices, we used a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework to analyze PT files from three major hospitals in Maryland and the surrounding region. We compared BM25, OpenAI embedding models, and a GPT-BM25 hybrid against a no-RAG baseline for cost estimation of individual procedures and procedure groups, then evaluated the best approach for symptom-based visit cost estimation using synthetic simulations. Results: Across hospitals, the GPT-BM25 retriever achieved the best performance, with average price MAPE of 19.44% for individual procedures and 4.90% for groups, compared with 147.98% and 82.82%, respectively, for the no-RAG baseline. In simulations, our framework correctly identified approximately 50% of reference procedures and reduced MAPE relative to the LLM-only baseline at two of the three hospitals, while achieving comparable performance at the third. Discussion: Our framework uses RAG to improve care price estimation in real-world settings. Compared with the no-RAG baseline, it substantially improved cost estimates for both individual procedures and procedure groups. Improvements were smaller in synthetic simulations, likely because inferring procedures from clinical information is more complex. Practical challenges remain, including heterogeneous PT file formats, unexplained duplicate entries, and limited availability of insurer-negotiated rates. Conclusion: LLMs that effectively integrate PT data show strong potential to provide patients with more accessible and accurate healthcare cost estimates.

papers.title: Oxygens breathe, electrons jump
papers.abstract: Electronic transport in polyanionic battery cathodes proceeds through small-polaron hopping between transition-metal sites and is commonly assumed to be tightly coupled to the motion of charge-compensating mobile ions. Using olivine Li$_x$MnPO$_4$ as a prototypical platform, we use first-principles molecular dynamics with extended Hubbard functionals to follow, in real time and at finite temperature, the adiabatic evolution of Mn oxidation states and atomic sublattices. We find that polaron hopping and cation migration are dynamically decoupled: Mn$^{2+}$/Mn$^{3+}$ valence exchanges occur frequently while the intercalated ions remain confined to their sites, and hopping is gated by the local oxygen framework. Freezing the six oxygen atoms of an individual MnO$_6$ octahedron excludes that site from the hopping network, while increasing the fictitious oxygen mass slows down electronic transport. Each valence exchange coincides with a concerted breathing of the donor and acceptor octahedra ($\Delta V \simeq 2$ $Å^3$), with their volume asymmetry crossing zero at the transition, consistent with the Holstein-Marcus coincidence condition. The hopping rate yields an activation energy of $E_a = 0.20 \pm 0.03$ eV, closely matching the elastic energy scale of the two coordination cages ($\lambda_V/4 \approx 0.20$ eV). These results identify the oxygen coordination cage, not the mobile cation sublattice, as the dynamical gate for small-polaron transport: a site can accept the electron only if its cage can breathe, and the barrier is governed by cage elasticity. Selective constraints and mass scaling applied to first-principles dynamics provide a general route to link electronic and lattice degrees of freedom in redox-active materials, opening the door to framework engineering in intercalation and mixed ionic-electronic conductors.

papers.title: Scaling large language model-assisted line-of-therapy adjudication with human-in-the-loop evidence-calibrated selection
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled the ability to scale clinical adjudication tasks traditionally dependent on exhaustive manual review. Line-of-therapy (LoT) adjudication, a major bottleneck in oncology cohort construction, is a prime example. Line boundaries must be inferred from longitudinal treatment histories according to nuanced, study-specific definitions, at every regimen transition for every patient. LLMs can apply this adjudication at scale, but their reliability varies across patients. Treatment histories differ in complexity, and ambiguous or atypical patterns depend on expert clinical judgment. Reliable automation thus requires verified support for model assignments and the ability to identify cases that warrant manual review. Here, we present evidence-calibrated selection (ECS), a human-in-the-loop framework for scaling LLM-assisted LoT adjudication. ECS derives confidence from observed clinician adjudications, prioritizes patients with the least-supported assignments for follow-up review, and returns completed adjudications to the model as precedent. As the evidence base grows, ECS continuously calibrates confidence to estimate residual error, thus enabling more efficient use of clinician time. In simulations on 136 clinician adjudicated patients with multiple myeloma, ECS achieved a residual error of 5% after review of 44.6% of patients, compared to 62.2% when review was directed by LLM self-reported confidence and 81.9% under random sampling. These results support a scalable approach to study-specific LoT adjudication, using clinician evidence to inform automated predictions, minimize error, and reduce review burden.

papers.title: Microfitting: Continual Learning via Cached Test-Time Training
papers.abstract: Continual learning is a promising approach to specialize language models to an organization's private data. However, current methods exhibit a number of drawbacks including catastrophic forgetting, where new training updates overwrite prior knowledge. We present microfitting, which trains and caches a small adapter for each document. Each adapter is trained once, offline, on synthetic questions targeted at demonstrated base-model shortcomings and reused whenever that document is queried. This method borrows from test-time learning literature and sidesteps the problem of continual learning through parameter isolation, allowing the system to specialize on new data without overwriting prior knowledge. The process that generates adapter training data also improves over time, revising its recipe from previous outcomes and fresh examples of the target workload. On DeepSeek V4 Flash, microfitting substantially improves accuracy over the base model. In Enterprise Document Operations (EDO), an open-book Q&A environment over real-world enterprise documents, our method achieves a 38.2% relative improvement over base-model performance. Microfitting makes continual specialization practical and cost-efficient: a frozen model can adapt to an evolving private corpus overnight on local hardware, without modifying the base model or previously cached adapters.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Non-Monotone Submodular Maximization under a Cardinality Constraint with Constant Recourse
papers.abstract: We study the maximization of a nonnegative submodular function under a cardinality constraint when elements arrive one at a time and an algorithm must report a feasible set after every arrival. The recourse of an algorithm is the largest number of insertions and deletions that it makes to the reported set at a single arrival. For every $\epsilon>0$, we give an algorithm with recourse $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ whose reported set has, at every time, expected value at least $1/4-\epsilon$ times the largest value of a feasible set of arrived elements. The algorithm evaluates the function polynomially often, and only on sets of arrived elements. We also show that no algorithm with constant recourse achieves a ratio above $1/4$, even if it knows the function and the arrival order in advance and has unlimited computation, and that any fixed ratio above $1/4$ requires recourse that grows as a positive power of the cardinality budget. Thus $1/4$ is the optimal limiting ratio with constant recourse. The previous best ratio with constant recourse was $3-2\sqrt2\approx0.172$. Our algorithm assigns selection probabilities of at most one half and maintains, as elements arrive, an inequality bounding the value of every feasible set by a multiple of the expected value of a random set drawn with these probabilities; the reported set moves to a rounding of these probabilities through gradual replacements. The upper bound uses a weighted directed graph whose vertices arrive in groups of decreasing sizes.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Stochastic Contraction Induced by Common White Noise
papers.abstract: This paper studies contraction properties of stochastic dynamical systems governed by Itô stochastic differential equations. We consider two trajectories driven by a common noise process and measure their separation using Finsler distances, which encompass Riemannian and norm-induced distances. Two notions of contraction are then investigated: $L^p$-contraction, defined by exponential decay of the $L^p$-norm (or the $p$-th moment) of the distance, and almost sure contraction, defined by exponential decay of the distance along almost every sample path. Each notion is characterized by a differential condition that is necessary and sufficient for contraction under mild hypotheses. Relations between contraction notions and an associated incremental input-to-state stability result are also established. As an illustration, we apply the established theory to analyze noise-induced synchronization and quantify its robustness with respect to parameter perturbations.

papers.title: Deep Sequence Model for Genome Wide Discovery of Coding and Regulatory Element Signatures
papers.abstract: Interpreting deep neural networks for genomic sequence classification remains challenging despite strong predictive performance. We develop a lightweight CNN with post-training gradient-based analysis to identify which sequence positions drive coding versus intergenomic classification. Applied to the standardized demo_coding_vs_intergenomic_seqs dataset, our model achieves 91.87% validation accuracy while revealing interpretable patterns: nine hot spots with consistently high importance, clear class-specific separation at positions 20-100 (coding) and 150-190 (intergenomic), and a strong mean-variance correlation (r = 0.530) indicating robust discriminative features. Gradient-based importance analysis shows that the model implicitly learns biologically meaningful sequence distinctions without explicit annotations. This work demonstrates that neural network interpretability and accuracy can coexist, providing a framework for understanding genomic sequence classification and enabling biology-driven hypothesis generation.

papers.title: VoxMel TTS Technical Report
papers.abstract: Continuous autoregressive TTS relies on an acoustic target that enables stable next-latent modeling while preserving fine-grained acoustic details. While existing approaches employ learned compressed representations (e.g., continuous VAE latents) to render prediction tractable, they rely on complex neural encoders that often cap generation fidelity. Conversely, training-free targets like mel-spectrograms eliminate encoder overhead, yet their potential for autoregressive generation remains largely underexplored. In this work, we propose VoxMel, a tokenizer-free framework for autoregressive TTS that makes stable mel modeling tractable through a fixed, exactly invertible two-axis Haar transform. The transform first decomposes each mel spectrogram along frequency into local averages and a frequency residual, then splits the averaged component along time into Coarse-Mel and a temporal residual. A language-model backbone with a flow-matching head autoregressively generates Coarse-Mel. Non-autoregressive residual tiers then predict the temporal residual from Coarse-Mel, followed by the frequency residual conditioned on the reconstructed Frequency-Averaged Mel. Neither residual is fed back into the autoregressive history. Trained on 100K hours of Emilia, the supervised 0.6B model obtains 1.51\% WER and 0.738 speaker similarity (SIM) on test-en, and 1.29\% CER and 0.755 SIM on test-zh. GRPO improves these results to 1.15\% WER / 0.753 SIM and 1.17\% CER / 0.776 SIM, respectively. We also distill the guided flow head into two- and four-step students, requiring 2 or 4 head evaluations per coarse frame. The four-step student retains competitive SIM and nearly matches the supervised model in WER/CER.

papers.title: Integrating Latent Block Models into Variational Autoencoders for Disentangled Representation Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce LBM-VAE, a novel framework that integrates Latent Block Models (LBMs) into Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to jointly cluster observations and latent dimensions. Beyond its clustering capabilities, LBM-VAE provides a block-structured latent representation that naturally supports disentangled representation learning. In contrast to conventional approaches that associate each factor of variation with an individual latent dimension, our framework allows factors of variation to be encoded across groups of latent dimensions. Experimental results demonstrate the promising clustering performance of LBM-VAE, while achieving competitive results in disentangled representation learning. LBM-VAE highlights the potential of combining co-clustering and variational inference to learn structured and interpretable latent representations.

papers.title: Contraction Analysis and Control of Polynomial Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Contraction analysis has found broad applications in synchronization, tracking, observer design, and nonlinear feedback control. However, establishing contraction conditions for polynomial dynamical systems remains challenging due to their state-dependent Jacobians. In this article, we develop a tensor-based framework for contraction analysis of polynomial dynamical systems by exploiting the structure of orthogonally decomposable (odeco) coefficient tensors. By transforming the dynamics into modal coordinates, we derive necessary and sufficient semicontraction conditions and characterize state-dependent semimetrics. We establish fundamental limitations on exponential contraction and prove polynomial decay of differential displacements on forward-invariant regions. To accommodate more general polynomial dynamical systems, we extend the framework to include linear dynamics and non-odeco tensor perturbations, deriving computationally tractable contraction certificates with explicit robustness guarantees. We further develop convex feedback synthesis conditions based on linear matrix inequalities for general input matrices. We demonstrate the effectiveness and computational scalability of the proposed framework through numerical experiments on both synthetic systems and nonlinear elastic relaxation models.

papers.title: Improving Tropical Cyclone Forecasts through Objective Ensemble Track-Error Reduction
papers.abstract: Accurate tropical cyclone (TC) track guidance is essential for warnings, evacuation planning, and risk communication, but outlying members and distinct track scenarios can degrade raw ensemble forecasts. Statistical and machine-learning (ML) methods proposed to improve ensemble guidance are difficult to compare because previous studies often use different forecast systems, basins, periods, and verification methods. Using a common verification framework, this study compares six objective methods (four statistical trimming and two ML methods) with the full ensemble mean for 138 TCs forecast by GEFS, MOGREPS-G, and IFS during 2016-2024. Dynamic trimming (DT) is the most consistent statistical method, reducing mean total track error by 8.0%, 13.4%, and 16.1% at short, medium, and long ranges. Its largest benefits occur in high-spread cases, where it can reach 70% of the low-error bound. Short-lead-error trimming (SLET) provides useful delayed guidance after early observations become available, but its improvement decreases with lead time. Regression-mixture clustering (RC) shows potential in low-spread cases and provides the largest improvement over the control run. The gradient boosted tree (GBT) produces the largest medium-range improvement and exceeds the theoretical trimming bound, suggesting strong potential, particularly when the observed track is poorly represented by the ensemble family. However, its 12.8% short-range degradation and gains concentrated in a small subset of cases indicate overcorrection when the ensemble mean is already accurate, highlighting the need for additional constraints. These results provide a consistent basis for using objective error-reduction methods to strengthen TC track guidance for operational decision-making.

papers.title: Asymptotic radial symmetry of $p$-Ginzburg-Landau minimizers on the disk
Uniform compactness in a family of $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problems
Logarithmic thermodynamic cost of prediction from rare observations
papers.abstract: A memory predicting changes in its environment from rare observations must spend energy on sampling and recording. We consider autonomous chemical memories driven by a sample-and-hold sensor observing an environment that switches at rate gamma, with sampling frequency f<<gamma. An ideal observer with access to the full observation history can retain predictive information proportional to f. However, retaining a finite fraction of this information in an autonomous physical memory requires work of order kBT ln(gamma/f) per sensor change. This additional thermodynamic cost arises from the competing requirements of suppressing false records during long intervals between observations and responding rapidly to new observations. We establish a universal low-power bound on predictive information, which grows at most as P/ln(P_ref/P) with power budget P, uniformly over any finite number of memory states and independently of network topology and memory relaxation times. We further demonstrate that memory architecture determines the attainable scaling. With bounded transition rates and readout from the memory alone, two-state memories are limited to P^2 scaling, whereas a three-state memory is sufficient to attain the optimal logarithmic scaling. Our results establish a fundamental thermodynamic distinction between acquiring information and maintaining a useful record of a changing environment.

papers.title: Machine Learning the $GW$ Self-Energy Operator for Real Materials
papers.abstract: Machine learning of $GW$ in solids has largely focused on prediction of scalar quasiparticle energy corrections. Here, we introduce a phase-aware many-body transformer that predicts the full $\mathbf{k}$-resolved complex self-energy matrix. As a proof of principle, we apply the model to predict quasiparticle energies before and after diagonalization of the quasiparticle Hamiltonian, obtaining a test set mean absolute error (MAE) of 29 meV for a dataset of 1745 2D materials in the static COHSEX approximation and 60 meV for a more limited dataset of 433 materials calculated within a plasmon-pole model. COHSEX pretraining followed by finetuning reduces this MAE to 42 meV. The predicted matrices also accurately reproduce QP wavefunctions.

papers.title: TileCache: Serving Multi-Round Diffusion Image Editing with Compressed Activation Caches
papers.abstract: Multi-round diffusion image editing can reduce computation by reusing intermediate activations, but retaining these activations across editing rounds introduces substantial memory and bandwidth overheads. Compression can reduce these overheads, but efficient cache construction is challenging: compressing only after editing requires buffering over 100 GB of activations per request. Moreover, the compressed cache must support selective reuse, as future masked edits require only a subset of the cached activations. It also exposes a scheduling challenge, as cached edits are faster than initial generations, causing naive policies to severely delay either initial generations or editing requests. In this paper, we aim to address both challenges through compression-informed serving. We develop TileCache, a serving system for multi-round diffusion editing. It compresses reusable activations and incorporates a scheduler that balances both edits and initial generation requests. Compared with the state-of-the-art image editing baseline, TileCache sustains over 2x the request arrival rate at 90% SLO attainment. It completes edits 2.4-4.5x and initial generations 1.3-2.2x faster than the baseline, while preserving image quality.

papers.title: From XR Sketches to CAD: Preserving Design Intent with AI
papers.abstract: Extended reality (XR) allows designers to sketch shapes directly in 3D, but converting these sketches into editable, feature-based CAD requires interpreting their intent. A sketch may contain drawing errors, intended features, and design choices that remain open. Correcting every irregularity risks erasing intended features, while automatic completion may impose choices the designer has not made. We argue that AI should add precision without overriding design intent, considering both the resulting shape and how the CAD model behaves during later edits. To guide this process, we propose a conceptual framework that distinguishes errors from intentions in individual sketch properties and relates them to correction, preservation, and exploration in editable CAD. We also outline five research directions for sketch interpretation, CAD construction, and evaluation, with testable hypotheses for selected questions.

papers.title: Right Goal, Wrong Body: Re-grounding Frozen VLAs under Actuation Shift
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are capable of producing desired robotic behaviors in ideal settings. However, they often fail when the robot's actuation changes at deployment. For example, remounting, mechanical wear, or command latency changes can lead to failed tasks and unsafe behaviors. To address the inevitable actuation shift, we propose ReGround, an inference-time method that keeps the VLA frozen and re-grounds its intended motion. ReGround learns the deployed robot's dynamics from task-agnostic motor babbling, and then tracks the policy's intended motion while staying close to the policy's own plan. ReGround activates only upon detecting a shift, and needs no rewards, demonstrations, or retraining. We show via two VLAs, eight LIBERO tasks, and five shift settings that ReGround can restore near-oracle success, such as raising $\pi_{0.5}$'s success from 0.16 to 0.90 under 400 ms latency, while remaining safer than a linear-calibration baseline. Project website and open-source code: this https URL .

papers.title: Achievable Information Rate for FTN under a Reduced Complexity BCJR Receiver
papers.abstract: The capacity of faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling in additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels has been established and is achieved by Gaussian inputs. However, the capacity of FTN signaling with finite-constellations is not yet fully characterized. The achievable information rate (AIR) provides a lower bound on this constrained capacity by quantifying the rate supported by a specified input distribution and receiver. This paper investigates the AIR of FTN signaling with finite constellations using full-state and reduced-state Bahl-Cocke-Jelinek-Raviv (BCJR) receivers, with bidirectional decision feedback incorporated into the reduced-state receiver. Especially, the detection problem is formulated in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), where a geometric foundation is established to understand FTN under severe time packing. The formulation establishes that the Ungerboeck metric remains valid even when the noise covariance is singular. We further characterize detection errors geometrically using RKHS distances between competing sequences. We also study outage probability for reduced-state detection, which occurs when AIR is zero, in addition to deriving the zero-AIR outage criterion for reduced-state detection. Unlike ISI-free Nyquist signaling, reduced-state FTN detection can retain residual ISI that causes the receiver to assign excessive confidence to incorrect symbols, leading to outage even at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Our results confirm both the spectral efficiency gains and the feasibility of FTN systems employing finite constellations and realistic receiver architectures.

papers.title: Markets for Compute and Inference: Structure, Financing, and Risk Transfer
papers.abstract: Capacity to run large language models is rented by the accelerator-hour, and their output is sold by the million tokens. Both goods now have published price indices, an over-the-counter forward has traded on one, a perpetual future on one is listed offshore, and CME and ICE have specified futures on rental indices that await the United States regulator. We ask what in these two markets can be hedged, by whom, and at what price. Three findings stand out. First, the price that exchange contracts settle on is not the price that drives operators' revenue. Every contract references the published short-dated rental rate, while most revenue, and with it credit quality, comes from private multi-year contracts whose prices are largely undisclosed. Second, the token price and the rental rate are linked by an identity through throughput and margin, but they are different exposures, so a hedge on the rental rate does not hedge the cost of inference; at the measured capability of GPT-5 the cheapest list price fell by a factor of 17 in twelve months, and by far less at lower capability. Third, the demand for hedging already sits in credit agreements, as the years by which operators' debt outlives their contracted revenue. Filings cannot measure that gap, because debt is scheduled year by year while contracted revenue rarely is, and the one loan that prices it settles the risk by cash prepayment against a model only the parties see. We design a reverse convertible note through which leveraged operators could buy protection against falling rental rates. Its coupon depends steeply on the annualised volatility of the rental rate, which the two public indices put between about 5% and 89% according to how each is built and the horizon measured; across that range the fair one-year coupon runs from 4.1% to 31.5%.

papers.title: EvoMem3D: Adaptive-Depth Temporal Representation Memory for Multi-Camera 3D Detection
papers.abstract: Modern multi-camera 3D detectors increasingly rely on large Vision Transformer (ViT) image encoders, making repeated full-depth encoding a dominant inference cost even though adjacent driving frames are highly redundant. We present EvoMem3D, an adaptive-depth temporal framework that caches the most recent full-depth detector-interface appearance representation as a read-only anchor and combines it with policy-selected partial features from the current frame. A lightweight pre-encoding controller chooses among semantic encoder exits before image processing, allocating shallow computation to stable frames and deeper computation when the visual state changes. To reuse appearance without carrying stale geometry, we decouple temporal appearance from geometric alignment: current-frame calibration defines the decoder geometry at every timestamp, while a motion-conditioned positional adapter accounts for anchor-to-current ego motion. On nuScenes, EvoMem3D achieves 61.50 NDS and 52.76 mAP while reducing end-to-end latency from 364.4 to 168.7 ms (x2.16) relative to standard dense DETR3D. With StreamPETR, it reaches 61.36 NDS and 52.55 mAP at a x1.92 speedup. Controlled studies isolate the effects of current evidence, temporal reuse, memory correction, and adaptive routing, while our audit confirms that the policy learns to distinguish semantic driving regimes.

papers.title: A Proof of Stein's Equidissection Conjecture
A Polynomial Time Approximation for the Minimization of Implication Systems and Horn CNFs
papers.abstract: An implication system is a collection of rules of the form $B \imp H$, where the set $B$ of Boolean variables is the {\em body} of the rule, while $H$ is the set of its {\em heads}. Such a rule is an aggregate representation of individual implications $B\imp h$, for $h\in H$ which correspond to the clauses of an equivalent CNF representation of a Horn Boolean function. An implication system is {\em body-minimum}/{\em clause-minimum} if it has the minimum number of bodies/clauses among all logically equivalent implication systems. The corresponding minimization problems appear not only in the context of implication systems, but also as problems for closure systems, directed hypergraphs, representation of dependencies in relational databases, or in Horn CNF minimization. While body-minimization is known to be solvable in polynomial time (and there are several algorithms in the literature that solve this task), clause-minimization is known to be NP-hard. In fact, body-minimization has a particular canonical solution, called the GD-basis of the underlying Horn function that also can be computed efficiently. In this paper, we utilize a known connection between the two minimization problems stating that for every implication system there always exists a logically equivalent clause-minimum implication system which has the same bodies as its canonical GD-basis, see (B{é}rczi and B{é}rczi-Kov{á}cs, 2017), and (Adaricheva and Nation, 2014). We use this fact to design a polynomial time approximation algorithm which for any $\delta>0$ outputs a $(\frac{1}{4} + \delta)n$-factor approximation of the logically equivalent clause-minimum implication system on $n$ variables. This is an improvement from the best known algorithm so far that provides only an $(n-1)$-factor approximation, see (Hammer and Kogan, 1993).

papers.title: Torsion phenomena in symplectic capacities via Clarke duality
Positivity of simplicial volume of convex projective manifolds
Unveiling the Multi-Phase Outflow in NGC 4151 with JWST Observations - I. Integrated Properties of the Outflow
papers.abstract: The biconical outflow of the nearby Seyfert 1.5 AGN NGC 4151 has been studied across the electromagnetic spectrum, yet mapping its multiphase structure with a single facility has remained challenging. Leveraging the broad wavelength coverage of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), we present new near- and mid-infrared observations tracing the ionization stratification of these outflows with a unified dataset. We analyze emission lines originating from molecular gas to highly ionized plasma and analyze the ionized gas using a 5-component Cloudy photoionization model covering three primary phases. Applying the footprint line method to characterize the X-ray emitting gas, we find that it holds the largest share of the total mass, suggesting that it is a primary candidate for driving AGN feedback in this system.

papers.title: Optical spin Edelstein response of d-wave altermagnets
papers.abstract: The momentum-dependent spin splitting and compensated magnetic order in altermagnets offer opportunities for electrical control of spin polarization. We explore the spin Edelstein effect in the frequency domain of a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We calculate the spin-velocity susceptibility response function beyond the intraband response regime and find that the interband longitudinal and transverse Edelstein responses are governed by the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature, respectively. The density of states presents a logarithmic van Hove singularity at exactly the negative value of the energy below which four disconnected Fermi contours emerge. This defines three distinctive regions for the position of the Fermi level, through which the Edelstein susceptibility tensor displays characteristic spectral features, reflecting the topological change of the Fermi surface. The resulting spin magnetization shows a strong dependence on the driving frequency and on the orientation of the in-plane external electric field. Our results highlight new possibilities for electrical and optical control of the spin Edelstein effect in altermagnets that could find spintronic applications.

papers.title: Impatience Makes Matching NP-Hard
papers.abstract: Motivated by emerging applications such as online marketplaces and quantum switches, we study a dynamic bipartite matching model with impatient agents, where the two sides represent customers and suppliers. Agents of each type arrive according to an independent Poisson process, and the platform decides which pairs of agents to match. The agents are possibly impatient and may leave the system if not matched before their patience expires. The platform aims to maximize throughput, i.e., the number of matches per unit time. In this paper, we reveal an interesting phase transition in the computational hardness of throughput maximization. In particular, we show that approximating the optimal long-run throughput within a sufficiently small fixed relative error is NP-hard, even when all agents have rate-one exponential patience. This result implies a computational barrier to constructing near-optimal, efficiently executable matching policies that induce a matching process with fast mixing. On the other hand, when all agents on at least one side have infinite patience, we provide a simple polynomial-time algorithm that maximizes the throughput.

papers.title: Local Limit Theorems and Edgeworth Expansions for some classes of inhomogeneous Markov chains
Approximate $K$-Conjugacy of Minimal Cantor--Circle Extensions I: The Rigid Case
$p$-ellipticity for systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients
A Matrix with Steps: An Episodic and Procedural Memory Method for Tool-Using Agents and Robots
authors: Peter Schüller (NeuraMix AI GmbH and Technische Universität Wien)
papers.abstract: Agents that call tools and robots that execute tasks are challenged by two shortcomings: they repeat what failed before, and they learn from runs that they only believe succeeded. We describe the construction of a memory that addresses both, built for a production agent platform. Every run is recorded as an episode, and only an outcome confirmed by an external check, a test, a tool result or a person counts; the agent's own claim never does. What is learned from episodes is kept in a memory with two parts: an associative matrix, written with the delta rule, which finds the procedure that applies to a situation; and a section of ordered, addressable step records that answers what comes after a given step, where a step is a goal of the agent, not a motion. Because the matrix sums its associations, it keeps no order and cannot return or delete a single one; it serves as the finder, and order, outcome counts and deletion live in the records. We describe how execution outcomes are stored, how episodes are recalled and used for solving tasks, and the file format that stores the memory. In simulation, a robot that judged its own success and stopped when it believed it was done reported $96\%$ of its tasks as done and solved $35\%$; with external verification it solved $79%$. In a store of $100000$ synthetic episodes ($457$MB on disk), the oldest episode was still found first, no episode from another person's memory was returned, and a success vouched for only by the model was never recalled; a lookup took $16$ms on a laptop and $40$ms on a server node (median). Task outcomes were measured up to about $10000$ confirmed records, where the exact records solved every revisit at the first attempt.

papers.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of active young Suns. New surface magnetic field maps for BE Cet, HN Peg, and kappa1 Cet
papers.abstract: Studying the magnetic activity of young solar analogues is important for understanding the dynamo mechanisms of the Sun and other late-type stars. We aimed to determine the surface magnetic field topology of four stars, analogues to the young Sun. This will contribute to long-term studies of the evolution of magnetic activity on different timescales of these targets. We obtained high resolution spectropolarimetric measurements with the HARPSpol instrument mounted at the ESO 3.6m telescope in the epoch 2021.6, and the SOFIN instrument, mounted on the 2.56m NOT telescope in epochs 2017.4 and 2021.5. The signal-to-noise ratio of the observations was boosted with least squares deconvolution. The surface magnetic field maps were calculated with the Zeeman-Doppler imaging technique. The magnetic field is decomposed into spherical harmonic expansions, allowing us to quantify the contributions from the axisymmetric and non-axisymmetric components, as well as the poloidal and toroidal fields. Out of the four stars observed (BE Cet, HN Peg, kappa1 Cet, V1358 Ori), three (BE Cet, HN Peg, kappa1 Cet) show clear signs of magnetic fields. Only one star, BE Cet shows clear evidence for the dominance of non-axisymmetric modes and the poloidal field being more dominant than the toroidal. HN Peg also shows signs of a stronger poloidal than a toroidal field, indicating an {\alpha}^2 dynamo, where the convective turbulence effects dominate over the differential rotation. The magnetic field of V1358 Ori could not be reliably reconstructed.

papers.title: On the relation of secondary motions to large- and very-large-scale motions
papers.abstract: The coexistence of secondary motions with large-scale and very-large-scale motions (LSMs/VLSMs) is investigated by direct numerical simulations of turbulent open-channel flow over streamwise-aligned Gaussian ridges, varying the ridge spacing $S$ and height $h$. First, the ridge height controls the secondary-motion strength and thereby the coexistence with VLSMs. VLSMs are suppressed for $h \geqslant 0.05\delta$, with $\delta$ the open-channel height, and re-emerge at $h = 0.025\delta$, where the mean secondary motions are comparable in strength to those over strip-type surfaces. Previously reported differences between strip- and ridge-type surfaces thus reflect secondary-motion strength rather than surface type. Second, proper orthogonal decomposition and conditional averaging reveal instantaneous secondary motions that span approximately $2\delta$, fill the channel height irrespective of $S$ and $h$, and are stronger than their mean. These are identified as LSMs spatially locked and amplified by the ridges. Over dense ridges, their alternation between neighbouring ridges yields weak, near-wall confined mean secondary motions, although VLSMs are suppressed over the full channel height. The ridge height thus sets the strength of the locked LSMs, whereas the ridge spacing sets where and for how long they persist. For weak locked LSMs, ridges spaced at their natural spanwise extent increase the VLSM energy, indicating that persistent locked LSMs concatenate into VLSMs. Third, large-scale instantaneous secondary motions persist over dense ridges in the absence of long streaks. This suggests that secondary motions are driven by intermittent cross-sectional motions rather than by long streaks, similar to the streak-less bursts in near-wall turbulence.

papers.title: Learning From the Best: What Makes Popular Hugging Face Models?
papers.abstract: Hugging Face has become a central platform for sharing and reusing pre-trained models, yet it remains unclear which practices are associated with higher visibility and adoption. Prior studies describe model reuse and model-card quality but do not systematically compare popular and unpopular models across documentation, repository structure, platform metadata, and technical metadata. We studied 66,909 Hugging Face models collected on 2026-02-28 and extracted 31 features across four dimensions: Documentation, Models, Platforms, and Techniques. For downloads and likes, we compared the top 10% popular models with the bottom 80% using statistical tests and effect sizes, trained five classifiers to predict popularity, ranked feature importance with the best-performing model, and tested whether predictions held across model domains and contributor affiliations. Popular models consistently had longer model cards, more code examples, and more GitHub and arXiv links, while quantized models showed contrasting patterns under downloads and likes. A Random Forest reached AUC 0.861 for downloads and 0.848 for likes, with root-level file counts and model size also among the most important features. Cross-group transfer stayed mostly above random but dropped by 0.12-0.17 AUC on average, showing that prediction performance was partly group-specific. The findings remained stable after removing download outliers and under alternative popularity thresholds, and a manual review of popular model cards linked the key documentation features to concrete content. We derive recommendations for model practitioners and directions for future research on model-sharing platforms.

papers.title: Streaming across viewing conditions - The effect of viewing distance and display luminance on video quality
papers.abstract: The visibility of streamed video distortions is affected by the user's display and viewing conditions, such as their display's luminance or the viewing distance. Distortions become less visible at lower luminance levels or farther viewing distances. However, most image and video quality metrics assume fixed optimal display and viewing conditions, making them insensitive to the viewing conditions. In this work, we demonstrate how existing metrics can be adapted to account for both factors and compare such an adaptation with the metrics that natively model viewing conditions. First, we collected a new video quality dataset, HDR-VDC, which contains streaming distortions in 4K HDR videos. The dataset consists of 12 4K and 4 FHD HDR source video content, each distorted with AV1 encoding and Lanczos upscaling from a lower resolution. The quality loss due to the distortions was measured at two viewing distances, corresponding to 60 and 120 pixels per visual degree, and two display mean luminance levels, varying by a factor of 8 in terms of luminance. Next, we developed a pre-processing framework that lets us adapt many quality metrics so that they can evaluate content across the viewing distances and luminance levels. The framework employs a display model and perceptually uniform encoding, PU21, to account for the effect of display luminance, and perspective projection scaling (PPS) to account for the effect of viewing distance. We used the framework to compare the performance of 35 state-of-the-art metrics. This allowed us to identify a selection of existing quality metrics that can be effectively adapted to account for the viewing conditions.

papers.title: Disparity in Influence: A Fairness Evaluation of Centrality Measures in Complex Networks
papers.abstract: Social networks are shaped by homophily-driven connections, which naturally lead to the emergence of communities with uneven sizes and influence. Such structural imbalances impact the fairness of network analysis tools, particularly centrality measures that are widely used to identify influential nodes for tasks like information diffusion and network robustness. In this work, we conduct a comprehensive assessment of fairness in centrality measures, using influence spreading across networks with heterogeneous community structures. We first analytically show that disparity is bounded by outreach; cross-community outreach is bounded by the inter-community cut; and when all seeds lie in one community, disparity approaches the normalized outreach within that community as cross-community transmission vanishes. This explains why attenuation concentrates influence in the community where diffusion starts. We further evaluate a broad spectrum of centrality measures, including local, semi-local, global, and community-aware measures, on both synthetic network generative models and real-world datasets, using the Independent Cascade and Linear Threshold Models. The results consistently show that influence tends to concentrate within larger communities, with disparities becoming more pronounced under constrained or deterministic diffusion settings. We further observe that fairness is highly sensitive to the choice of centrality measure rather than its general category. In particular, fairness-aware adaptations of PageRank demonstrate a strong balance between maximizing influence reach and maintaining equitable distribution across communities. On real networks, these conclusions are largely stable under random removal or addition of up to 3% of the edges. Our findings highlight the need to explicitly account for fairness when designing and selecting centrality-based strategies in networked systems.

papers.title: Averaging for multi-scale McKean-Vlasov equation
Understanding Users' Security, Privacy, and Trust Concerns in Healthcare AI Systems
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into healthcare systems, from clinical information retrieval to workflow automation and decision support, which introduces new security, privacy, and trust risks with direct implications for patient care. While prior work has examined these risks from technical and regulatory perspectives, less is known about how these risks are naturally discussed in online communities. To address this gap, we conduct a large-scale analysis of 14 medical communities on Reddit and extract 6,514 relevant posts. Through systematic qualitative coding and LLM-assisted classification, we investigate concerns expressed in healthcare AI discussions, their prevalence, and how they evolve over time. Our analysis reveals that users perceive healthcare AI as expanding traditional healthcare trust boundaries and attack surfaces through integrations with electronic health records, third-party services, cloud platforms, and automated clinical workflows. Posts express concerns about over-privileged access to sensitive records, opaque data flows, unauthorized secondary use, and unsafe automation can amplify the consequences of errors and misuse. We identify four attitudes toward these risks: exploring questions of accountability and harm, cautiously accepting AI with stronger safeguards, skepticism about system trustworthiness, and resignation to growing data exposure and automation. Longitudinal analysis shows that SP&T discussions have increased significantly, with shifts coinciding with major healthcare AI deployments, privacy incidents, and regulatory developments. These findings illuminate changing trust relationships and data-governance challenges, informing the design and governance of safer, more transparent, and accountable healthcare AI systems.

papers.title: feedback-grape: A JAX-based Python Package for GPU-Accelerated GRAPE with Feedback
Lengths and Counting of Palindromic Prefixes of Standard Sturmian Words
papers.abstract: Every standard Sturmian word $c_\mathbf{d}$ is determined by a directive sequence $\mathbf{d}=(d_i)_{i\ge 1}$ of positive integers, and its palindromic prefixes are obtained by iterated palindromic closure. We describe the lengths of these prefixes by the numbers $j\,\ell_{i-1}+\ell_{i-2}-2$, where $\ell_n$ is the length of the $n$-th standard word and $1\le j\le d_i$, and we show that each nonzero length is attained by exactly one pair $(i,j)\neq(1,1)$. For a purely periodic directive sequence of period $k$ we then prove that the number $\pi_\mathbf{d}(N)$ of nonempty palindromic prefixes of length at most $N$ satisfies \[ \pi_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\frac{d_1+\cdots+d_k}{\log\lambda_\mathbf{d}}\,\log N, \] where $\lambda_\mathbf{d}$ is the largest eigenvalue of the matrix $M(d_1)\cdots M(d_k)$. For the Fibonacci word this gives $\pi_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\log N/\log\varphi$, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$.

papers.title: Feasibility certificates for DeePC: A set invariance approach
papers.abstract: DeePC is posed on a window of past inputs and outputs, so its feasible set is a set of histories and is not available in closed form. We write the DeePC solution as an implicit ReLU network whose weights are built from Hankel matrices and whose activation patterns are the critical regions of the underlying quadratic program. This gives, directly from the Hankel matrices, the feasible set of DeePC as a polyhedral projection, its explicit piecewise-affine control law, and an exact linear model of the history window. We compute three invariant sets of histories: the maximal positively invariant set of the unsaturated linear branch, the region of recursive feasibility of DeePC without terminal ingredients, and the maximal control invariant set of admissible histories. We show these sets are nested and provide numerical examples.

papers.title: Ocular Recognition: Interoperability, Multi-Resolution, and Spectrum Challenges
papers.abstract: Ocular recognition is typically developed under controlled acquisition conditions, limiting its use in semi-controlled and on-the-move scenarios. A key obstacle is the lack of representative data spanning real-world capture conditions. At a border checkpoint, for example, images may range from low-resolution visible-light periocular crops (RGB) to high-resolution near-infrared iris images (NIR). Using this heterogeneous evidence raises three questions: whether resolution-specific processing improves recognition, how to compare templates from different processing routes, and how to allocate training data across resolution specialists. We investigate resolution-specific processing and parameter sharing using three AdaFace-based architecture families: fixed-resolution specialists; Independent Backbones with Shared Heads (IBSH); and models with resolution-specific front-ends for 40x40, 80x80, and 160x160 inputs, followed by a shared identity trunk and embedding projection. We evaluate each architecture with route-specific training subsets and with a full-pool strategy, in which every specialist uses the complete selected training set. Results reveal a trade-off among same-resolution specialization, cross-resolution interoperability, and common-route re-extraction. Route-specific training produces distinct performance profiles across routes, whereas full-pool training makes route performance more uniform and primarily benefits the 160x160 route. Thus, adding training data does not improve all resolution routes equally.

papers.title: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
papers.abstract: A coding agent working within a software organization must establish what to build, collaborate with colleagues, and verify what it delivers. We introduce SWE-CoWork, a benchmark comprising 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains. Each assignment places an agent in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues who have distinct responsibilities, bounded knowledge, and controlled collaboration behavior. Starting from a brief handoff, agents must recover requirements distributed across colleagues and workplace records, reconcile conflicting evidence, and implement changes evaluated by private executable tests. We evaluate eleven models and find a substantial gap between partial implementation and complete task delivery. The two leading models satisfy approximately 63% of fail-to-pass (F2P) tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments. Providing complete requirements upfront improves F2P by approximately 16 percentage points for Seed Evolving and GPT-6 Astra, yet leaves complete task success unchanged. Requirement-level trajectory analysis reveals failures throughout the delivery process: Claude-Opus-5.5 directs a mean of 93% of first questions about queried cards to their accountable owners across runs but obtains only 64% of colleague-held requirements. Deferred questions go unfollowed, implementations remain incomplete even after requirements are acquired, and 31% of requirements reported as completed fail their tests. These findings highlight sustained requirement tracking, from clarification through implementation, verification, and handoff, as a key challenge for reliable autonomous software engineering.

papers.title: Functional Principal Component Analysis for Ordinal Functional Data with Application in Diabetes Intervention
papers.abstract: Traditional functional principal component analysis (FPCA) is typically designed for continuous functional observations. In this paper, we address the scenario where the outcome consists of repeated categorical data defined over a bounded interval. Our objective is to develop an FPCA methodology tailored specifically for ordinal functional data. Our approach leverages recent advancements in ordinal data modeling to estimate both the mean function and the eigenfunctions, while employing a computationally efficient method for predicting the scores. The performance of the proposed methodology is evaluated numerically in simulation and data application on diabetes intervention.

papers.title: FIDEL: Abugida-Aware Pre-tokenization for Ethiopic Languages
papers.abstract: Subword tokenizers assume that meaningful linguistic units can be recovered by splitting text at learned boundaries, an assumption better suited to concatenative morphology than to Semitic root-and-pattern systems. The challenge is acute for the Ethiopic languages, whose abugida script encodes consonant-vowel units as single characters and hides consonantal structure. We introduce FIDEL (FIdäl DEcomposition and Linearization), a family of reversible abugida-aware pre-tokenization schemes that expose consonant and vowel-order structure, extend SPLINTER reductions from abjad scripts to the Ethiopic abugida, and evaluate them on three Ethiopic languages under controlled conditions, holding corpus, architecture, budget and protocol fixed so that tokenization is the only variable. We report intrinsic tokenizer statistics for BPE and UnigramLM across vocabulary sizes alongside downstream NLP tasks, including transfer scenarios. We find that FIDEL reduction improves news classification consistently and named-entity recognition at larger capacity, while sentiment analysis performance declines under the more aggressive schemes, and extractive question answering performance is preserved.

papers.title: Hausdorff continuity of logarithmic and Riesz capacities
Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute $SO(5)$ CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector $\phi$, singlet $s$, and traceless symmetric scalar $t$, we characterize the bootstrap cone whose tip lies remarkably close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC. We extract an extensive spectrum across $SO(5)$ irreducible representations, together with operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients. We study a fuzzy-sphere realization of the $SO(5)$ nonlinear sigma model with a level-1 Wess--Zumino--Witten term. Using the special conformal generators, we identify 52 conformal primaries in a system with \(N=10\) Landau orbitals, including 31 not previously classified as primaries in the earlier fuzzy-sphere study. Symmetry projection extends fuzzy-sphere exact diagonalization to $N=12$. The bootstrap spectrum and OPE coefficients show close agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, including 16 of the newly identified primaries in channels accessible to the mixed-correlator bootstrap. The lowest $SO(5)$ singlet scalar is relevant in the bootstrap and QMC results; its fuzzy-sphere data is $\Delta_s=2.816$ at $N=12$ and decreases with system size. Our results suggest that the mixed-correlator bootstrap solution represents a unitary CFT with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar and is closely connected to the QMC and fuzzy-sphere data for the DQCP. The conformal bootstrap, fuzzy-sphere, and QMC together provide comprehensive evidence for an $SO(5)$ multicritical CFT and critical data to decode the phases in two-dimensional quantum magnets.

papers.title: Decorated lattices: hyperuniformity and limit theorems
Counterfactual Screening of Rare Secondary Overloads in Power Grids with a Stochastic Surrogate for Electromagnetic Transient Simulations
Detection of minimum ionising particles with internal gain in the first Silicon Electron Multiplier demonstrators
papers.abstract: The Silicon Electron Multiplier (SiEM) is a novel sensor concept for minimum ionising particle (MIP) detection that uses internal gain achieved through a composite electrode structure embedded within the silicon bulk. Unlike conventional gain sensors (LGADs, APDs), the SiEM achieves amplification through applied electric potentials rather than doped gain layers, potentially offering superior radiation hardness above $10^{16}\,n_{\mathrm{eq}}/\mathrm{cm}^2$. Following initial conceptual studies and simulation work, several fabrication approaches were explored, including Deep Reactive Ion Etching (DRIE) at Centro Nacional de Microelectrónica (CNM) and Metal Assisted Chemical Etching (MACEtch) at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI). This paper reports the first experimental results from functional SiEM demonstrators produced by Hamamatsu Photonics K. K. (HPK) using a single-electrode configuration with modified geometry. Electrical characterisation through I-V measurements and test beam studies with minimum ionising particles demonstrate clear evidence of charge multiplication, with gains comparable to simulation predictions.

papers.title: A Gravitomagnetic Bootstrap: from Newtonian gravity to general relativity via localizing rotational and conformal symmetries
papers.abstract: Newtonian gravity, in the light of the Equivalence Principle, is best understood as a localization of Galilean inertial structure --- or at least, of the part of Galilean inertial structure that defines rectilinear acceleration. I consider what kind of theory can be constructed if we also localize rotational inertia and spatial and temporal scales. The resultant theory, given weak assumptions, is unique up to a constant with the dimensions of velocity and an overall sign. For an appropriate choice of these, it coincides with the first post-Newtonian approximation to general relativity, so that this construction gives a method to bootstrap from Newtonian gravity to general relativity without explicitly presupposing special relativity.

papers.title: Knowing Less After a Diagnostic Test: Dilation in Clinical Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Dilation (Seidenfeld and Wasserman 1993) occurs when conditioning on new information \textit{only} increases uncertainty regardless of what the information reveals. Often viewed as an undesirable feature of models of ambiguity, dilation has sparked sustained debate about belief updating. This paper shows that following established clinical guidance can induce dilation, even for diagnostic tests that meet conventional performance benchmarks. We characterize when a test is dilation-inducing and show that a ubiquitous feature of performance studies -- evaluating tests against an imperfect reference -- creates scope for dilation. To facilitate detection before clinical use and inform regulatory standards, we develop a finite-sample valid hypothesis test of the null that a diagnostic test is dilation-inducing in this context. Applying the method to an influential study that preceded and contributed to the clinical adoption of chest CT screening for COVID-19, we find that the data are consistent with dilation.

papers.title: Long time derivation of the Boltzmann equation from dynamics of short-range potentials
AstroPIE-53: Towards Understanding Failure Modes of Human Pose Estimation in Space
papers.abstract: Reliable monitoring of astronauts is essential for safety, situational awareness, and autonomous assistance in space missions. While modern computer vision enables accurate human detection and pose estimation on Earth, its robustness in space environments remains largely unquantified due to limited data availability. We present AstroPIE-53, a pilot dataset of 53 annotated astronaut videos collected from publicly available mission footage. To respect copyright restrictions, we release video identifiers, reconstruction scripts, and dense annotations rather than raw videos. The dataset includes bounding boxes, challenge classes, and human-annotated pose failure tags. We benchmark state-of-the-art person detection and pose estimation models under realistic zero-shot deployment conditions and perform the first systematic failure analysis for astronaut monitoring. Our results reveal substantial performance degradation caused by occlusions, unusual body orientations, low contrast, and microgravity motion patterns.

papers.title: Energy and Radius Estimates for Molecules
Independent set reconfiguration is hard at treewidth four
papers.abstract: Independent Set Reconfiguration asks whether one of two given independent sets of equal size can be transformed into the other by moving one token at a time while keeping the occupied vertices independent. In token sliding, a token moves along an edge. In token jumping, it may move to any unoccupied vertex. For both rules, the problem is solvable in polynomial time on trees and is PSPACE-complete on graphs of treewidth at most $c$ for some fixed constant $c$. For each rule, the smallest treewidth bound that suffices for hardness has long been open. We narrow this gap by proving that both versions are NP-hard on graphs of treewidth four.

papers.title: Paying Creators for Training Data Can Increase AI Displacement
papers.abstract: Generative AI increasingly competes with creators while using their content as training data. In response, policymakers have called for platforms to compensate creators for training data use and allow opting out. We study how such policies affect creator displacement in a model of a platform where creators choose whether to contribute training data and consumers choose between purchasing from creators and prompting generative AI trained on their content. When compensation is required, the low-quality creator chooses to remain solely as a training data supplier while AI fully displaces her demand, despite AI quality and the price the platform charges for AI-generated content being identical with and without compensation. Without compensation, the risk of losing creators and their training data constrains the platform to set the price of creators' content to preserve their demand. This constraint also prevents further AI displacement as AI improves, with the platform raising AI prices while keeping creators' prices and demand unchanged to prevent exit.
