To overcome these challenges, we propose MrLIE (MLLM-empowered reference Low-light Image Enhancement), a novel reference-based unsupervised LLIE framework that synergizes the generative and reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with conditional diffusion. MrLIE employs the MLLM as a high-fidelity reference synthesizer and diagnostic critic, iteratively generating, diagnosing, and correcting normal-light references directly from degraded nighttime observations. Based on this, our method governs the enhancement process through two complementary mechanisms, in which a confidence offset module rectifies spatial-geometric inconsistencies for reference reliability and a structure-anchored injection scheme harmonizes aligned reference cues, low-light structural constraints, and ControlNet additive anchoring during the denoising process. Extensive experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that MrLIE achieves superior perceptual quality, natural appearance, and robust generalization.

papers.title: LC-ISP Benchmark: Learning Advanced ISP with Live and Capture Streams
papers.abstract: High-quality paired RAW-to-sRGB datasets are essential for data-driven ISP, yet existing datasets often rely on cross-device collection, causing misalignment and failing to faithfully reflect real capture conditions. We therefore introduce LC-ISP, a large-scale benchmark built from the intrinsic gap between a camera's live preview and offline capture streams. LC-ISP contains 53.9k spatially aligned groups, each comprising live RAW/live sRGB and multi-frame fused RGB/capture sRGB, and covers day, night, indoor, outdoor, and HDR scenes. It also provides capture-stream intermediates for modular supervision. We further develop a compact two-stage baseline that uses these intermediates as auxiliary targets. Under a 2.5-GFLOP budget for 448$\times$448 RAW inputs, it outperforms the strongest single-frame baseline by over 2 dB PSNR while improving texture, denoising, and color reproduction. LC-ISP supports realistic benchmarking, the design of supervision strategies, and the development of lightweight ISP models.

papers.title: Fourier Crosstalk and Leakage Correction for Binary-Encoded Fourier Single-Pixel Imaging
papers.abstract: Digital micromirror devices enable high-speed Fourier single-pixel imaging (Fourier-SPI), but their binary modulation introduces quantization errors that degrade the reconstructed image quality. In particular, each binarized Fourier probe contains non-target Fourier components, thereby distorting the corresponding Fourier-domain measurement. This Letter presents a Fourier domain correction framework that characterizes these errors using the Fourier-domain response matrix of the decoded binary Fourier patterns. Accordingly, a response-matrix-based Fourier-SPI measurement model is established by partitioning the matrix into components associated with the sampled and unsampled frequencies, thereby decomposing the quantization error into sampled-frequency crosstalk and unsampled-frequency leakage. This model established a generalized correction framework, termed Fourier Crosstalk and Leakage Correction (FCLC), alongside two simplified methods: Fourier Sampled-Frequency Crosstalk Correction (FSCC) and Fourier DC Crosstalk Correction (FDCC). FSCC is implemented via an inversion-free Richardson-type iteration, whereas FDCC admits a closed-form solution. Numerical simulations and experiments across multiple binary encoding strategies reveal that the proposed framework improves reconstruction fidelity without modifying the binary patterns or acquisition process.

papers.title: Sensing with OFDM Signals: How Do the Constellations Affect the Sensing Accuracy?
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how communication constellations affect joint range-velocity estimation with data-bearing orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals. To this end, starting from the continuous-time sensing process, we derive a discrete observation model and specify its validity conditions. For multiple targets with unknown delays, Doppler shifts, and complex gains, the complete Fisher information matrix (FIM) admits a structural factorization separating deterministic channel derivatives from random symbol-energy weights. This structure yields a Jensen-type lower bound on the average conditional Cramer-Rao bound (CRB), which is attained exactly by constant-modulus constellations. Single-target closed-form expressions further reveal the dependence of the bounds on the transmitted energy distribution and physical OFDM parameters. We also formulate two-dimensional fast Fourier transform (FFT), concentrated maximum-likelihood (ML), and sliding-subarray multiple signal classification (MUSIC) processing under the derived observation model. Numerical results support the theoretical optimality of constant-modulus constellations but also show that the CRB gap between phase-shift keying (PSK) and quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) becomes negligible when the numbers of subcarriers and OFDM symbols are considerably large. The performance of ML estimation closely approaches the derived bounds, which confirms the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis. FFT processing exhibits grid-induced error floors. In the considered scenarios, MUSIC provides lower estimation errors than FFT and exhibits a more pronounced constellation dependence.

papers.title: Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers from rainbow Turán numbers and beyond
Hardware-Friendly Plug-and-Play MVDR Beamforming for Microphone Arrays: Algorithm, Prototype, and System-Level Feasibility
papers.abstract: Beamforming has been widely recognized for its spatial filtering capability in speech signal processing, enabling effective interference rejection and signal enhancement. The performance of adaptive beamforming methods, e.g., the conventional minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamforming, often deteriorate significantly in complex and dynamic acoustic environments. Part of the reason is that such conventional beamforming ignores the intrinsic characteristics of speech. To address this issue, this paper proposes Plug-and-Play Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (PnP-MVDR) algorithm, which integrates data-driven speech prior information into the MVDR framework to enhance robustness against non-stationary noise while maintaining its interpretability. The PnP-MVDR framework supports joint interaction of signal processing and deep learning methods and is designed to be compatible with modern DSP-NPU architectures, making it hardware-friendly for potential edge deployment. Beyond the algorithmic innovation, we have developed a complete microphone beamforming system to validate practical feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms traditional and deep learning-based baselines, establishing PnP-MVDR as an effective and deployable solution for edge audio scenarios.

papers.title: Rethinking KV Caching for LLM Decode: Free-Space Optical KV Regeneration for Reduction of Memory Traffic
papers.abstract: Long-context large language model (LLM) decoding repeatedly reads the historical key-value (KV) cache, making multi-head attention (MHA) memory-bandwidth-bound. Caching layer-input activations instead halves historical-cache storage and traffic, but requires regenerating KV from each cached activation. On digital accelerators such as GPUs, this regeneration takes far longer than fetching the activation from HBM. The KV regeneration overhead outweighs the savings from reduced memory traffic, shifting decode attention from a memory bottleneck to a compute bottleneck. We present OptiDecode, a hybrid optoelectronic decode-attention accelerator that regenerates historical KV using free-space optics and computes attention digitally. Projection weights remain resident on optical tiles, exploiting reuse across historical tokens for high-throughput optical regeneration. Scaling to large models introduces two challenges. First, distributing weights across tiles requires sending the same activations to every head group, while each readout die produces only partial KV. Activation replay shares one set of electrical-to-optical converters across head groups without costly broadcast. In-situ attention avoids transferring partial KV from readout dies to reducers by computing on them locally and exchanging only partial scores, probabilities, and partial outputs. Second, processing an activation chunk through all dependent stages takes longer than one activation-fetch interval. Chunk pipelining overlaps successive chunks so that OptiDecode sustains the HBM activation-fetch rate. OptiDecode demonstrates 1.92-1.99x decode-attention speedup over an ideal GPU KV-read baseline at equal peak HBM bandwidth (A100-B200), for 32K-token contexts across evaluated 30B-175B MHA models, approaching the 2x upper bound from halving historical memory traffic.

papers.title: Matroid Parity Meets Vertex Splitting
papers.abstract: A vertex split replaces a vertex by two non-adjacent descendants and partitions its incident edges between them. We study exclusive $\ell$-shallow splitting, where each original vertex has at most $\ell+1$ descendants, with the aim of obtaining a forest, a pseudoforest, or a cluster graph. We consider two natural objectives: minimizing the total number of split operations and minimizing the number of original vertices that are split. Our main conceptual contribution is a connection between vertex splitting and matroid parity. For both forests and pseudoforests, we give a characterization of feasible splitting sequences that leads, via weighted linear matroid parity, to polynomial-time algorithms for minimizing the number of split vertices when $\ell=2$. These algorithms are complemented by NP-hardness for every fixed $\ell\ge3$; for pseudoforests, hardness holds even on graphs of maximum degree four. The total number of split operations behaves differently: for both sparse target classes, this objective is polynomial-time solvable for every $\ell$, using matroid intersection. For cluster graphs, both objectives admit linear-time algorithms when $\ell=1$ and are NP-hard for every fixed $\ell\ge2$. Together, these results identify how the target class, the local splitting bound, and the choice of objective determine the complexity of vertex splitting.

papers.title: $α$--$α$ Correlations in Excited Clustering Nuclei Across the Solid-Liquid Transition
papers.abstract: We investigate the structural evolution of $\alpha$-cluster matter using a microscopic transport model for four $\alpha$-conjugate collision systems, including $^{12}\text{C}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{16}\text{O}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{28}\text{Si}+^{12}\text{C}$, and $^{40}\text{Ca}+^{12}\text{C}$ at incident energies ranging from 2.0 to 7.0~MeV/u. The $\alpha$-cluster structure of an excited nucleus undergoes a solid-liquid phase transition with increasing incident energy. Whether it proceeds by the dissociation of individual clusters or by the collapse of their spatial organization remains unexplored, as does the question of whether any characteristic $\alpha$--$\alpha$ correlation survives. The one-body density $\rho(\mathbf{r})$, the standard clustering diagnostic, cannot by itself settle this question, since it neither distinguishes a genuine cluster configuration from a density fluctuation nor reveals the sparse residual clusters masked by the surrounding nucleon medium. We therefore construct the exclusive $\alpha$--$\alpha$ two-body spatial correlation function from the $\alpha$-cluster centroids to isolate the $\alpha$ clusters. In all four systems the $\alpha$--$\alpha$ correlation exhibits two peaks, a nearest-neighbor one and a next-nearest-neighbor inter-cluster one. Both peak positions increase with system size. Over the energy range studied, which spans this transition, the mean number of $\alpha$ clusters per event falls steeply while the $\alpha$--$\alpha$ correlation persists and the inter-cluster distances change only slightly. The individual clusters therefore dissociate rather than lose their spatial organization.

papers.title: ReCALM: A Residual-enhanced Crowdsourced Analytic Learning Mechanism for Distributed Continual Service Construction
papers.abstract: Crowdsourcing has emerged as a promising paradigm for constructing AI services by harnessing the collective capabilities of distributed workers. As consumers' demands continually evolve, service models must acquire new knowledge while retaining previously learned information. However, due to the inherited reliance on gradients for backpropagation, existing approaches typically suffer from catastrophic forgetting during continual model updates on heterogeneous data. Recent studies have introduced analytic learning, a gradient-free paradigm that achieves invariance through recursive closed-form solutions. Nevertheless, existing analytic methods are typically constrained by single-layer linear networks, which tend to suffer from underfitting due to their inability to perform deep representation learning. To address this issue, we propose ReCALM, a Residual-enhanced Crowdsourced Analytic Learning Mechanism that achieves deep nonlinear invariance for distributed continual service construction. Inspired by the success of ResNet, we develop gradient-free residual blocks for ReCALM with closed-form solutions. To implement distributed continual training for ReCALM, we further devise a cross-recursive strategy via least squares. Both theoretical and experimental analyses verify ReCALM's dual superiority in heterogeneity invariance and deep representation. With 20 residual layers, ReCALM improves accuracy by 8.85%-9.83% over the single-layer analytic baseline, while reducing computational costs by over 94% compared with gradient-based baselines.

papers.title: Beyond Clumsy Agentic Tool Calling: How Cueing and Spotting Make the Difference
papers.abstract: LLM-based task-oriented agents depend on tools to interact with their environments, but may overlook execution feedback, repeat ineffective calls, or persist with unproductive strategies. These behaviors can hinder agents' ability to use tools autonomously and sustain task progress. We characterize tool-use symptoms at two temporal granularities: local clumsy tool-use behaviors and tool-use detours spanning multiple interactions. Towards greater autonomy in tool use, we present ToolPulse, an online middleware supporting autonomous tool use through cueing and spotting. ToolPulse tracks execution state and temporal interaction patterns, monitoring proposed calls before dispatch and inspecting execution feedback prior to the agent resumes reasoning. It combines state-based rules, semantic sequence analysis, and interaction-feature similarity to identify intervention opportunities and provide verbal reminders, structured feedback, or context-specific advice from auxiliary models. Our process-oriented evaluation distinguishes trigger validity, behavioral cessation, and substantive correction alongside task outcomes and resource costs. Using SWE-agent with three backbone models, we evaluate 1,350 trajectories on 90 Python, C++, and Java bug-fix tasks, comparing unassisted execution with four assistance strategies. Substantive responses follow 61.6-90.9% of valid triggers for tool-use detours. Concise reminders achieve the highest observed aggregate substantive-response rate; more elaborate assistance offers symptom-dependent benefits and can be less effective. Aggregate repair outcomes remain close to baseline, with token savings in selected settings. These findings support proactive runtime assistance for autonomous tool use. The gap between behavioral adjustment and aggregate repair gains calls for careful decisions on intervention timing and assistance strategy in autonomous agents.

papers.title: HospitalBench: Diagnosing Where and Why Embodied Agents Fail on Long Hospital Task Chains
papers.abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks fail in ways that end-task success cannot see. HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark of ten hospital chores in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, each two unscored warm-up steps followed by a causal chain of five scored sub-tasks in one continuous simulation: the state one step leaves (an object pose, a choice, a fact seen once) determines what the next step must do, unlike benchmarks that place sub-tasks side by side. Vision-language agents act through skill-level tools from camera images. A scripted robot that makes only the calls a model gets is the solvability check of a chore. From each trajectory the benchmark reads where a chain breaks, what the agent did after a failed call, and how far its own position estimate drifts from the true one. This version reports first results only: 15 of 60 planned runs (three models at high effort, one run each on chores T1 and T10 from both start states and T3 from one), with scripted-robot proofs on three of the ten chores. Of the 15 runs, 2 passed all five sub-tasks. Runs still going after sub-tasks 1 to 5 were 15, 8, 4, 2, 2. Of 189 failed calls, 168 were followed by a different call and 111 by a call that did not fail. These are first results and not a full benchmark. We will release the scenes, task chains, scripted robot, evaluation harness and trajectories.

papers.title: B-OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Self-Generated Problem Briefs
papers.abstract: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) has recently attracted interest because it provides dense teacher guidance without a separate, often larger teacher model. However, OPSD conditions its teacher on ground-truth solutions, which limits its use when such solutions are unavailable. We propose On-Policy Self-Distillation with Self-Generated Problem Briefs (B-OPSD). Using a prompt template, the initial model or a saved student checkpoint generates a problem brief from the question alone. The prompt asks for relevant principles, applicability conditions, and likely pitfalls, but not a final answer or a complete solution. A frozen teacher uses the brief as privileged context to guide the current student's on-policy rollouts through token-level distribution matching. B-OPSD uses no ground-truth solutions during training. Results on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and HMMT 2025 show that both B-OPSD variants achieve higher average accuracy than OPSD at each of three Qwen3 model sizes. Code is available at this https URL

papers.title: Distributed Shaping of Robot Swarms Through Spatial Moments of Arbitrary Order
papers.abstract: This paper shapes a swarm into a target pattern, such as a figure taken from an image, by controlling its spatial moments. The image is sampled into a reference configuration whose centroid and covariance set the position and principal spreads of the formation, while its higher-order moments, expressed in covariance-normalized (whitened) coordinates, encode the remaining shape. In contrast with geometric formation control, which prescribes distances, bearings, or relative positions between specific agents, this specification concerns the swarm as a whole and assigns no agent to a particular place. The key mechanism is orthogonalization in the swarm's own empirical inner product: projecting negative-gradient velocities onto the complement of low-degree polynomials sampled at the agents makes every higher-order correction preserve all lower-order moments exactly. The resulting hierarchical controller has lower triangular error dynamics and converges locally exponentially for any positive gains, so orders can be added without undoing those already achieved. A joint alternative regulates the higher moments together through a regularized Gauss--Newton step while preserving the centroid and covariance dynamics. We give bounds on the number of agents and sufficient conditions for regularity. Both controllers admit a distributed implementation that uses only relative positions and neighbor communication and retains local exponential convergence when estimation is sufficiently fast. In a distributed simulation on a sparse graph, 350 agents form an airplane from an unstructured swarm through moments up to order ten; the hierarchy reaches the full specification, while the joint law approaches it with smaller velocities.

papers.title: DLR variational principle for the one-dimensional log-gas and another proof of existence of Sine-beta
Arginine metabolism drives tumor immune escape by shaping an immunosuppressive microenvironment
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment evolves through the ``elimination-equilibrium-escape'' paradigm, yet the quantitative mechanisms by which metabolic reprogramming contributes to immune evasion remain unclear. We develop a mathematical model of tumor-immune interactions to investigate how arginine metabolism shapes an immunosuppressive microenvironment. We establish the positivity and boundedness of solutions and analyze the existence and stability of equilibrium states. The model is calibrated using tumor growth data from three mouse cohorts and reproduces tumor growth patterns under distinct immune conditions. The calibrated model predicts faster tumor growth in immunocompetent mice than in immunodeficient controls, with macrophage dynamics accounting for this difference. It further predicts that arginine administration promotes tumor progression by enhancing macrophage polarization and weakening T cell-mediated tumor control. To account for interindividual heterogeneity, we develop the TVInfABC algorithm to generate a virtual mouse cohort. Moreover, our analysis indicates that tumor-associated macrophages can promote transitions from immunologically ``hot'' to ``cold'' states. Systematic pharmacodynamic simulations further uncover a synergy between arginine depletion (anti-ARG1) and immune checkpoint blockade (anti-PD-1/PD-L1). These results provide a mathematical basis for studying metabolic-immune interactions and for evaluating mechanism-based combination therapies.

papers.title: Entropy-Based and Quadratic Conditional Innovation Metrics for Informed Dynamic Scheduling of Belief-Propagation Decoding for LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: We propose two enhanced conditional innovation (CI) metrics for informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) in belief-propagation (BP) decoding of LDPC codes. The CI-based residual BP (CIRBP) algorithm uses the CI metric to guide the selection of the variable node (VN) to be updated and has been shown to outperform several existing IDS-based BP decoders, especially at the early decoding stage. However, the original CI metric uses only the absolute difference between the current and precomputed posterior probabilities and does not separately account for the reliability associated with each probability. By reformulating the CI metric relative to the decision boundary, we separate each posterior probability into its decision side and a linear-distance term reflecting reliability. Replacing the latter with the binary entropy complement yields the proposed entropy-based CI (E-CI) metric. Moreover, the proposed quadratic CI (Q-CI) metric is derived from the leading quadratic term in the local expansion of the entropy complement, avoiding the logarithmic operations required for direct E-CI evaluation. We apply both proposed metrics to the CIRBP decoder and its node-wise variant. Numerical results show that the proposed metrics generally provide lower frame error rates than the original CI metric, with their relative advantages depending on the code and decoding procedure.

papers.title: Multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for Banach space valued holomorphic functions
Small Harnesses, Default Checks, Limited Coverage: Bounded Model Checking in Practice
papers.abstract: The growing use of AI to generate software and verification artifacts has increased the need for automated systems that provide reliable software assurance. Bounded model checking (BMC) offers a practical foundation for such systems by automatically checking correctness and security properties directly on software. However, effective verification requires choices about properties, input assumptions, function models, and execution bounds that influence the guarantees obtained. Little systematic evidence exists on how practitioners make these choices, limiting the empirical foundation for developing automated verification systems. We present an empirical study of BMC practices in open-source C and Rust projects using CBMC and Kani. Through LLM-assisted open coding, static analysis, and artifact execution, we characterize verification properties, artifact complexity, and verification outcomes. Our findings reveal diverse verification objectives and generally small harnesses, but also property-specification errors and extensive use of execution bounds and environment models. Most artifacts complete verification quickly and achieve high coverage within their scope, while repository-level coverage decreases with project size. Our findings and annotated dataset provide empirical baselines for verification automation and motivate improved techniques for property validation, harness generation, and scaling verification breadth.

papers.title: Lipschitz bounds and gradient continuity for the Trudinger equation
Quantum Dynamics of Dynamics
Read Boundaries in Agent Memory: Consistency, Completeness, and Repair
papers.abstract: Agent-memory services assemble evidence through several reads across connections or stores. An update between those reads can pair an assertion with source content from another revision. We protect the complete recall, including enrichment and materialization, and evaluate the resulting evidence and service behavior in Hindsight and Cognee. A 600-run Cognee study compares unprotected recall, a repeated recall, a read/write lock, and optimistic epoch validation under default incremental updates and full rebuilds. At approximately 20 recalls/s, unprotected default updates yield 199 conflicting responses among 12,010 scheduled recalls with spaced writes and 284 among 12,010 with bursts. The lock and epoch validation each deliver complete, compatible evidence for all 24,020 default-update recalls. With default bursts, epoch validation reduces update p95 by 109 ms while adding 290 ms to recall p95 relative to the lock. A separate 160-run incremental-failure study distinguishes mixed revisions from complete new derived content whose canonical source record remains old. Both protected policies refuse service after failure; the first default retry restores all 80 fault runs through native full-rebuild fallback. In Hindsight, a shared PostgreSQL snapshot removes the mismatch in ten controlled pairs, with recall p95 rising from 19 ms to 29 ms. These results identify the read boundary needed for coherent evidence and the publication and recovery conditions governing service after an update fails.

papers.title: Femtosecond Free-Space Time-Frequency Transfer at km/s Relative Motion with Doppler Compensation
papers.abstract: A global optical clock network holds great promise for a wide range of applications, including international metrology--particularly the redefinition of the ``second''--as well as navigation, geoscience, and fundamental physics. Satellite-based high-precision time-frequency dissemination is essential for realizing such a network. Despite remarkable progress in ground-based free-space simulations over high-loss channels, the Doppler effect arising from satellite motion has remained an unsolved barrier. Here we demonstrate femtosecond two-way time-frequency transfer over a 113-km free-space link under simulated Doppler shifts of up to 1.55 km/s. To overcome the Doppler barrier, we first reproduce satellite-like Doppler shifts of up to 1.55 km/s on the ground by locking a frequency comb to a broadly tunable laser. We then correct the resulting disturbances with two complementary techniques: a dual-channel sampling architecture that compensates for optical dispersion and radio frequency (RF) nonlinearity while eliminating Nyquist dead zones, and an iterative interferogram reconstruction algorithm that removes Doppler-induced distortion. After correction, residual systematic errors are within $\pm10$ fs over the full 1.55 km/s range. Using simulated medium earth orbit (MEO) and geosynchronous orbit (GSO) satellite trajectories, we achieve fractional frequency instability of $3.9\times10^{-19}$ at 4,600 s and $3.6\times10^{-19}$ at 23,600 s, respectively. This extends the operational velocity range by nearly two orders of magnitude beyond previous free-space demonstrations, removing the last major technical barrier to a global femtosecond-precision satellite-based time-frequency link.

papers.title: Half-factorial generating sets and the realization of Dedekind class groups
dit.xpu : Taming DiT Sparse Inference on Mobile SoCs
papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) enable on-device image generation and editing but incur high attention costs at high resolutions. Existing sparse attention reduces computation, yet dynamic sparsity introduces preprocessing and irregular data accesses that poorly fit mobile NPUs. We present this http URL , a sparse DiT inference framework for heterogeneous mobile SoCs. this http URL combines tile-aligned sparse attention with anchor-based error compensation by exploiting slowly varying dense-sparse output residuals across denoising steps. Heterogeneous XPU collaboration overlaps NPU dense attention with GPU sparse calibration, while mask-guided dataflow reduces data transfers and layout conversion by overlapping data movement with computation. Across five DiT models on two Snapdragon smartphones, this http URL achieves up to 1.56x end-to-end denoising speedup over the Hexagon-NPU backend and 11.5x attention-kernel speedup over the fastest alternative, while preserving generation quality close to dense attention. Code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Auditory-Feedback-Conditioned Flow TTS for Implicit Lombard Adaptation
papers.abstract: Conventional text-to-speech (TTS) systems can lose intelligibility in noise environments because they cannot adapt to environmental changes. However, humans tend to increase their vocal efforts in noisy environments, a phenomenon known as the Lombard effect. Building on an auditory-feedback Lombard TTS, we investigate whether a pretrained Flow-based TTS can learn acoustic adaptation directly from auditory feedback without explicit prosodic control. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) feedback and automatic speech recognition (ASR) feedback are extracted from the noise-corrupted waveforms and injected into the Flow-matching condition for utterance refinement and causal block-level updates. We assess feedback benefits across prompting and noise conditions using plain/Lombard prompting, prompt-switching controls, and paired-finetuning. Experiments show that while finetuning provides strong robustness under in-domain conditions, auditory feedback yields additional cue-dependent benefits that generalize to unseen noise. Moreover, stronger power/F0 tracking alone does not guarantee better speech intelligibility or quality.

papers.title: Thermal-energy relaxation in chiral quantum Hall edge mode
papers.abstract: We study the nonequilibrium state generated by a real Ohmic contact (ROC) in the charge-fractionalization regime. We then investigate its thermal-energy relaxation along a quantum Hall edge mediated by a fictitious Ohmic contact (FOC) with large capacitance and perfect coupling to the edge. For cold Ohmic contacts, the electron distribution function and current noise are fully described by their equilibrium forms and the corresponding Fermi-Dirac distribution. In contrast, in the case of hot Ohmic contacts, strong thermalization effects do not drive the outgoing state into complete equilibrium. Both the distribution function and the noise retain signatures of the initial nonequilibrium state and therefore cannot be characterized solely by the effective contact temperature, contrary to common assumptions.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for Riesz capacity in all dimensions
A unified cross-scale framework for the dynamic Waddington landscape
Independent Sets in $C_4$-Free Planar Graphs: Sharp Claw-Free Bounds and Structural Reductions
Many faces of integer semidefinite programming
Bringing coherent closer to compute: coherent-lite multidimensional on-chip interconnect beyond 100 terabits per second
papers.abstract: The continued scaling of artificial intelligence (AI) demands optical interconnects that deliver higher bandwidth density within stringent electrical-bandwidth and energy budgets. Coherent optics offers a route beyond the per-lane bandwidth constraints of intensity-modulation direct-detection links, yet its receiver complexity and power overhead have largely confined its use to longer reaches. Here we bring coherent optics closer to compute by demonstrating a coherent-lite multidimensional on-chip interconnect that combines wavelength- and mode-division multiplexing with self-homodyne detection. The architecture co-transmits the local oscillator (LO) and parallel data channels within a single silicon waveguide, using polarization-division routing to preserve LO purity and support high-order modulation. Based on this principle, we develop an inverse-designed dual-polarization mode multiplexer that provides over 37 dB inter-polarization isolation across the C band in an $8 \times 6~\mu$m$^2$ footprint, enabling millimetre-scale on-chip multimode routing. Without power-intensive digital carrier recovery, the architecture delivers a single-wavelength line rate of 2 Tb s$^{-1}$ and scales to an aggregate line rate of 103.96 Tb s$^{-1}$ across four modes and 100 wavelengths, using formats up to 64-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). These results extend on-chip coherent interconnects into the hundred-terabit-per-second regime, offering a scalable route to bandwidth-dense optical connectivity for next-generation computing systems.

papers.title: KaleidoKV: Rearranging Evidence for Efficient KV Cache Reuse in Offline RAG Inference
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) augments large language models (LLMs) on question-answering (QA) tasks with retrieved evidence at inference time. Related questions in an offline batch often retrieve overlapping evidence, but prefix caching reuses key-value (KV) states only for identical token prefixes, making reuse dependent on evidence order. Although all questions and evidence are known before execution, existing reordering methods commit to early grouping decisions and can miss sharing opportunities that require several requests to move together. Evaluating alternative layouts can incur planning costs that offset inference savings, while concurrent requests may still recompute shared prefixes before their KV states become available. To address these challenges, we propose KaleidoKV, a framework that plans evidence orders across the batch and controls when requests enter the engine while preserving each request's evidence set and content. Joint layout planning revises formed groups through coordinated request moves and keeps a move only if it lowers planned prefill, the computation required when each shared prefix is computed once. A global prefix index selects evidence orders by locating reusable prefixes and evaluates each move incrementally from only the affected request paths. Prefix-ready admission tracks nested prefix dependencies, delaying requests whose shared prefixes are still being computed while allowing independent requests to proceed. Experiments on four QA workloads and four LLMs show that KaleidoKV achieves the highest throughput and lowest mean time to first token in all 16 settings, with approximately 1.24-1.75x the throughput of the strongest baseline, including planning time. With Llama-3.1-8B under the default configuration, actual prefill stays within 0.5% of planned prefill across all four workloads.

papers.title: Exploration as Feedback in Model Predictive Path Integral Control
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how exploration affects closed-loop stability in model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. With a warm start, MPPI optimizes a control sequence by sampling candidates around the previous solution, and their covariance, the exploration covariance, is typically tuned to balance solution quality and computational cost. Small exploration is attractive because most samples then contribute to the solution, and existing stability analyses treat reduced exploration only as a bias toward the previous solution. Whether insufficient exploration can destabilize the closed loop has therefore remained open. We show that, for linear quadratic (LQ) problems with infinitely many samples, the exploration covariance also determines the feedback gain, i.e., how strongly MPPI updates the previous solution in response to the current state. With small exploration at a fixed temperature, MPPI nearly repeats the previous solution and fails to stabilize an exponentially unstable plant. Because a single covariance governs both exploration and feedback, stability and sample efficiency are in structural conflict: stabilization requires large exploration, which leaves few samples that contribute to the solution. To resolve this conflict, we propose Stabilizing Subspace MPPI (SS-MPPI), which computes the control inputs required for stabilization and samples only the rest. For LQ problems, SS-MPPI remains stable with small exploration and is thus sample-efficient. Simulations of an inverted pendulum and a quadruped robot confirm the analysis, showing that MPPI fails under small exploration, whereas SS-MPPI remains stable even with few samples.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning for Nonstationary Robot Dynamics
papers.abstract: Reasoning about what an action will cause requires internalizing how a system behaves. As conditions seldom stay fixed, this must often happen within a few interactions. Yet systems that look identical in a snapshot can respond differently to the same action, depending on physical conditions the snapshot hides. Context-based models capture this separation by summarizing recent transitions into a latent context, but do not specify how that context should change the equations of motion. Physics-informed neural networks build those equations into the model, but describe only a single system and cannot recognize when it has changed. We present Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning (PICR), which bridges the two. Only a context, re-inferred from recent interactions, is updated; it conditions a fixed physics-informed network that determines the robot's inertia and potential energy, so the robot adapts to new physical conditions from its own experience without retraining or a hand-specified robot model. On a Franka Panda arm in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, PICR predicts motion under changing and unseen payloads, reducing error on the latter by 1.6-3.8x over baselines, and extends to counterfactual queries under alternative torques. Our analysis shows that the context, inferred solely from interaction, encodes payload physical properties, tracks their changes, and governs the arm's response. The gravity and inertia terms induced by the context further demonstrate its physical validity, each agreeing with the simulator at the level of individual Lagrangian components.

papers.title: Learning Graph-Conditioned Predictors in Weight Space
papers.abstract: The same node attributes can imply different labels in different structural contexts. Yet fast graphless models typically treat topology as additional evidence supplied to a globally shared predictor. This assumes that structure augments the available information, rather than determining how node attributes should be interpreted. We introduce SCOPE (Structure-COnditioned PrEdictor), in which a small generator maps each node's cached structural fingerprint to coefficients over a shared low-rank basis, producing a context-specific update to a global weight matrix. The base predictor, basis, and generator remain shared across all nodes, while the resulting transformation adapts how attributes are processed in each relational environment. Once fingerprints are cached, inference requires only a forward pass and no online message passing. This design combines context-specific specialization with global parameter sharing, compact low-rank adaptation, and message-passing-free inference. On two large OGB node-classification graphs, conditioning the weights with raw positional signals yields clear gains over supplying the same signals through input concatenation. Further results under a structure-transductive held-out-node protocol and in teacher-free graph classification show that the mechanism extends beyond a particular distillation setting. These findings establish graph structure not only as predictive evidence, but as context that determines the predictor used to interpret that evidence.

papers.title: Classification problems for diassociative and dendriform algebras: a survey
Size-Matched Nulls Reveal What Block Ablation Measures in MambaVision
papers.abstract: Hybrid vision backbones interleave Mamba state-space mixers with self-attention, and a block's role is usually probed by removing it and measuring the damage. We test what that measurement means in MambaVision. On all 50,000 ImageNet validation images and three model sizes, every block ablation is paired with a size-matched null, the same perturbation with its channels shuffled or their signs flipped. In top-1 accuracy and in true-class rank, real and null damage are nearly indistinguishable in absolute terms: pooled over the blocks of MambaVision-T, the content effect lies within [-0.044,+0.016] percentage points (90% interval). Two attention-only controls show that the test detects content, with real ablations worse than their nulls by up to 4.2 points in DeiT-Small and 1.0 point in Swin-T. Part of MambaVision's near-equivalence reflects how little damage its blocks do (0.11--0.34 points on average, against 1.7 and 2.1). Scaled by damage, its content share is comparable to Swin-T's in accuracy, lower in rank, and far below DeiT-Small's: single-block damage in MambaVision is small and mostly positional. Ablation also hides what blocks carry together: removing all blocks of one type compounds damage to 3.7--8.4 times the sum of single effects, far more than size-matched nulls, including nulls that keep the alignment between the blocks' perturbations; for adjacent pairs, aligned nulls reproduce most of it. Freezing input-dependent selection in all Mamba mixers shows that it accounts for 20--32% of the Mamba contribution, mainly through the B and C projections. We turn these results into a protocol for causal attribution in hybrid networks.

papers.title: GameWM: Toward Next-Generation Video Games with Interaction-Centric World Models
papers.abstract: For more than half a century, video games have pursued better graphics, more natural interaction, and more engaging gameplay. Generative video models (VMs) now bear on all three. Neural networks already draw most of the pixels in shipped games, and recent world models let a lightweight game engine keep the world state while a VM turns the engine's coarse proxy video into final frames. These systems, however, treat the VM as a renderer that only restyles motion the engine has already authored, which leaves most of its generative capacity unused and limits the diversity a game can offer. We present GameWM, a design for next-generation games built on a clear division of labor. The GameWM-engine keeps what must be exact: rules, state, camera, and the layout of the world, which also spares the video model from having to remember it. The GameWM-VM generates what is expensive to author by hand: the look of the world and the detail of the player's interactions. One game mechanic can then be realized in many visually and physically distinct ways, while its outcome stays exactly as the engine computed it. To realize this division of labor, we build GameWM as a complete system: a data engine centered on interactions rather than exploration, an interface through which authored character sheets, scene art, and skill descriptions enter the model, and a model family from 5B to 33B parameters with a real-time causal variant for play. Together they give every player a fresh version of the same game: each player's own character, world, and skills turn the same engine mechanics into a new experience, while every event keeps the timing and outcome the GameWM-engine computed.

papers.title: On the Power-Law Duality in Wigner-Yang Quantum Mechanics
Integrated Co-design Framework for High-Efficiency Assembly and Integration of Small Satellites
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of small-satellite constellations has increased the need for higher manufacturing throughput, lower production costs, and shorter turnaround times. This makes efficient assembly, integration, and testing (AIT) increasingly important. Building on our prior work, this paper presents an integrated design-for-AIT approach for the 65 kg Lumelite-5 satellite. The integrated approach incorporates co-designing the satellite configuration, structural interfaces, subsystem placement, harness routing, and ground support equipment to facilitate efficient AIT. Service interfaces are centralized on one satellite side to simplify electrical ground support equipment access and routing. Skeletal support interfaces are developed to retain mounted components and service interfaces when removable enclosures are opened to expose internal harness-routing paths for inspection, troubleshooting, and rework. Defined mechanical references further support controlled removal and reinstallation of sensors and components. A removable double hinge ground-support mechanism allows the top deck to open up to 180 degrees relative to the bottom deck while accommodating interconnecting-harness articulation, without introducing permanent hinge mass and complexity to the satellite. Finally, dedicated harness-routing and tie-down provisions provide predefined yet adjustable restraint locations to accommodate as built routing variations and maintain controlled harness articulation during top-deck rotation. Through this work, we demonstrate how co-designing satellite architecture and AIT processes from the early development stages can support more scalable, repeatable, and efficient constellation production.

papers.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $\tau^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $\tau^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $\tau^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

papers.title: Veech dichotomy for specific covering surface over Veech surface
Teralizer: A Tool for Generalizing JUnit Tests into Property-Based jqwik Tests
papers.abstract: Background: Property-based testing validates properties across many generated inputs and can thereby detect regressions that conventional unit tests miss. However, writing property-based tests is challenging for practitioners, which limits their adoption. Tool: Teralizer automatically generalizes JUnit tests into property-based jqwik tests for regression detection. Through single-path symbolic analysis, it extracts from each test execution a path condition, which characterizes the inputs that follow the same execution path, and a symbolic output expression, which computes the expected output for these inputs. The generalized tests generate inputs that satisfy the path condition and use the symbolic output expression as the oracle. Results: In our evaluation, generalization increased the mutation scores of EvoSuite-generated test suites by 0.8 to 3.9 percentage points. On the EqBench benchmark, generalizing the test suites that EvoSuite generated with 1 s per class reached the mutation score of EvoSuite's 60 s test suites with 31.9% less total runtime. Availability: Teralizer is available as open source at this https URL .

papers.title: HyperDBDiag: Multi-Root-Cause Identification and Operator-Level Localization for Database Performance Anomalies
papers.abstract: Database performance anomalies in modern production environments are not always triggered by a single cause. Instead, they often arise from the concurrent interaction of multiple causes within the same time window, posing substantial challenges to accurate operator-level root-cause analysis. When multiple root causes interact through shared resources, metric anomalies may be amplified, attenuated, or masked. Consequently, salient local anomalies may no longer correspond directly to the actual root causes, making conventional single-path diagnosis and shallow correlation-based methods prone to misdiagnosis. To address this challenge, we propose HyperDBDiag, a method for multi-root-cause identification and operator-level localization of database performance anomalies. HyperDBDiag connects root causes, performance metrics, SQL templates, and execution operators in a knowledge graph, captures joint anomaly patterns across metrics with a metric hypergraph, and uses a constrained LLM to determine the final root-cause set and provide remediation suggestions. When finer-grained localization is possible, HyperDBDiag also identifies the associated anomalous SQL statements and execution operators. We evaluate HyperDBDiag on a database performance anomaly dataset constructed using DB-MAGS. Experimental results show that HyperDBDiag effectively reduces graph complexity while improving root-cause localization accuracy.

papers.title: Numerical evidence for the validity of the inverse hoop conjecture for black holes
papers.abstract: The inverse hoop (IH) conjecture, ${\cal M}_{\text{irr}}\leq {\cal C}_{\text{s}}/4\pi$, originally discussed in the context of stationary black-hole configurations, suggests that the surface area of a black hole cannot undergo unconstrained geometric wrinkling (here ${\cal M}_{\text{irr}}=\sqrt{{\cal A}/16\pi}$ is the irreducible mass associated with the horizon area ${\cal A}$ of the black hole and ${\cal C}_{\text{s}}$ is the circumference length of the smallest ring that can engulf the horizon of the black hole in every direction). In the present compact paper we provide evidence supporting the validity of the IH conjecture for non-stationary black-hole configurations. In particular, we show that all the non-stationary black-hole solutions recently constructed by Croft, García-Moreno, and Pani (CGP) [ arXiv:2611.13266 ] satisfy the IH relation.

papers.title: Global dynamics and the diffusive limit of the one-species non-cutoff Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system
Continuous Lower-Limb Joint-Angle Estimation from sEMG and IMU: The Conditional Value of Cross-Activity and Cross-Subject Data under Update-Matched Controls
papers.abstract: Intent-driven exoskeleton control needs a continuous, causal estimate of the wearer's joint kinematics and an answer to a second question: whose data should train the estimator for a new user? Borrowing the user's recordings of other activities, or other users' recordings of the same activity, is usually evaluated as "more data" versus "less data," which confounds the information a source carries with the optimizer updates it adds and hides negative transfer behind averages. We separate these effects for hip, knee, and ankle angle estimation from high-density sEMG and an IMU across six locomotion activities on all ten participants of a public dataset. A compact residual causal TCN-GRU decoder is frozen, and an update-matched replay control prices every added source against the same number of updates on the user's own data. A user's own other activities raise $R^2$ from 0.722 to 0.788, of which +0.048 is information beyond replay; stair descent is a reliably harmful donor and sit-stand-walk a reliably beneficial one. Other users' same-activity data help while the user has only the target activity ($G_\mathrm{T} = +0.053$) and half as much once own other-activity data exist ($G_\mathrm{W} = +0.028$); at full calibration, donor value collapses after one to two target records. Per-target gains from the two sources correlate, and leave-one-participant-out gates recover most of the cross-subject value only at low calibration. Data value is hierarchical, state-dependent, and directional; the bottleneck is deciding, without test labels, when to transfer.

papers.title: Auditable Authorization for LLM Agents: Empirical Evidence Across Model, Harness, and Workflow Layers
papers.abstract: Human approval provides effective control only if rejected work stops and authorized work completes. We formalize refusal safety and bounded authorization completeness, and audit three execution boundaries: the model selects a call, the harness schedules and resumes it, and the workflow routes the decision to a protected effect. Paired decisions, exact traces, and native business-state witnesses support experiments with three models, five prompt arms, four runtime approval designs, two additional framework replays, and 100 public workflow sources. The paired model panel leaves seven of 300 approvals unfinished despite zero denied effects; parallel confirmation loses an approved branch in three tasks per model, restoration omits 336/672 CrewAI approvals, and four of 59 comparable n8n workflows execute after Reject. Comparing intent, generated calls, dispatch, and native effects identifies the first observable divergence and its repair target. This yields a practical audit contract that makes both refusal safety and authorization completeness independently verifiable, converting human approval from a procedural formality into an enforceable control boundary between intent and real-world effect.

papers.title: Attribution-Guided Shared-Private Decoupling for Noise-Reduced Audio-Visual Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Audio-visual representation learning commonly aligns paired audio and visual signals with sample-level contrastive objectives. However, real-world audio-visual pairs usually contain heterogeneous patch tokens: only a subset carries reliable cross-modal shared semantics, while many others mainly encode modality-private residuals. Aggregating all tokens into a single global representation can therefore introduce semantic noise into cross-modal alignment. Motivated by the minimal-sufficiency principle, we propose an attribution-guided shared-private decoupling framework to mitigate this issue. Our key idea is to identify shared-cover subviews that preserve dominant cross-modal information while suppressing modality-private residuals, and use them to supervise decoupled shared and private representations. To identify such subviews efficiently, we draw on transformer attribution method and introduce Layer-Truncated Attribution (LTA), which provides a lightweight estimate of token-level relevance to cross-modal shared information. We further adopt a teacher-student framework, where the teacher provides attribution-induced supervision and the student internalizes shared-private decoupling into its representations, without introducing extra inference cost. Experiments on retrieval, classification, and sound-prompted semantic segmentation show consistent gains over strong baselines. Compared with baseline, our method improves the average zero-shot R@1 by 4.0 across AudioSet and VGGSound retrieval, and improves AS20K classification mAP by 3.1, demonstrating the effectiveness of fine grained attribution guidance for reducing semantic this http URL semantic noise. Code will be released at this https URL

papers.title: Spectral Gaps and Low-Energy Modes in Anisotropic High-Contrast PDEs
papers.abstract: We study the low-energy spectrum of high-contrast partial differential equations with strongly anisotropic inclusions. The inclusion stiffness and mass are scaled by a contrast parameter \(\eta\), while a small material eigenvalue \(\epsilon\) controls anisotropy. Stable extensions of local kernel fields give eigenvalue upper bounds proportional to the inverse contrast, uniformly in anisotropy. Additional low-energy modes arise from fields whose nonzero differential images lie in weak material directions. Each fixed family of compatible weak fields yields additional eigenvalue upper bounds of order $\epsilon+ \eta^{-1}$, provided a stable extension exists. Under discrete stability assumptions, we obtain corresponding finite element bounds for the weak modes represented by the mesh. For separable scalar diffusion, we prove norm-resolvent convergence to independent background Dirichlet and inclusion Neumann operators as contrast tends to infinity with anisotropy fixed. Numerical experiments for four PDE models illustrate weak modes and mesh-dependent spectral transitions, and scalar diffusion experiments also test spectral decoupling and eigenvalue counting.

papers.title: Fundamental group and $Q$-curvature on open four-manifolds
The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere from multi-target density matrix renormalization group
papers.abstract: The fuzzy-sphere regularization provides a powerful framework for studying three-dimensional (3D) conformal field theories (CFTs) through radial quantization, but conformal defects have so far been studied with it only by exact diagonalization (ED) of small systems. In this work we realize the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere by imposing antiperiodic boundary conditions on the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-odd fermion flavor, and solve it with a multi-target density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) algorithm that optimizes several low-lying states of each symmetry sector in a common matrix-product basis. This gives the defect spectrum at system sizes well beyond the reach of ED (up to $2s+1=25$, or $49$ spinless orbitals). The spectrum obeys the spin-parity selection rule of the twist line and organizes into conformal multiplets along the line. Using the displacement operator as an intrinsic ruler, its protected descendant as a test, and the bulk stress tensor as an independent cross-check, we identify the leading finite-size corrections and obtain controlled continuum extrapolations, which sharpen the dimensions of several known defect primaries and resolve four higher-lying ones. This study establishes the fuzzy sphere combined with multi-target DMRG as a framework for precision studies of conformal defects.

papers.title: Beyond Alignment: Supervising the Generator for EEG-to-Image Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Visual brain decoding translates neural activity into human-interpretable images. While recent EEG-to-image reconstruction methods rely on aligning EEG signals with pretrained visual embeddings to condition an image generator, we empirically demonstrate that stronger cross-modal alignment do not translate into comparable gains in reconstruction quality. This indicates that improving the input condition alone is insufficient; the generative process itself requires explicit supervision. Although Representation Alignment (REPA) offers a solution by guiding diffusion transformers with pretrained vision encoder features, we find that EEG-conditioned generators struggle to follow these fixed targets. To address this mismatch, we introduce generation-derived supervision (GDS): an image-conditioned teacher that translates static image-encoder features into the internal representation space of a diffusion transformer. Our EEG-conditioned student generator closely tracks these dynamic targets during denoising, discarding the teacher at inference. Evaluated on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG, our approach consistently outperforms conditioning-centric baselines, achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity.

papers.title: EdgeNet City: Context-Aware AI-RAN Planning toward Autonomous Urban Connectivity
papers.abstract: The evolution from 5G toward 6G calls for more anticipatory and context-aware Cell-on-Wheels (COW) planning in wireless networks. We present EdgeNet City, an online framework that grounds free-form natural-language inputs in geographic activity representations and path-gain data. A catalog-referenced representation links activity roles, geographic features and predefined demand profiles, separating semantic selection from deterministic spatial computation. The algorithm combines prescribed demand with relative propagation support to screen service areas for subsequent COW assessment. We publicly release a London dataset with 22,678 transmitters, approximately 449.4 billion path-gain records and retained receiver geometry. Within prepared propagation domains, the online prototype reuses these records without new ray tracing or live operator measurements. In a matched 20-event study across six London environments, the expanded representation increases mean spatial overlap with the reused full technical-review reference from 0.4929 for the single-feature Venue-only baseline to 0.7203. Rule-based and language-model planners select identical activities in this panel. With need-aware ranking and a three-cell diagnostic budget fixed, the expanded representation increases mean Reference-need Capture by 25.44 percentage points over Venue-only.

papers.title: CompoundingKernel: Self-Improving from Zero to First
papers.abstract: We present CompoundingKernel, a self-improving agent system that writes GPU kernels by search. As of 2026-11-11, its generated kernels rank #1 on the public L1, L2 and Quantization boards of SOL-ExecBench (NVIDIA B200). They have held #1 on L1 since 2026-10-27, albeit a short loss on 2026-11-07. All 235 problems have a site-verified correct kernel; on the 209 public-board problems they are 4.40x faster than the benchmark's reference baseline. The search starts from zero: agents get each problem's PyTorch definition but no reference kernels or official scores. A per-problem archive outside the model holds every correct kernel and its lineage. An LLM controller reads it, picks a parent or a new design, and gives each parallel child agent one direction. Checks outside the model decide correctness. At equal wall time, it beat a coded UCB style tree on 35 of 38 problems by making 2.4x as many correct attempts. Over a thousand agents ran at once, and one warm restart fix raised their evaluation rate 3.6x. We find that the rate of reliable measurements, not the number of agents, limits how far such a search scales. Our code and kernels are available on URL.

papers.title: Feedback-Aware Residual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Timely Communication in Cognitive Radio Networks
papers.abstract: Supporting time-sensitive services in cognitive radio networks requires distributed access strategies that translate shared spectrum opportunities into timely packet delivery. Achieving this objective is challenging because reception conditions are only partially observable to individual transmitters, while dynamic competition and access overhead constrain the service that can be completed within packet deadlines. We formulate a distributed access problem that captures the coupling among interference-dependent reception, queue evolution, and protocol durations. To address this problem, we propose feedback-aware residual multi-agent proximal policy optimization (FAR-MAPPO) under centralized training and decentralized execution. The method constructs channel-specific historical feedback representations that complement instantaneous sensing with evidence from completed access attempts. A residual policy network integrates this experience with current observations and packet urgency to guide local access decisions. Numerical results show improved timely delivery over the baseline methods, particularly under heavy traffic and bursty arrivals with mixed packet deadlines.

papers.title: Sum of Powers with Matrix Coefficients
Can an Agent Rethink What It Knows? Selective Scene Memory Updates in a Changing World
papers.abstract: Task configurations in factories, warehouses, and everyday physical environments change over time. Physical AI systems therefore need to incorporate new facts into scene memory while preserving valid information about equipment, objects, and operating constraints. We study updates to this parametric semantic-memory layer and present a joint evaluation of correction and preservation under finite update budgets. At fixed current fact count and memory parameter count, the protocol combines independent single-fact updates, budget trajectories, old-to-new answer diagnostics, and first stable success. Using a frozen 4B language model with late-layer LoRA, we evaluate seven preparation conditions and six update budgets on four-field synthetic semantic configurations. In two exposure-matched history conditions, increasing the budget from eight to 32 updates raises joint success from 6.25% to 94.79% and 91.15%, respectively, while exact obsolete-value outputs fall from 174/192 and 166/192 to zero. Constant32, which matches preparation steps but repeatedly trains on unchanged content during the first 32 events, achieves higher early joint success at eight steps (53.65%); at 32 steps, it reaches 85.42%, below both changing-history conditions. These results distinguish rapid correction under a small budget from simultaneous correctness of the new fact and the other three facts after further training. For both changing histories, most cases remain jointly correct at all subsequent measured points from step 16 onward. Output analysis shows that short-budget failures primarily retain the old value; repeated training on the new fact together with the other current facts progressively replaces these obsolete answers.

papers.title: Temporal Attention-Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts Guidance for Multi-Revolution Low-Thrust Rendezvous
papers.abstract: Multi-revolution low-thrust rendezvous requires both long-duration orbital transfer and precise terminal control. This paper proposes a temporal attention-enhanced mixture-of-experts guidance law trained by deep reinforcement learning. A far-range expert acts on modified equinoctial elements, a terminal expert acts on the relative state in the target's local frame, and a learned gate blends their thrust commands. The terminal expert encodes its observation history with a Transformer to address partial observability, and the gate uses a separate encoder to account for the resulting history-dependent command. The experts are pretrained separately, the gate is trained with both experts frozen, and the complete guidance law is then fine-tuned end to end. On 600 test missions, it achieves rendezvous in every case at tolerances of 10 m and 1 m/s, reduces mean flight time and delta-v by 50.6% and 44.5% relative to distance-based hard switching, and remains successful without retraining under navigation errors, unmodeled orbital perturbations, eclipse-induced thrust outages, and thrust loss.

papers.title: Budgeted Decision-Model-Guided Joint-Action Search for Satellite Edge Computing
papers.abstract: Efficient task offloading in satellite edge computing requires coordinated allocation of communication and computing resources. Search methods based on large language models (LLMs) have been shown to generate high-quality resource allocations, but the latency of individual model requests and repeated model interactions can lead to substantial solver overhead. We propose budgeted joint-action search (BJAS), an integrated decision-model-guided solver that jointly optimizes satellite offloading and power allocation to minimize average task-completion latency under explicit search budgets. Its bounded candidate pools combine single-terminal updates with power-inheriting offload replacements for batched selection, retaining two-terminal coordination without enumerating additional power vectors. Across 60 completed runs per method under the workflows' respective configurations, BJAS reduces mean total solver time by 97.16% relative to LLM-generated offloading while achieving a mean task-completion latency close to that of the LLM baseline. BJAS also achieves lower mean task-completion latency than the tested genetic algorithm and deep deterministic policy gradient baselines.

papers.title: Quadratic Embedding Constants of Block Graphs and Characterization of Cactus-like Graphs
ProSing: Zero-Shot Fine-Grained Singing Technique Conversion
papers.abstract: We study zero-shot fine-grained singing technique conversion (STC), which applies specified techniques to selected regions of an existing singing recording while preserving lyrics, melody, timing, and singer identity. Existing singing conversion and synthesis methods offer complementary strengths in source preservation and explicit technique control, but combining both in an audio-to-audio setting remains underexplored, especially with limited technique-annotated data. We propose ProSing, a zero-shot fine-grained STC framework that adapts a pretrained flow-matching acoustic model with frame-level technique conditioning. To mitigate conditioning shortcuts during adaptation, we introduce a paired training strategy to learn generalizable technique representations. We further incorporate continuous pitch trajectories for explicit and expressive control of pitch-related techniques. Subjective and objective evaluations on unseen singers and source recordings show that ProSing achieves accurate technique control while preserving singing naturalness and singer similarity.

papers.title: Strong Well-Posedness for One-Dimensional Quantile-Dependent SDEs with Hölder-Continuous Diffusion
A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents
Revisiting What Makes a Good Context Subset: A Sparse Latent Basis Perspective
papers.abstract: Selecting context subsets is increasingly important in modern LLM inference, yet what makes a subset effective remains unclear. We study this question in the controlled setting of few-shot demonstration selection. We examine a hypothesis that demonstrations should collectively provide task-relevant information needed by a target query. Assuming that the query representation provides a useful proxy for these requirements, we formulate selection as sparse reconstruction and instantiate it with Residual Explanation Search (RES), a Matching-Pursuit-style diagnostic procedure. Across seven benchmarks and eight open-weight LLMs, no retrieval objective is universally best. RES outperforms MMR in 34 of 56 model--dataset pairs, with its clearest advantage on sentiment tasks, suggesting that query-conditioned collective reconstruction may capture useful complementarity that pairwise dissimilarity misses. Relevance-based retrieval remains strong on template-heavy reasoning benchmarks, while all retrieval methods underperform zero-shot prediction on average on StrategyQA, where a solution-reconstruction analysis is consistent with the query not exposing the required external knowledge. Target-model hidden states further show that retrieval objectives interact differently with representation spaces: middle-layer representations generally favor similarity retrieval, whereas last-layer representations are often stronger for residual- and diversity-based selection. These findings support a conditional, representation-dependent account of context subset quality rather than a universally superior selector.

papers.title: Stabilizing Parabolic Vector Bundles
Neural Dual Bounds: Valid-by-Construction JGLP Warm-Starts for MAP and Constrained MAP
papers.abstract: We present Neural Dual Bounds, a calibration-free framework that produces deterministic upper bounds for MAP inference in probabilistic graphical models using a single neural-network forward pass. The framework trains a network to output the edge messages of a mini-bucket style upper bound on a given join-graph decomposition in a self-supervised manner by directly minimizing a smooth dual objective. The output of this network can be used at test time to warm-start a standard JGLP optimizer. Across diverse benchmarks, this warm start yields dual gaps that are orders of magnitude tighter than those from zero initialization, with the largest gains in the early-iteration regime. We also apply our framework for the constrained MAP (CMPE) task, where neural warm starts with test-time adaptation are comparable to the adaptive baseline on Bayesian networks and achieve the tightest dual gaps, by one to two orders of magnitude, on the grid and segmentation families.

papers.title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
Operating-Point Failure of Frozen Guardrail Probes Under Backbone Updates
papers.abstract: We freeze a guardrail probe and threshold, then measure its operating point across 18 cells covering 16 public language-model updates. At a 1% target, the threshold fails closed in 8 of 9 cells in the first phase and either fails closed or open in 3 of 9 cells in a registered second phase (descriptive). The two phases also differ in update type and input format. The largest increase is from 1.01% to 15.12%, while the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve changes by no more than 0.0058 in any of these cells. A benchmark's staleness criteria classify none of them as stale. A rule based on these criteria flags 0.019 of layer cells where the rate doubles or halves. A label-free rate estimate flags 0.918, clearing 0.898 of the remaining cells. A two-moment model matches the change within a factor of 1.5 in 0.905 of 63 registered cells and in 0.773 of the 22 cells that moved. Resetting the threshold using stored benign prompts restores the false-positive rate without requiring new labels. However, poisoning 1% of these prompts leaves at most 0.017 of harmful prompts flagged. An attacker controlling the update cut detection of one of three targeted categories in three of five seeds. Both checks missed this attack, while a post hoc labelled check detected it.

papers.title: Mem2Fair: Online Fairness Control for Text-to-Video Generation via Fair Memory
papers.abstract: Text-to-video (T2V) generation models can produce systematically unfair demographic outcomes when prompts leave protected attributes unspecified. For example, prompts describing nurses without specifying gender may disproportionately generate videos depicting female nurses. Mitigating unfairness in T2V generation is particularly challenging: training-based methods that modify model internals require architecture-specific access and risk disrupting temporal consistency, while sampling-based methods often incur costly pre-deployment video generation. We present the first conditional online approachability formulation of attribute-level fairness for T2V generation. Building on this formulation, we introduce Mem2Fair, a plug-and-play framework that maintains concept-conditioned Fair Memory. Using generated videos at inference time as feedback, Mem2Fair selects prompt-level attribute interventions based on the deviation from each concept's prescribed fairness target, without training or separate pre-deployment sampling. Experiments demonstrate that Mem2Fair consistently improves fairness over the unmodified generator and existing baselines across multiple demographic attributes, prompt settings, and target distributions, while maintaining comparable prompt-video alignment and video quality. We further demonstrate its effectiveness on commercial black-box T2V models.

papers.title: STaSBO: LLM-Guided Strategy Planning and Configuration Selection for Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) enables sample-efficient search for expensive black-box problems, but its performance depends strongly on surrogate-acquisition configurations whose suitability varies across problems and optimization states. We take a significant step toward LLM-driven strategic management of BO with STaSBO, a task-agnostic meta-controller that plans search behavior and jointly selects surrogate-acquisition configurations, while numerical BO retains responsibility for probabilistic modeling and candidate generation. STaSBO comprises two coordinated stages: strategy planning and strategy-guided configuration selection. A structured memory system connects prior plans, configuration selections, and candidate behaviors to optimization states, allowing the controller to revise its trajectory summary and behavioral plans during planning. To navigate the large joint configuration space, the selection stage shortlists configurations using surrogate fit evidence. Prospective BO-action diagnostics then expose the candidate behaviors, supporting final joint selection against the behavioral plans. Across 12 synthetic mathematical and 10 scientific and engineering application tasks, STaSBO achieves the best average rank against 11 baselines: 2.17 and 2.60, compared with 4.08 and 4.10 for the strongest baseline in each suite, respectively.

papers.title: Incremental Learning of Vision-Language Models via Task Subspace Projection and Dynamic LoRA
papers.abstract: Recent pre-trained vision-language models often encounter a Multi-Domain Task-Incremental Learning (MTIL) scenario in practice, where a set of classes of multi-modal tasks arrive incrementally. Due to privacy concerns and memory constraints, MTIL with pre-trained models encounters forgetting of knowledge from old tasks, degradation of zero-shot transfer capability, and underfitting of new-task knowledge. To overcome these challenges, previous MTIL methods attempt to learn a discriminative cross-task identification (CTI) module and an effective new-task adaptation (NTA) module. However, current CTI modules suffer from severe task confusion between seen and unseen tasks, and NTA modules cannot adaptively balance the performance and parameter cost while incorporating task-specific knowledge. To alleviate the above dilemmas, we propose an effective and efficient TSP-DLoRA method for MTIL, which consists of Task Subspace Projection (TSP) and Dynamic Low Rank Adapter (DLoRA) modules. Specifically, our TSP module includes a task identifier classifier based on task-specific subspaces and a feature projection strategy that can determine the identifier associated with samples from both seen and unseen tasks. Our DLoRA improves the knowledge adaptation from new tasks by dynamically assigning Low Rank Adapter (LoRA) across transformer layers based on the task distributions. Experimental evaluations across 11 datasets, using three performance metrics, demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. Code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Site-Specific Cell Shaping: An Agentic Framework
