Finally, our analysis of the logit-space behavior illustrates how asymmetric fusion successfully mitigates base model overconfidence. Overall, our findings demonstrate that the benefits of an asymmetric fusion successfully transfer to the language domain, providing a simple, highly cost-efficient approach to improving uncertainty estimation in LLM classifiers.

papers.title: Averaged-Cost Control with Shared Feedback under Model Uncertainty
papers.abstract: This paper studies the shared-feedback design problem for finite-horizon averaged-cost control under model uncertainty represented by a joint law over the model parameter and initial state. One feedback map is shared across all realizations and uses only time and the current state as online inputs. We develop two methods: the nonlinear adjoint method combines forward closed-loop solves, backward adjoints, and joint-law policy gradients, while the linear moment method gives exact cost and gradient formulas for a homogeneous linear-quadratic design model by propagating conditional second moments. Numerical studies compare averaged and nominal designs for time-dependent neural feedback and static linear feedback in nonlinear Van der Pol and Stuart-Landau systems; the static gains are designed from oscillator linearizations and evaluated on the original nonlinear systems. Averaged design has lower cost in most comparisons.

papers.title: A PTAS for Euclidean Capacitated Vehicle Routing
papers.abstract: In the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP), introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959, we are given an $n$-node graph $G=(V,E)$ with metric edges costs $c(e)$, a depot $r\in V$, and an integer vehicle capacity $Q$. The goal is to find a minimum-cost collection of tours, each containing the depot and visiting at most other $Q$ nodes, such that the tours cover all the nodes. In this paper we focus on the Euclidean CVRP problem, where the nodes represent points on $\mathbb{R}^2$, and the edge costs are the respective Euclidean distances. Euclidean CVRP generalizes the classical NP-hard Euclidean TSP problem (the special case with $Q=n-1$), that admits a PTAS [Arora FOCS'96/Mitchell SODA'96]. A long-standing open problem has been generalizing the latter PTAS to Euclidean CVRP. A polynomial-time $(2+\epsilon)$-approximation for this problem follows from the PTAS for Euclidean TSP and the tour-partitioning technique for CVRP [Haimovich, Kan Math. OR'85]. This was the best known until a recent improvement of the approximation factor to slightly below 2 [Friggstad, Grandoni, Mousavi SODA'26]. There have been a series of papers presenting improved QPTASs by Das and Mathieu [SODA'10] (time $n^{\log^{O(1/\epsilon)}n}$), Jayaprakash and Salavatipour [SODA'22] (time $n^{O_{\epsilon}(\log^6 n)}$), and recently Sitters [ArXiV'25] (time $n^{O_{\epsilon}(\log\log n)}$). In this paper, we solve the mentioned long-standing open problem by presenting a PTAS for Euclidean CVRP.

papers.title: Witnessing Magic (and other Quantum Resources)
Match and Correct: A Repeated Computational Motif in Evoformer Layers
papers.abstract: Triangle attention and triangle multiplicative updates form key components of the Evoformer, and were introduced specifically to encourage consistency with the triangle inequality. Yet whether representational changes over layers reduce triangle inequality violations has not been tested. We probe the pair representation at each of OpenFold's 48 Evoformer layers, decoding final C$_\alpha$-C$_\alpha$ distances with four probe families (a shared linear probe, per-protein linear probes, a sequence-separation-gated linear probe, and XGBoost) and reconstructing intermediate 3D structures from the decoded distances via multidimensional scaling. Across a cohort of 552 CAMEO and ECOD proteins, distance decodability ($R^2$) and reconstruction quality (TM-score) rise in early layers, plateau in the middle of the network, and rise again in late layers. Directly measuring triangle-inequality violations in the decoded distances reveals a similar, more exaggerated pattern: violations rise to a peak, fall to a trough, rise to a second peak, and only then decline, revealing two distinct episodes of decreasing normalized triangle violations rather than one continuous improvement. Cumulative forward and reverse layer-wise ablations of the Pair Transition, MSA Transition, and triangle mechanisms localize the regions in which specific Evoformer components become essential. The two stages of geometric refinement coincide with the use of the Pair Transition MLP and the triangle mechanisms. These results characterize how distance information and decoded geometric consistency evolve across layers, and motivate hypotheses about the computations behind their trajectories.

papers.title: Comets in Kepler background photometry: the ion tail and tail disconnection of C/2009 K5 (McNaught) and an analysis of comets crossing the Kepler field
papers.abstract: Kepler recorded several thousand dedicated sky-background pixels per detector output every 29.4 min from 2009 to 2013, an archive that we use to study comets. During 2010 April 14-21 a narrow band of excess light swept across the field at 1.46 deg/day. This feature is the ion tail of comet C/2009 K5 (McNaught), whose head passed just beyond the edge of the detector array. We trace the tail from 0.9 deg to ~13 deg from the nucleus at surface brightnesses of 26.7-30 mag/arcsec^2; its aberration implies a solar-wind speed of ~500-750 km/s. At 30-min cadence we follow a tail-disconnection event on 2010 April 17-19 whose timing and geometry are consistent with a flank encounter with a coronal mass ejection, although other triggers cannot be excluded. We then analyze all 21 known comets with perihelion distance q < 15 AU whose heads crossed the detectors, using photometry at the predicted head positions calibrated against displaced control tracks. Eight comets are detected, including C/2010 J4 (WISE) a few days before its discovery and two comets at 6.3-7.4 AU with one-sided streaks that we interpret as dust tails. The undetected comets give 3-sigma limits of typically Kp > 16.6-18.1 within 5 arcmin of the head. A blind shift-and-stack search for moving diffuse sources, roughly 50% complete at Kp ~ 15.5-16 for rates of 0.3-1 deg/day, recovers four known comets and finds no unknown ones. Animations show the K5 tail and comets C/2011 L3 and C/2010 J4 crossing the field.

papers.title: Beyond global density in a stochastic sandpile: the role of spatial signatures in the predictability of extremes
papers.abstract: In self-organized critical systems the global load is a strong precursor of extreme events. In the two-dimensional Manna sandpile, grain density alone predicts extreme avalanches with an AUC of about 0.96. We ask whether density fully determines the system's readiness for an extreme event, that is, whether microstates with the same number of grains are equivalent. Because density is such a strong predictor, a method that sees the full microstate can score well just by counting grains. We therefore compare only states with an identical number of grains. Even then, both a parameter-free statistic and a convolutional network distinguish states that precede an extreme avalanche from typical ones, while shuffled controls do not. The signal is a load contrast between the center and the dissipative boundaries, carried by the two lowest symmetric cosine modes. Their normalized energy is a single variable that needs no training. Together with density it recovers most of the gain that a network trained on the full microstate achieves over density alone. Readiness for an extreme avalanche therefore depends both on the total load and on how that load is distributed relative to the boundaries.

papers.title: MemoryLane: Supporting Reminiscence Conversations Between Older Adults with Mild Dementia and Lay Caregivers Using a Simulated AI Agent
papers.abstract: Reminiscence Therapy (RT) is a non-pharmacological intervention that invites patients to discuss and review past life experiences and memories to improve their emotional and mental well-being. In practice, many reminiscence conversations are led by lay caregivers, such as spouses and adult children. While traditional RT often relies on personal photographs, curating them can be tedious and difficult. In addition, caregivers who lack shared life experiences with the patient may struggle to facilitate engaging reminiscence conversations. This paper presents MemoryLane, an AI-integrated tool that helps lay caregivers facilitate reminiscence conversations without curated photographs. MemoryLane supports a triadic conversation among the patient, the caregiver, and a simulated AI agent that acts as the patient's peer. A shared interface shows the agent and AI-generated images of the memories being discussed, while a private smartphone interface lets the caregiver control the behavior of the simulated AI agent and moderate the AI-generated images. A preliminary focus group study with five dementia-care stakeholders suggested the value of MemoryLane's AI agent as a peer companion and of AI-generated images, as well as the feasibility of having caregivers moderate images and control the AI agent.

papers.title: Nonlinear spin generation and spin photocurrent as a symmetry and magnetic domain probe in unconventional magnets
papers.abstract: Unconventional magnets host momentum-dependent spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling. We demonstrate that the combination of nonlinear spin polarisation and spin photocurrent is a powerful diagnostic tool for probing the spin space group symmetry, magnetic domain, and quantum geometry in unconventional magnets, providing information beyond their equilibrium spin texture. We develop a mechanism-resolved joint symmetry analysis of second-order spin photoresponse tensors and analyse their frequency dependence, magnetic parity and relaxation scaling. We show that unconventional magnets are natural platforms to achieve large magnetic-even spin photocurrent induced by unpolarised light, making them promising candidates for polariser-free spin sources. We present numerical illustrations for prototypical hybrid parity and odd parity magnet models. Our work provides optical fingerprints connecting spin-space symmetry to distinct microscopic pathways of spin accumulation and transport.

papers.title: Taking Band-Limited Maximum Likelihood to High Dimensions: Linear Memory, the Parametric Rate, and a Self-Tuning Cut-off
papers.abstract: Band-limited maximum likelihood (BLML) estimates a density as the square of a band-limited function. The estimate is non-negative, and when the square root of the true density is band-limited its error falls at the parametric rate $n^{-1}$. Its algorithm bins the data, which is fast only in one or two dimensions: from three on every point has its own bin, the kernel system is dense, and memory grows as $n^2$, 40 GB at $10^5$ points. Whether the rate survives in higher dimension, where kernel estimators slow down, had not been tested. We study dense data, densities that fill their space, not data near a low-dimensional manifold. We show that the binned equations are the stationarity condition of a strictly convex objective and minimise it by block coordinate descent without forming the kernel matrix: memory is linear in $n$, a sweep costs $O(n^2 d)$ and a fit takes about ten, and one A100 GPU fits $10^6$ points in eight dimensions in about ten minutes. On band-limited truths the error then decays as $n^{-1}$ in every dimension we tested, up to eight, while the slopes of kernel estimators flatten from -0.67 to -0.28, and it is 2 to 18 times lower than a neural spline flow's. A streaming fit learns the cut-off, BLML's only tuning parameter, from analytic gradients of the held-out likelihood, for about the cost of one more fit. On real data BLML is the strongest nonparametric estimator we tested: it leads kernel and nearest-neighbour estimators on electricity prices by 0.27 to 0.47 nats per hour, and a tuned kernel estimator on the full POWER and GAS benchmarks by 0.39 and 1.58 nats per point, placing it between early and recent normalizing flows. It loses on densities with a kink.

papers.title: Equivariant intersection cohomology of some $4$-dimensional locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds
Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers: Global Rule Isolation and Deterministic Sampling Manifold Compression
papers.abstract: We present Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers (RoSeDiT), a new diffusion transformer architecture that isolates the global rule from the image tokens. RoSeViT showed in visual reasoning that a vanilla ViT spreads a shared rule over all $L$ tokens at an entropy of order $Ld$, whereas an enforced controller route reduces it to order $d$. In class-conditional DiT and SiT, the class and the noise level are explicitly conditioned by adaLN, so a RoSeViT-style controller channel on the ViT side is insufficient to establish the full role separation. By introducing the adaLN listening mechanism, which makes adaLN compute under the controller's command, RoSeDiT brings the entropy theorem and role separation into the latent diffusion domain. Under the same SiT training and evaluation protocol at the same level of parameter count, RoSeDiT surpasses SiT at all four model scales at 400K steps, and RoSeDiT-L/2 even surpasses SiT-XL/2's 17.2 FID with 15.34 and 32% fewer parameters. RoSeDiT-XL/2 surpasses SiT-XL/2's 7M-step FID of 8.3 at 1.4M steps with 7.98, using one-fifth as many training steps. We further observe that models with the same denoising loss can have a large FID gap, which indicates a misalignment between the denoising objective and the image manifold. We formalize this phenomenon into Deterministic Sampling Manifold Compression (DSMC), a two-stage training schedule with which RoSeDiT-XL/2 surpasses SiT + REPA's 4M-step FID of 5.9 at 2.4M steps with 5.84.

papers.title: Providing Accuracy Guarantees for the Fixed-Point Emulation of Matrix Multiplication
papers.abstract: Fixed-point methods such as Ozaki-II emulate double-precision matrix multiplication (GEMM) on fast low-precision hardware. Software that chooses the mantissa bit count automatically is numerically safe when the emulated product keeps the error guarantee of the floating-point GEMM it replaces. We analyze the worst-case and average-case error of fixed-point and floating-point dot products, define exponent span capacities that determine the extra mantissa bits an input requires, and approximate them with a low-precision GEMM. We prove that 53 bits plus such a capacity and a small constant preserve the classical worst-case error bound for a floating-point dot product, and we demonstrate this guarantee in software on several test cases. In a developer build of cuBLAS on an NVIDIA B200, each implemented bit-count rule earns grade~A on Test~2c of ``Grading the BLAS'' at every size and exponent range tested, falling back to double precision at the widest ranges; in exact arithmetic, the bound holds on every adversarial and random input tested.

papers.title: On p-adic modularity of abelian threefolds with imaginary multiplication and rational p-isogeny
Cosmography with gravitational waves II: Padé approximants in an extended redshift regime
papers.abstract: We evaluate the capability of next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, including LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and DECIGO, to probe cosmographic parameters using electromagnetically bright standard sirens. Adopting Padé approximants, we extend the cosmographic analysis to substantially higher redshifts and constrain the parameters $H_0$, $q_0$, $j_0$, $s_0$, and $l_0$. We examine the constraints primarily as a function of the number of detections and, in a complementary analysis, across correlated SNR--redshift regimes. LISA provides percent-level constraints on $H_0$, while the Einstein Telescope and DECIGO reach subpercent precision as the catalogue size increases. The parameter $q_0$ can be constrained at the tens-of-percent level, whereas the higher-order parameters $j_0$, $s_0$, and $l_0$ remain progressively less determined. Compared with the low-redshift Taylor analysis, the Padé approach extends the usable redshift range, increases the accessible event population and enables a higher-order reconstruction of the expansion history.

papers.title: AdaMenu: Query-Adaptive Menus for Decision Models over Large Label Spaces
papers.abstract: Decision models such as Jev return probabilities over caller-defined options and are increasingly used for classification. Large label spaces challenge both accuracy and scalability: larger menus can impair decisions, increase input costs, and exceed option limits. Hierarchical classification reduces menu size but introduces serial calls and error propagation. We propose AdaMenu, which builds a compact candidate menu from retrieved labeled examples and makes a single decision-model request. Its candidate labels adapt to the query, and its default setting also adjusts menu size using aggregated retrieval scores. We evaluate AdaMenu with open and closed decision models on four label sets containing up to 1,016 labels. It outperforms TypeSafe's beam-search baseline on all 16 model and label-set pairs where both methods run, improving accuracy by 16.6-34.3 percentage points. Relative to the full menu on the three smaller label sets, accuracy differences range from -0.5 to +7.2 percentage points, while input token usage falls by factors of 3.2-22.9. AdaMenu also runs when option limits exclude the full menu, including settings where the hierarchical baseline is unavailable.

papers.title: Tunable Multi-Frequency-Band Generator and Detector of AC Signals Based on a Spin Hall Device with Two Antiferromagnetic Layers
papers.abstract: Antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin Hall oscillators offer an electrical route to compact terahertz sources, while AFM spin Hall diodes can be used as a promising detectors of terahertz signals, however, their attainable frequency and the redout efficiency are constrained by the dynamics of a single AFM layer. We theoretically and numerically investigate a spin Hall multilayer junction Pt/AFM/Pt/AFM/Pt comprising two canted AFM layers, driven by independent drive DC currents flowing in the outer platinum (Pt) layers. Using a model based on the coupled Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equations for four AFM sublattices and a phase-dependent two-interface spin Hall magnetoresistance model, we show that the device manifests itself as a DC current-driven oscillating spin Hall magnetoresistance. When an additional DC (AC) signal current is applied to the junction, the device generates an output AC (DC) voltage. Our model predicts current-driven, locked, co- and counter-rotational states of the net magnetization at Neel-vector frequencies in the top and bottom AFM layers, respectively. These states result in a multi-frequency response of the spin Hall magnetoresistance at the sum and difference frequencies. The counter-rotation regime additionally activates the phase-sensitive mixing contribution, producing a fourth harmonic. In contrast, the co-rotation regime provides a difference-frequency channel on the order of 100 GHz, although mutual locking prevents this output from being tuned continuously toward zero. Our estimations show that the device matched to an external load can generate output AC power of 1.2 nW at the second harmonic and 0.8 pW at the fourth harmonic, and can produce a DC voltage of about 1 mV for a 6 mA input signal current.

papers.title: Regularity of Solutions to Non-Local Equations on Homogeneous Groups
Quantum Coloring Games on Complete Graphs
Gravitational and Maxwell--Proca-Type Structures in a Variational Metric-Affine Framework
Lie Group Structure of Six Degree-of-Freedom Rigid-Body Uncertainty Representation and Propagation
papers.abstract: For six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body motion, the choice of Lie-group structure affects both how well the group-theoretic mean and covariance represent the state distribution and how accurately these moments are propagated. A quaternion-based, left-trivialized semidirect-product formulation of the velocity phase space is developed for the actuated body-frame dynamics, with closed-form group operations and Jacobians that avoid matrix-group embeddings. We derive the controlled stochastic dynamics and establish that the direct- and semidirect-product formulations describe the same physical process under the specified noise model. Since the semidirect exponential coordinates account for frame changes between body twists at different poses, they capture pose--twist coupling more naturally. A lunar powered-descent experiment assesses low-order moment representations of uncertainty and propagation performance under the proposed group structure using two distinct algorithms. Compared with direct-product formulations and a linearized baseline, the proposed structure improves the representation of the banana-shaped body-velocity distribution using group-theoretic moments, yields more consistent propagated moments, and produces distribution approximations that agree more closely with the Monte Carlo reference. In this experiment, changing the group structure accounts for most of the observed improvement, highlighting the practical value of the proposed semidirect-product formulation.

papers.title: Agent-ZTA: A chain-Aware Zero Trust Model for Bidirectional Security-State Propagation and Runtime Containment in Multi-Agent Delegation
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly delegate tasks and permissions across chains of autonomous agents that invoke protected tools. Although agent identities and delegated credentials may remain valid throughout a workflow, the security condition of any agent along the chain can deteriorate during runtime execution-either through upstream compromise or downstream ingestion of untrusted inputs. Authorization models based solely on the immediate caller and its static delegated scope fail to account for these mid-execution state changes. This paper develops Agent-ZTA, a chain-aware Zero Trust authorization and containment model that links runtime security-state changes across multi-agent delegation graphs. The model distinguishes an agent's path-specific delegated authority bound from the effective permissions currently exercisable under trusted policy. It defines an architecture featuring independently enforced policy decisions, authenticated delegation provenance, a dynamic chain-state view, and explicit fail-safe handling of missing or stale authorization signals. Furthermore, Agent-ZTA defines bidirectional security state propagation, allowing downstream security events to affect relevant upstream workflow states, and specifies adaptive branch-scoped containment through restricted permissions and a sandbox ("jail") execution mode where an isolation boundary is available. The deterministic decision procedure, five stated security properties, and worked authorization traces show how accepted security-state changes constrain affected operations while preserving original delegation bounds and separating unrelated workflow branches under the defined policies. Finally, the paper states its trust assumptions and the exact scope of its security properties.

papers.title: Model Maps: A Documentation Framework for Tracing Foundation Model Ancestry and Understanding AI Entanglement
papers.abstract: The development of foundation models incorporates pre-existing AI artifacts like models, datasets, and benchmarks. These relationships, as part of the broader AI supply chain, produce "entangled" webs in which properties of artifacts upstream can influence the outputs of a foundation model downstream - a phenomenon known as AI entanglement. Without visibility into these connections, a black-box model can inherit upstream properties that result in security vulnerabilities, hallucinations, or biased predictions, yet developers are left with no recourse to identify or mitigate the root issue. To address these concerns, we introduce model maps as a conceptual documentation framework for tracing model ancestry that builds on previous documentation frameworks like ecosystem graphs, datasheets, and model cards. A model map for a given foundation model is a detailed knowledge graph that represents the relationships between artifacts that influence the resulting foundation model. Our framework incorporates a taxonomy of 13 dependency mechanisms including model fine-tuning and synthetic data generation. We apply this framework to construct model maps of 15 closed and open-weight foundation models to illustrate the complexity of AI entanglement in current model development practices. From our model maps, we record 2,778 unique dependencies and trace artifacts that are located up to 9 hops away from a resulting foundation model. Our findings suggest that AI transparency requirements should extend beyond individual models and training-data disclosures to encompass upstream dependencies, which would enable more effective risk assessment, auditing, and accountability across the AI supply chain. To help developers, regulators, and researchers understand and analyze the interactions that can influence the behavior of a foundation model, we release these these model maps at this https URL .

papers.title: Cosmic ray muon seasonal variations with the ProtoDUNE-SP Detector
papers.abstract: We present the measurement of the cosmic ray muon seasonal variation using single-muon events with the ProtoDUNE single-phase detector located at the CERN Neutrino Platform, using data collected from December 2018 to July 2020. Cosmic ray muon runs recorded during this period are analyzed to determine the muon rate as a function of time. The results show a seasonal modulation of the muon rate, with a significance of 4 {\sigma} relative to the null hypothesis of no seasonal variation. The observed muon rate reaches a maximum during the winter, consistent with measurements from other surface experiments with a low muon-energy threshold. This measurement is possible due to the overall excellent performance of this detector technology and serves as a clear demonstration that such a detector can stably measure small, time-dependent physical signals such as seasonal variations in cosmic muon rates over long timescales.

papers.title: Revealing the Biases of Large Language Models By Inferring Prior Distributions
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been known to exhibit a wide range of social biases including name-nationality associations, occupation-gender associations and racial stereotypes. Existing approaches to evaluating these biases typically involve measuring surface-level behavior where a model is fed a dataset of prompts and its outputs are scored relative to ground-truth answers. Inspired by prior elicitation in cognitive science, we propose a different perspective that reconstructs latent bias as a prior underlying the model's behavior. We formulate the problem as a Bayesian inverse problem where, given prompt-response observations on a bias benchmark dataset, we infer a low-dimensional latent distribution that summarizes the model's stereotyping tendencies. This paper develops the mathematical foundation, a practical reconstruction algorithm, and experiments using the Bias Benchmark for QA (BBQ) benchmark to infer the prior distributions of LLMs over responses in ambiguous social contexts.

papers.title: NEMESIS2.0: LLM-Aided Netlist-Driven Performance Equation Modeling for Accelerated Analog Circuit Sizing
papers.abstract: This work presents NEMESIS2.0, an open-source LLM-aided framework that automatically derives equation-based performance models for analog circuits. The resulting equations provide fast, accurate surrogates for SPICE evaluation. To validate the method, equation-based models are developed for seven circuit test cases in a commercial 65nm CMOS technology, covering 15 metrics on five operational transconductance amplifier topologies, and six metrics on two dynamic comparator topologies. When tested on 1000 unseen variants of these seven designs, each corresponding to a different set of independently sampled transistor sizes, the accuracy is found to be within 5% of SPICE. To demonstrate use cases for NEMESIS2.0, the generated models are used as performance evaluators in multiple transistor sizers based on different population-based stochastic search optimizers. For each of the seven test cases, transistor sizing is performed for 100 different sets of performance specifications, with final SPICE simulation confirming that 83.3% of the resulting designs meet all specifications after a single sizing run. The rest fail to meet the specifications due to discrepancies between the model and SPICE, and require iterative resizing under tightened specifications; all such scenarios meet specifications within five iterations. Within the transistor sizers, this equation-based performance analysis evaluates ~400 design candidates per second, versus 0.14 candidates per second for SPICE-based evaluation, achieving 196-238x sizing runtime speedup, including final SPICE verification.

papers.title: Large language models as oncology world models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can synthesize cancer patient cases, but their internal representation of oncology, or world model, has not been explored systematically. By only specifying tumor type, we show that LLMs tend to generate similar patients per cancer, with on average 81.0% to 93.2% of a cancer's patients sharing the most frequent value of each baseline feature. By systematically varying patient features in 12 clinical scenarios, we show that they follow biomarker and treatment logic in 29 of 36 model-scenario assessments, against 1 of 12 when previous treatment or frailty matters. Continuing real patient trajectories, an LLM predicted 89.9% 12-month survival, and 79.2% with similar patients as examples, against 72.2% observed. To represent these trajectories, we developed the Clinical State Space, a dynamic representation framework that we also applied to real patients. Despite the limits we show, improved world models may support digital twins, which our framework can evaluate.

papers.title: Zero area of quartic Fibonacci Julia sets
NeRI: Neural Residual Iteration for Elliptic Operator Equations and Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a so-called {\it Neural Residual Iteration} (NeRI), a weak-form neural-network framework for solving a class of elliptic operator equations and variational inequalities, including nonlinear and nonsymmetric problems that may not admit a global energy functional. The key idea is to construct, at each iteration, a state-dependent linear functional whose derivative with respect to the trial function recovers the current weak residual. A single gradient step is then performed on the residual, yielding a residual-driven neural update without requiring a global energy functional or an additional test network. From a function-space perspective, NeRI can be interpreted as a neural-tangent-kernel-preconditioned realization of classical residual iterations, thereby bridging classical iterative solvers and neural-network optimization. We further extend NeRI to elliptic variational inequalities (VIs) through penalized and constraint-preserving formulations. For wide two-layer networks under gradient flow, we prove finite-time lazy-training estimates and derive an $H^1$-error decomposition relative to the exact weak solution. Numerical experiments on several elliptic problems demonstrate the effectiveness of NeRI, particularly for nonsymmetric and low-regularity problems.

papers.title: Nondoubling Calderón-Zygmund theory across geometries
Universal Statistics of Random Waves in Multi-Port non-Hermitian Scattering Systems
papers.abstract: We study the statistical properties of wave transport of a fixed multi-port non-Hermitian scattering system through wavefront shaping to explore all possible coherent illumination conditions. This is a departure from traditional approaches utilizing cavity shaping to create an ensemble of systems with different detailed scattering arrangements that lead to uncorrelated field configurations. Using microwave measurements in the low channel-number limit, we empirically demonstrate universal statistics in the probability density functions (PDF) of reflectivity, transmissivity, and absorptivity, Fisher information and the difference between forward propagating and time reversed transmissivity. Because the PDFs depend only on the number of input channels and the eigenvalues of Hermitian operators, we demonstrate how cavity shaping can be used to manipulate these eigenvalues, even creating Diabolic Point degeneracies, giving us direct control over the shapes and bounds of transport phenomena PDFs. We further investigate the PDFs when the excitations are finite bandwidth pulses as opposed to monochromatic waves, and determine the behavior in the limits of two channels and many channels. Our results establish a new paradigm in statistical investigations and cavity shaping applications by focusing on outcomes arising from all possible excitations, rather than creating conditions for one specific wavefront that optimally achieves a desired purpose.

papers.title: Rank Functions of Flag Matroids with Applications to Order-Neutral Submodular Valuations
papers.abstract: We provide a rank function axiomatization for flag matroids and show that it is cryptomorphic to the definition of flag matroids as a sequence of matroid quotients. Afterwards, we present some applications of flag matroid rank functions by providing solutions to selected problems. In particular, we discuss connections between flag matroids and submodular valuations in computational economics by showing that rank functions of flag matroids of length $k$ are precisely the same as $\{0, 1, \dots, k\}$-order-neutral submodular valuations. We then prove that $v:2^E\to \mathbb{R}$ is an order-neutral submodular valuation if and only if $v$ can be written as $v(X) = b|X| + \sum_{i=1}^l c_ir_{N_i}(X), \quad b \in \mathbb{R}, c_i > 0$, where $N_{i+1}$ is a quotient of $N_i$. Doing so allows us to prove that every order-neutral submodular valuation is a gross-substitute valuation and that not every order-neutral submodular valuation is a Rado valuation. Furthermore, we prove that if $|E|\geq 3$, then a set $A$ is a Sidon set if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are order-neutral, if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are gross-substitute valuations.

papers.title: Level Set Method; partial regularity in ${\mathbf R}^3$
PREFACE: Separating Shared Corrections from Prefix Conditioning in PEFT
papers.abstract: Does input-conditioned parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) improve because it uses the current input, or because it adds a useful learned correction? We investigate this distinction with PREFACE, a bounded channel controller for PEFT-adapted projections that requires no test-time gradients. The controller reads observed context; in multiple-choice likelihood scoring, its state is independent of the candidate continuation. Our central study freezes IA3, tuned LoRA, and DoRA adapters and matches controller architecture, initialization, batches, and updates across current-prefix and learned-global controls. Across ARC-Challenge and SciQ, current-prefix control improves all six mean accuracies over frozen adapters, but none of its paired contrasts with learned-global control excludes zero. Replacing its corrections with their training-prefix mean changes accuracy by at most 0.34 percentage points; input-varying corrections contribute only 1.8-2.8% of correction RMS. On ARC test, frozen-adapter current/global controls score 25.68%/25.77%, distinct from the earlier jointly trained 23.1% to 26.4% gain over IA3. We derive and evaluate static compilation of fixed corrections, separating deployment simplification from statistical equivalence. Broader GPT-2, Pythia, and Qwen experiments show family-, task-, and scoring-dependent gains, with modest recent-model effects. The study provides an intervention-based evaluation of conditional PEFT: improvements over a static adapter do not by themselves demonstrate a benefit from input matching.

papers.title: AGI: Agility Index for Power Systems Dynamic Performance, Inspired by Reynolds Number
papers.abstract: Multiple established metrics and indices exist to quantify the dynamic performance of power systems. With the growth of inverter based resources, these mostly conventional metrics and indices may not encompass all important elements and variables that hold information about the grid performance, especially the damping properties. This paper proposes the Agility Index (AGI), which is a Reynolds number-inspired metric for power system dynamics relating the ratio of inertia to damping. With the current trends towards high-power inverter assets and reduced-inertia grids, explicit attention is necessary in monitoring inertia and damping together. This paper shares insights the AGI presents about the dynamic performance of power systems.

papers.title: High-Resolution DKIST/ViSP Observation Reveals Small-scale Photospheric Magnetic Flux beneath a Coronal Hole Region
papers.abstract: The magnetic unipolarity of photospheric regions beneath coronal holes is well established at spatial resolutions of about 1 arcsecond, but the effect of smaller-scale magnetic structures remains uncertain. We compare co-aligned observations from the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) aboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory and the Visible Spectro-Polarimeter (ViSP) at the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST). HMI observes the Fe I 6173 Å line, while ViSP observes the Fe I 6302.5 Å line; both form at similar photospheric heights. We derive the line-of-sight magnetic field (B_LOS) from ViSP spectropolarimetric data using a Milne-Eddington inversion and compare it with the HMI field derived from vector magnetograms over a common coronal-hole region. ViSP detects smaller magnetic structures with stronger fields than HMI. The absolute mean field and mean absolute field are higher by factors of 1.30 and 1.37, respectively. HMI measures approximately 28% less unsigned magnetic flux and 24% less net signed magnetic flux than ViSP. A comparison of spatially degraded ViSP data with HMI indicates that differences in effective resolution and associated spatial averaging contribute to these discrepancies. Nevertheless, the magnetic flux imbalance remains similar: 69% for HMI and 65% for ViSP. Thus, the additional small-scale flux detected by ViSP does not substantially change the measured unipolarity in this region. Because ViSP has a limited field of view, observations covering entire coronal holes are needed to test whether this result holds more generally.

papers.title: 3D Radiative Transfer Simulations for Characterization of the Optically Thick DART Ejecta Plume
papers.abstract: The Hyperion package is a three-dimensional Monte-Carlo radiative transfer approach to modeling dust ejecta. Because it has proven to be a powerful tool for simulating optically thick environments with complicated structure, we are applying the routines to observations of the DART impact on asteroid Dimorphos. Our analysis focuses on the LICIACube LUKE red-filter image acquired 175 s after impact, when the near-surface plume remained dense and not strongly structured. The model incorporates the updated Dimorphos shape model, spacecraft and solar geometry derived, and size-dependent scattering properties of realistic dust particles. We adopt an axisymmetric conical ejecta geometry and iteratively adjust the particle size distribution (PSD) and vertical number density profile to reproduce observed brightness profiles extracted from the LUKE image. We find that a power-law PSD with slope k = 3.0 and a number density peak located at approximately 120 m above the surface best reproduces the brightness contrast between the illuminated surface, the bright ejecta plume, and the adjacent dark band produced by shadowing within the optically thick material. The resulting best-fit model implies a total ejecta mass of 1.25 x 10^6 kg within 500 m of the impact site.

papers.title: Who Shows Up, Who Benefits, and Who Wins? Expert-Novice Disparities in Team-Seeking Forums and Competition Performance on Kaggle
papers.abstract: Team formation is the first social gate to collaboration in online communities, yet it remains unclear whether public team-formation mechanisms broaden access to collaborators or reproduce existing hierarchies. We examine this question on Kaggle, a data science competition platform whose "Looking for a Team" (L4T) megathreads let participants publicly seek teammates for on-platform competitions. Grounded in Communities of Practice theory, we conduct two complementary studies of 18 competitions held in 2023. Study 1 analyzes the reply network among 671 megathread participants and finds that 89.3% are low-tier users, yet higher-tier users receive significantly more replies (Kruskal-Wallis H=16.46, p=.00246) and achieve higher rates of forum-visible teaming success (52.9% vs. 32.6%; chi-squared=10.53, p=.001), a proxy for eventual team membership. Linking megathread posters to verified team rosters from 16 competitions partially supports this proxy. Twenty-six final teams contained two or more megathread posters, indicating that megathread interaction sometimes, but not always, maps onto realized teaming. Study 2 links participation traces from 219 users to private leaderboard outcomes and finds that productive participation (submission count rho=.435, cross-competition participation rho=.247) is positively associated with performance, whereas megathread-specific discussion is not (rho=-.021). The submission-performance association appears stronger in higher tiers, although the novice subgroup estimate is imprecise. Together, the findings suggest that open access to team-seeking forums does not guarantee equal participation. Visible expertise shapes who attracts attention, and engagement in the community's core practice is more strongly linked to success than discussion alone. We discuss implications for designing more equitable team formation in online collaboration environments.

papers.title: Robot Demonstration Videos Should Include Transparency Disclosures
papers.abstract: This paper argues that the robotics and AI community should adopt disclosure standards for demonstration videos. As physical and financial constraints limit direct public access to embodied AI, public dissemination of progress in robotics is mainly through curated demonstration videos rather than direct experience with the technology. In a large-scale (N=9,341), pre-registered experiment across six countries, we find that the general public struggles to discern both the visual authenticity (e.g., distinguishing real footage from CGI) and behavioral authenticity (e.g., distinguishing autonomy from teleoperation) of robot demonstration videos. The omission of these details distorts public perception, leading people to overestimate the ability of robots to perform tasks and navigate real world environments. Using evidence from behavioral science, we design a disclosure intervention and demonstrate that the inclusion of clear disclosures in robot demonstration videos significantly improves discernment of visual and behavioral authenticity, as well as understanding robots' capabilities. We propose the adoption of disclosure standards for robot demonstration videos to accurately calibrate public expectations and promote transparency in robotics research.

papers.title: GPBam: A Retrieval-Aware German Public Law Exam Benchmark
papers.abstract: Legal reasoning in civil-law systems is not rule-lookup: the German state examination asks for a structured opinion (Gutachten) that names the governing norms, applies them to the facts, and argues to a conclusion. We introduce GPBam (German Public Law Bar-style Exam), 81 public-law examination cases with reference solutions, paired with a recitation task over 200 statutory provisions. Drawn from state examination preparation, the cases are broad and rarely repeat, and are not publicly available - we find no evidence of exact-solution memorisation in the models we evaluate, and keeping them private limits contamination. Because each reference solution's cited norms form a retrieval gold set over the very instances the essays are graded on, GPBam scores retrieval and long-form generation jointly, which makes it a benchmark for legal retrieval as well as for legal writing and lets us ask how much retrieval quality a legal opinion actually needs. Across 32 open-weight and proprietary models evaluated without retrieval, scores span 4.81-76.42 out of 100. Supplying the law helps modestly: across seven models and eight retrieval configurations, retrieval performance varies nearly threefold and buys at most 4.1 essay points, and nothing significant for three of the seven, while an oracle with 91% gold-norm recall improves scores by 2-6 points. Essay quality strongly tracks prior knowledge: verbatim statute recall, measured in a separate task, correlates at $\rho = 0.92$ over 32 models.

papers.title: Gradients of Turbulent Fluctuations as New Tracers of Astrophysical Magnetic Fields
papers.abstract: Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence is ubiquitous in astrophysical plasmas and produces scale-dependent anisotropy with respect to the local magnetic field. Because turbulence cascades preferentially perpendicular to the field, its spatial gradients acquire preferred orientations that can be used to probe magnetic-field structure. This property underlies a family of gradient techniques based on spectroscopic, synchrotron-intensity, and synchrotron-polarization observations. In this review, we summarize the theoretical foundation of these techniques, including the anisotropy of MHD turbulence and the corresponding behavior of velocity, magnetic-field, and density fluctuations. We then describe how these fluctuations are encoded in spectroscopic data and synchrotron observables, and review the implementation of Velocity Centroid Gradients, Velocity Channel Gradients, Intensity Gradients, Synchrotron Intensity Gradients, and Synchrotron Polarization Gradients. We also discuss the effects of isotropic fast modes, shocks, self-gravity, stellar outflows, thermal broadening, and self-absorption. Finally, we review applications to the diffuse interstellar medium, star-forming regions, the Galactic center, external galaxies, and galaxy clusters.

papers.title: Probing Where Surprise Happens: Localized Violation-of-Expectation Evaluation of Video World Models
papers.abstract: Violation-of-expectation (VOE) benchmarks evaluate intuitive physics in video world models by testing whether physically impossible events produce greater prediction errors than matched possible events. However, conventional VOE evaluations aggregate prediction errors across space and time, making it unclear whether successful discrimination reflects model's understanding of physical violations at the locations and time where they occur. To address this limitation, we introduce localized VOE evaluation, a framework that measures prediction error differences between possible and impossible events within spatial regions and temporal intervals associated with physical violations. We compare global, temporally localized, and spatiotemporally localized evaluations of V-JEPA models pretrained on developmental egocentric videos or large-scale natural video datasets. Our results reveal that global and localized judgments can diverge in both directions: global aggregation can either obscure correct localized discrimination or produce apparent discrimination without corresponding localized evidence. During continued pretraining on developmental egocentric videos, agreement between global and localized judgments changes non-monotonically, while confidence in localized judgments increases despite modest improvements in accuracy. Together, these findings establish localized VOE evaluation as a complementary diagnostic for assessing intuitive physics in video world models and demonstrate that global prediction errors do not necessarily reflect the spatiotemporal evidence of physical violations.

papers.title: Bayesian Learning of Uncertain Linear System Behaviours
papers.abstract: We present a Bayesian approach to learning uncertain behavioural representations of linear dynamical systems from noisy input-output data. In behavioural systems theory, the finite-horizon behaviour of a linear system is represented by a subspace. We quantify uncertainty in this subspace through probability distributions on the Grassmann manifold. This leads to a geometric formulation of Bayesian inference over the Grassmannian. We derive the posterior distribution under Gaussian measurement noise and discuss how uncertainty in the inferred behaviour can be propagated to trajectory predictions, with a view towards data-driven control.

papers.title: Relational Semantics and Completeness for Onto-Epistemic Logic
TMA: Sim-to-Real Forceful Humanoid Manipulation via Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation
papers.abstract: Recent humanoid loco-manipulation in articulated environments has largely focused on geometry-dominant interactions, where success is primarily determined by geometric alignment and motion execution. In contrast, forceful multi-finger manipulation requires the robot to adapt to real-world uncertainties in contact and interaction dynamics. We present Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation (TMA) and an integrated whole-body system for zero-shot sim-to-real forceful humanoid manipulation, and study round-doorknob opening as a challenging benchmark requiring stable multi-finger frictional grasping, sufficient torque generation without slip, force-regulated pushing, and whole-body stability. TMA structures policy learning around interactions observable through tactile feedback, uses cone geometry as an inductive bias for multi-finger contact representation, and adapts motor behavior online from tactile history. An upper-body manipulation policy is trained alongside a pretrained general locomotion controller to coordinate dexterous interaction and whole-body stabilization. Trained entirely in simulation, TMA transfers zero-shot to a Unitree G1 humanoid with BrainCo Revo2 multi-fingered hands and substantially outperforms standard Rapid Motor Adaptation (RMA) and reactive tactile policy baselines across four commercial round doorknobs in the real world.

papers.title: Hidden Momenta due to Magneto-Electric Coupling in Non-Reciprocal Media
papers.abstract: From a canonical quantisation approach of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics, we derive the interaction Hamiltonian due to a dipole emitter interacting with a time-symmetry-broken topological insulator (TSB-TI), described by an axionic coupling Lagrangian. This provides an additional interaction term dependent on the magneto-electric coupling strength inherent to the TSB-TI which will modify measurements on related observables. The spontaneous decay rate is calculated in the Born-Markov approximation for a general electromagnetic Green's tensor, and then specifically for the case of a planar parallel-plate cavity.

papers.title: Bilateral Log-Linear Attention
papers.abstract: Sequence models represent past context at different resolutions, using token-level keys and values, fixed-size recurrent states, or hierarchies of compressed summaries. Full attention supports strong associative recall but requires quadratic work during training and prefill and a linearly growing key-value cache during inference. Linear attention and state-space models reduce these costs through fixed-size recurrent memory, but this compression can limit recall. Log-linear attention offers a middle ground by maintaining logarithmically many state matrices. However, its hierarchy favors finer resolution near the current query while compressing earlier context into coarser summaries. To complement this allocation of resolution, we introduce bilateral log-linear attention, which pairs the existing hierarchy with a second hierarchy anchored at the sequence origin. By combining their reads, the two branches provide finer access to both early and recent context while remaining causal. We derive recurrent and chunkwise parallel formulations for the added branch, preserving log-linear training and prefill work, logarithmic decoding work per token, and logarithmic persistent state storage at fixed feature dimensions and chunk size. In multi-query associative recall, this design raises mean overall test accuracy from 76.37% to 96.12% over forward log-linear attention across multiple training seeds. For pretrained language models under approximate parameter matching, it raises the mean score on six selected RULER needle-in-a-haystack tasks from 26.97% to 50.03% at a context length of 6144 tokens. In the same setting, bilateral attention also outperforms forward log-linear attention on seven of eight downstream retrieval tasks, including question answering and information extraction.

papers.title: On stretched Kostka polynomials
NVFP4-MLA: Unified FP4 KV-Cache Storage and Attention Computation for Multi-Head Latent Attention
papers.abstract: Long-context reasoning and agentic workloads make key-value (KV) cache capacity and attention computation the dominant costs of serving frontier large language models. We present NVFP4-MLA, the first design to push both KV-cache storage and attention computation of multi-head latent attention (MLA) to FP4. NVFP4-MLA co-designs the quantization algorithm with the attention kernel and the cache system. Selective residual compensation preserves model accuracy by adding NVFP4 residuals only to the quantization-sensitive channels. Two-dimensional quantization blocks make the shared latent cache compatible with the different reduction directions of the two attention batched matrix multiplications (BMMs), removing requantization between them. On DeepSeek-R1 and Kimi-K3, NVFP4-MLA matches BF16 MLA average accuracy across nine benchmarks while compressing the MLA KV cache by 3.20x and 3.05x relative to BF16 MLA. On NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, NVFP4-MLA speeds up the attention kernel over FP8 MLA by up to 2.82x on DeepSeek-R1 and 2.71x on Kimi-K3, and lowers p90 time to first token in agentic multi-turn serving by up to 3.5x and 2.1x, respectively. In disaggregated DeepSeek-R1 serving, it also raises per-GPU throughput by up to 2.30x.

papers.title: Three Invisible Failure Modes in Speech-Based Age Estimation for Child Safety
papers.abstract: Child safety in AI depends on the accurate identification of minor users. Young children tend to talk rather than type when interacting with AI, so in practice this identification requires predicting age from speech. We evaluated whether three audio-capable large language models can predict a child's age from their speech across five studies using two speech corpora of children under the age of 13. Models classified children as over 13 on 2.5% to 42.5% of audio responses, and every model that answered placed some 5- to 11-year-olds over 18. While measuring these rates, we uncovered three distinct failure modes. A client library silently double-encoded speech samples, leading one model to classify children aged 5 to 10 years old as being in their thirties and forties with hallucinated explanations. A second model's endpoint was replaced by a successor that refused nearly every age-related question and never produced an age. Every model sometimes placed the same speech sample under 13 and over 18 years of age, but a third model went further, giving threshold answers that contradicted its own numeric estimates. None of these failure modes produced a warning, a status code, or a change in output format, so they would all pass standard monitoring. These results demonstrate why child-safety claims about age assurance should be evaluated at the level of the pipeline rather than the model. We describe the reporting practices that would make such failures detectable.

papers.title: A Distributionally Robust Framework for Safe and Generalizable Utilization of Surrogate Markers
papers.abstract: Surrogate endpoints can accelerate treatment evaluation, but their validity is challenging to establish because the joint distribution of counterfactual outcome surrogate pairs is not identifiable. We propose a distributionally robust framework for safe and generalizable surrogate evaluation that explicitly accounts for this uncertainty. By treating cross arm dependence as partially identified, we formulate a maximin optimization problem that learns an optimal surrogate transformation by maximizing the worst case explained variance of individual treatment effects over admissible counterfactual dependence structures. The resulting robust surrogacy measure provides a conservative lower bound on explained treatment effect variation. Moreover, our maximin construction guarantees nonnegative alignment between the treatment effects on the transformed surrogate and the primary outcome over the admissible counterfactual couplings. To generalize surrogacy evaluation across populations under covariate shift, we integrate transfer learning with debiased machine learning to estimate the required target population moments using source trial data and target baseline covariates. The computational tractability and asymptotic properties of our method are established. Simulations demonstrate good finite sample performance and show that the proposed method guards against counterfactual misalignment by shrinking the learned transformation toward zero, revealing a robustness prediction tradeoff. We illustrate the framework by evaluating 18 month glomerular filtration rate change as a surrogate for two year change using multiple randomized clinical trial data sets.

papers.title: Intrinsic memory limits resonant control of complex cardiac spiral waves
papers.abstract: Resonant forcing is known to induce controlled drift of phase-locked spiral waves in excitable media. Here, we show that intrinsic memory fundamentally alters this paradigm in complex meandering spirals typical of cardiac tissue, where phase-dependent responses to successive perturbations over the meander cycle interfere destructively to produce metastable quasi-stationarity or constructively to induce stable confinement. These dynamical insights motivate an improved low-energy multi-pulse feedback protocol that robustly drives spiral waves to termination through sustained directed drift.

papers.title: Beam-pattern Prediction for Radio Antenna Arrays using Mutual Coupling and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Radio antennas are often used to form arrays, such as phased arrays and interferometer arrays. For most applications the beam patterns of these instruments must be accurately known. For phased arrays the array patterns are formed by coherently adding the embedded element patterns (EEPs) of the individual antennas in the array. For interferometers, the fundamental measurement is of visibilities, which depend on the products of pairs of EEPs. Unfortunately, in either case, for closely-spaced arrays, the EEPs can be distorted by mutual coupling between the antennas and can be very different from the isolated element patterns (IEPs), measured when the antennas are far apart. Mutual coupling is characterized by the scattering parameters for the array. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations can simulate the EEPs, including mutual coupling effects, but these simulations can be computationally expensive and require accurate knowledge of the design of the array elements, their placement, and the environment in which they are deployed. Directly measuring either the EEPs or the array patterns for instruments in the field is often impractical as well. In this paper we show that in cases where the scattering parameters between array elements can be measured, they can be used to infer the array patterns of a phased array. We demonstrate the training of a deep neural network to simulate array patterns when given: the design of the antennas, the locations of the antennas, the frequency of operation, and measurements of the scattering parameters of the array. As a demonstration for a simple model, we apply this approach to the simulation of the array patterns for a small phased array of three dipole antennas and evaluate the sensitivity of this procedure to uncertainties in measurements of the antenna positions and scattering parameters.

papers.title: On boundaries of boundary value problems: The cases of Regularity and Neumann problems
Decompositions of the diagonal of complete intersections in products of projective spaces
Contextual Non-Convex Bandit Optimization with Two-Point Feedback
papers.abstract: We study a non-stochastic contextual bandit problem with Lipschitz losses. At every round, the learner observes the context then picks two actions, observes the difference between their losses, and incurs their mean. The aim is to minimize the regret against a generic non-parametric comparator class of policies mapping contexts to actions; for example, Lipschitz policies and Hölder-smooth policies. We show how relying on a hierarchical discretization technique allows us to improve upon the regret rates achievable under one-point feedback, and even recover the full-information rate in some cases; notably, for sufficiently smooth policy classes or low-dimensional instances. Additionally, for Lipschitz policies, we present an algorithm whose per-round computational complexity is only logarithmic in the time horizon.

papers.title: Context Matters: Improving LLM-Based Code Summarization with Hierarchical Information
papers.abstract: Source code documentation plays an important role in software quality activities, such as code review, program comprehension, maintenance, and bug fixing. However, it is often fragmented across individual code elements and focuses on local implementation details, providing little information about their surrounding context. This limits both developers' understanding of software systems and the effectiveness of Large Language Models (LLMs), whose reasoning is constrained by finite context windows. Enriching documentation with hierarchical context has the potential to improve software comprehension and support downstream, quality-related tasks for both developers and LLM-based tools. In this paper, we present an in silico study that showcases the impact of augmenting context on the generation of code-level documentation, using a variety of LLMs. By varying the function, class, and module hierarchy visible to the LLMs, we assess whether this variation produces a significant difference in the resulting code documentation compared with the existing documentation, which serves as a proxy for developer intent. Our results show that Documentation-Aware prompts with class or module-level context consistently yield summaries that are closest to the original documentation. Adding surrounding documentation yields statistically significant improvements over the baseline across models, with effect sizes ranging from negligible (DeepSeek) through weak (GPT-4o-mini) to medium (Gemini). We restrict the study to this immediate hierarchical context; call-graph traversal and cross-module dependency context fall outside our scope and are left to future work. These findings provide a clear path to improve automated documentation tools and enhance LLMs' ability to reason about codebases for downstream tasks, such as code retrieval.

papers.title: SpecRelay: Amortize or Avoid the Round Trip in Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Edge-cloud speculative decoding moves autoregressive drafting to an edge device while a larger cloud model verifies draft tokens in parallel, so that edge drafting and cloud verification overlap under a synchronous draft-verify schedule. Beyond low-latency local networks, however, the next verification request of that schedule can be sent only after the previous reply arrives, so every round still waits out a full round trip, and throughput falls as the network RTT grows. To recover this loss, we present SpecRelay, an edge-cloud LLM inference system that addresses this cost at two levels: it amortizes round trips when cloud verification is necessary and avoids them when local reasoning suffices. For cloud-bound queries, an asynchronous verification pipeline keeps fixed-budget draft trees in flight while earlier replies are still outstanding, and the cloud rejects stale requests before the target-model forward pass (the asynchronous schedule). At the query level, an RTT-conditioned router (the Latency-Aware Router) estimates quality and completion latency for three on-device modes (direct generation, Chain-of-Draft, and full reasoning) and cloud speculative decoding, selecting among them under a configurable accuracy-latency objective without adding latency during inference, since the router runs concurrently with the draft-model prefill. The asynchronous schedule alone improves decoding throughput by up to 50% over a reproduced synchronous baseline across multiple benchmarks. At matched target-model accuracy and 250 ms of added round-trip latency, the full system with the router delivers 1.95x and 1.55x the throughput of the same baseline on SPROUT and OlympiadBench, respectively, while sending only 47% and 39% of the queries to the cloud.

papers.title: Leafwise thermalization near vacuum for the inhomogeneous Landau equation with very soft and Coulomb potentials
Accelerating Atomistic-Continuum Simulations of Multilayer 2D Materials with Functional Principal Component Analysis-Based Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Atomistic-continuum simulations of complex wrinkling deformations in large-area multilayer two-dimensional (2D) materials are computationally expensive. To accelerate these simulations, this work presents a machine-learning (ML) framework that first constructs a low-dimensional representation of the deformation field, then learns the deformation in this reduced space. Dimensionality reduction of deformed 2D membranes is challenging because of the extremely high dimensionality of discretized deformation fields, the need to preserve surface continuity and prescribed geometric constraints, the stochastic nature of wrinkling patterns, and the limited availability of training data. We address these challenges using two-dimensional functional principal component analysis (FPCA). The proposed FPCA representation reduces deformation fields containing millions of degrees of freedom to latent spaces with only tens of dimensions while preserving the continuity of the deformed surface. In addition, prescribed homogeneous boundary constraints are satisfied exactly through an appropriate choice of basis functions in the FPCA representation. A neural network is then trained to predict the principal components from the system and loading parameters. The resulting ML-predicted deformation fields are used as high-quality initial configurations for the atomistic-continuum solver, which subsequently performs energy minimization to obtain equilibrium solutions. The framework is demonstrated for multilayer graphene subjected to uniaxial compression, biaxial compression, and combined biaxial compression and simple shear. For the most computationally intensive large-strain cases, the proposed approach achieves speedups of at least 6.8 times while converging to final energies comparable to, and in some cases lower than, those obtained using conventional atomistic-continuum initialization.

papers.title: Weighted $H^p$--$L^q$ estimates for fractional operators with multiple kernels under a strengthened Hörmander condition
Rigidity for Families of Abelian Varieties over $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$
Dual-Stage Channel-Posterior Integration for MLM-Aided Token Communications
papers.abstract: Token transmission over conventional digital modulation is vulnerable to channel impairments, leading to bit errors that cause received tokens to become contextually inconsistent. This paper proposes a receiver-side dual-stage channel-posterior integration framework for masked language model (MLM)-aided token reconstruction. In the proposed framework, the receiver detects unreliable token positions from channel reliability and constructs a vocabulary-level channel-posterior. In particular, within the receiver, Posterior-Weighted Input Embedding (PWE) injects this posterior into the MLM input, while Adaptive Output Logit Fusion (AOF) reuses it at the output with a channel-adaptive weight. Consequently, multiple unreliable tokens can be reconstructed in a single bidirectional MLM inference without retransmission, transmitter-side encoding, or additional MLM training. Experiments over noisy channels show up to a $67.2$\% improvement in cosine similarity over context-only MLM reconstruction, with consistent gains across different MLM architectures and existing language-model-aided methods.

papers.title: Community Odour Reports as a Forecastable Sensor of Fugitive Emissions
papers.abstract: Ambient air quality monitors (AAQMs) measure exposure to emissions from waste facilities at few points; for most residents the only record is their own odour reports, used by regulators as evidence of impact but not typically as measurements of exposure. Calibrated public reports are accepted measurements in seismology, but whether community odour reports can serve as a sensor of exposure, and be forecast, is untested against independent monitors. Here we show they can, at a UK landfill, with SENTINEL, which combines the public weather forecast, run through a dispersion model, with the reports already received and no instrument at the site. Judged against the independent monitors, monthly report frequency was correlated with hydrogen sulphide (r = 0.92) and daily reports remained associated with it beyond weather; they fell fourteenfold after a change at the source while modelled transport did not; and, with no gas data as input, gave exposure in both monitored postcodes within a factor of three of that measured. SENTINEL forecast daily report counts with skill 0.64 one day and 0.50 four days ahead, exceeding damped persistence four days ahead; the one-day gain over persistence was unresolved. Community odour reports can act as a relative sensor complementing sparse monitoring; a monitor is needed for absolute scale.

papers.title: Supercharging Olmo-core for Efficient and Scalable MoE Training
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models add parameters without proportionally increasing per-token compute. However, training cost also depends on bytes moved, memory held, and kernels launched, and many of those costs follow total parameter size rather than active compute. On infrastructure built for dense models, this mismatch is costly: in early baselines, throughput fell as stored expert parameter size grew, even though the useful work per token stayed nearly fixed. To close this gap, we present a redesigned training stack in Olmo-core, built for efficient, scalable MoE training. We replace the Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) of earlier Olmo-core versions with an architecture built on Distributed Data Parallel (DDP), and add Expert Parallelism (EP), Pipeline Parallelism (PP), a distributed optimizer, and activation recompute. We propose NVSHMEM-based rowwise EP, which writes each token directly into its expert's buffer, avoiding dispatch and combine permutation overhead. We make EP fully synchronization-free by keeping routing metadata on the GPU and using device-scheduled grouped GEMMs. Closely integrated MXFP8 cuts compute, activation-memory, and transport costs, and topology-agnostic checkpoints let the parallel layout change between runs. On NVL8 B300 nodes, the stack supports training configurations from 12.9 billion to 1.2 trillion total parameters on up to 512 GPUs, reaching 858 useful-model TFLOP/s/GPU at 1.2 trillion with MXFP8 and per-layer recompute; an experimental capacity test with the optional DeepEP v2 backend reaches 2.38 trillion. We also explain each design choice and share findings for other training systems; for example, we identify a failure pattern we call Token Gerrymandering, in which the MoE router can learn to hack the load-balancing loss, and find that overlapping communication with computation can slow the overlapped kernels by more than it hides.

papers.title: Certifying quantum generative models beyond the Fisher trace
On the extension of meromorphic mappings and correspondences with finite volume
Reflective Spin Wave Filtering Limiters with Bandpass to Bandstop Bifurcation
papers.abstract: Spin wave (SW) filters using thin-film yttrium iron garnet are an attractive technology for reconfigurable and software defined radio (SDR) systems in which parameters such as channel frequency or transmit power are adjusted in real time to efficiently utilize constrained spectrum resources. Operating in congested electromagnetic environments leave communication systems vulnerable to damage or disruption from strong interference and jamming. Therefore, frequency tunable filters and power limiters are needed to support SDR operation on the physical layer. Here, we report a frequency tunable bandpass filtering limiter which reflects excess above threshold power using a network of nonlinear SW resonators in a ladder filter topology. The reported devices show insertion losses as low as 3.29 dB, isolation above 14.22 dB, center frequency tuning over more than two octaves from 4.75 GHz to 21.08 GHz, fast transient response of 14.01 ns, and low transient spike leakage. A physics-informed nonlinear SW model is discussed and a method to simulate and design networks of nonlinear resonators is introduced.

papers.title: From Language-Specific to Cross-DSL: Semantic-Role-Guided Model Completion with LLMs
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of large language models (LLMs), trained on vast and diverse corpora, has positioned them as a promising source of domain knowledge to assist modelers. However, leveraging LLMs for model completion remains challenging: suggestions must respect both the syntax of a domain-specific language (DSL) and the intended domain semantics, while remaining consistent with an evolving model. This paper presents RAFiC, an LLM-based approach for iterative domain model completion that generalizes across DSLs. It drives completion using metamodel information to ensure syntactic validity and enriches prompts with semantic-role annotations to better capture the intended modeling role of DSL elements. The approach provides context-aware, incremental guidance during model construction. We evaluate RAFiC through an ablation-based comparative study over three DSLs and two scenarios per DSL to isolate the contribution of syntactic and semantic guidance. Across these six scenarios, semantic role guidance improves contribution rate in every case, and RAFiC improves completion effectiveness over weaker prompting configurations in most of them. The largest gains occur for DSLs that are less represented in LLM training data. In these cases, iterative guidance leads to earlier and more stable accepted suggestions, while semantic role guidance improves their relevance.

papers.title: Coordinating Distributed AI Servers with Industrial Loads to Reduce Grid-Interconnection Needs
papers.abstract: We show that co-locating distributed AI servers with industrial demand and coordinating AI workloads with production loads can substantially reduce the additional grid interconnection that AI computing requires. Grid interconnection is increasingly constraining the expansion of large AI data centers. Factories already have grid connections sized for their peak production loads, and we propose hosting AI servers during production valleys. We formulate a joint optimization that sizes CPU and GPU servers, schedules deadline-constrained tasks, and routes tasks among factories, and use it to compare three factory-site architectures with new large data centers serving the same demand. Applying this framework to 31 Chinese manufacturing industries, we find that AI demand and production loads often do not peak together. As a result, AI servers placed at factories and scheduled according to production peaks need about 60% less additional interconnection capacity than new large data centers, and 98% less when tasks are routed among a group's factories.

papers.title: Adiabatic Electronic Momentum and the Continuity Equation with Nonlocal Effective Core Potentials in an Electronic Phase-Space Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: Adiabatic electronic momentum and current density provide fundamental information about electronic motion induced by nuclear motion under the Born-Oppenheimer separation. In practical electronic structure calculations, core electrons in heavy atoms are commonly replaced by effective core potentials (ECPs), whose nonlocal components introduce additional contributions to electronic momentum and the continuity equation. Here, using a phase-space electronic Hamiltonian approach, we investigate these nonlocal components on adiabatic electronic momentum and the continuity equation in small molecules with moving nuclei. We demonstrate that this approach efficiently describes adiabatic electronic momentum and the divergence of electronic current density when the nonlocal contributions to the corresponding electronic operators are properly accounted for. We find that the nonlocal correction to electronic momentum is important when the ECP-centered atoms move but is small otherwise, reflecting the spatial locality of the electronic response and ECP. We further examine the implications of moving ECPs, which account for the motion of nonlocal pseudopotentials with the nuclei to restore Galilean covariance, for adiabatic electronic transport. We show that, for nondegenerate systems with time-reversal symmetry, moving ECPs do not modify the coordinate space adiabatic evolution of time-reversal even observables through second order in nuclear velocity, although they can alter the electronic momentum operator and its feedback on nuclear dynamics.

papers.title: Effects of Conventional, Adaptive, and AI-Powered Upscaling on the Legibility of License Plates
papers.abstract: Small details in digital images -- a face, a street sign, a license plate -- are routinely upscaled in hopes of making them interpretable. Upscaling options now range from conventional interpolation, whose operations are spatially invariant and fully explainable, to AI-powered methods that synthesize detail potentially absent from the source. Here, we ask which of these techniques most reliably helps human readers. In two online experiments, we measured legibility of 255 US license plates ranging in resolution from 128 to 8 pixels tall, as well as their legibility after upscaling by eight different methods. Legibility of the un-upscaled plates collapsed from ceiling to floor across a narrow band of plate heights (32 to 10 pixels). Conventional upscaling techniques (bilinear, bicubic, and Lanczos interpolation) gave modest gains of about 5-9 percentage points within this range. Nearest-neighbor interpolation, however, was harmful, rendering unreadable many plates that were readable without any upscaling.
