Paired bootstrap analysis exposes metric disagreement on 4-bit quantization; guided by WMT24 human meta-evaluation, we use MetricX24-XXL as primary and CometKiwi-XXL as a cross-check. Removing the unused vision stack and non-task vocabulary and using int8 weights or fp8 activations causes no resolved loss, whereas int4 leaves a small residual. QLoRA healing overfits its calibration domain. A Cometoid best-of-4 reranker at $T=0.3$ improves both the 8-bit and 4-bit systems under WMT25 test set. On post-submission WMT26, both remain competitive with bf16 under reference-free metrics; the small difference between the reranked variants is treated as noise.

papers.title: Human vs Machine Translation Detection: A Cross-Model, Cross-Domain, and Low-Resource Analysis
papers.abstract: The growing reliance on web-crawled corpora for training large language models introduces a critical challenge: machine-translated (MT) content is often treated as human translation (HT), potentially degrading data quality and propagating synthetic artifacts, especially in low-resource settings. In this work, we study MT-HT detectability across high-resource (English, Spanish) and low-resource (Swahili, Afrikaans) languages using both decoder-only LLMs in zero-shot and few-shot settings, and fine-tuned multilingual encoders trained at the sentence level and on token-chunked inputs. We find that decoder-only models provide limited discrimination overall and exhibit a consistent class-asymmetric failure mode: they recognize human-written text reliably (high HT recall) but rarely flag fluent machine output (low MT recall). Encoder-based classifiers achieve high accuracy when evaluated on data generated by the same MT systems and translators used during training in a legislative domain, but their MT recall drops sharply on unseen translators and on unseen domains such as low-resource conversational text and medical content. To address this limitation, we evaluate models on longer inputs by chunking text into segments of up to 300 tokens, which substantially improves generalization, suggesting that sentence-level signals are insufficient for robust detection. Finally, we analyze the relationship between translation quality and detectability using COMET and BLEURT, showing that lower-quality MT is more easily identified, while high-quality MT remains difficult to distinguish from HT. Our results highlight the importance of input granularity, translator generalization, and translation quality in building robust MT detection systems across domains and languages.

papers.title: Read, Route, Patch: Robust Test-Time Evolution for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents can improve long- horizon interactive decision-making through test-time evolu- tion, yet existing methods face three information bottlenecks: memory retrieval overemphasizes textual similarity, candi- date harnesses are often behaviorally redundant, and whole- harness rewriting may overwrite useful evidence or introduce cross-component inconsistency. We introduce Trident, which improves experience utilization, behavioral exploration, and harness evolution through boundary-aware memory reading, diversity-aware candidate routing, and order-aware insertion- based updating, respectively. We evaluate Trident on five benchmarks spanning text games, web interaction, and cod- ing tasks. Across qwen-32B, mistral-small-3.2-24B, and gpt- oss-20B, Trident achieves the best average performance and consistently outperforms non-learning, memory-based, reflection-based, and automated prompt optimization base- lines. Compared with the strongest baseline, APEX, Trident yields relative average gains of 30.7%, 30.8%, and 38.3% on the three backbones, respectively. Ablation and sensitivity stud- ies further show that the three designs provide complementary gains and remain robust to parameter variations.

papers.title: Powering the Space Elevator
papers.abstract: Powering the Space Elevator is a report on the work of an International Space Elevator Consortium study group tasked with determining the technology options for delivering power to the climbers on the space elevator at any altitude above Earth. The book covers options such as laser power beaming, microwave beaming, a solar-powered climber, and delivering power through the electrical conductivity of the tether. This report starts with the reference conceptual design of a climber from the 2023 study report, "The Climber/Tether Interface of the Space Elevator," and adds features to the climber that allow it to ascend or descend the elevator tether. The strengths and limitations of current technologies are identified, along with areas for future research.

papers.title: "I Am Not a Kiddo!": Quantifying Epistemic Infantilization in Large Language Models via Multi-Metric Bias Analysis
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for tutoring and professional knowledge retrieval, yet safety evaluations still focus mainly on overt harms such as toxicity while overlooking benevolent failure modes. We study epistemic infantilization, defined as an identity-conditioned reduction in technical depth that appears when disability disclosure precedes an expert-level query. To measure this effect, we construct a counterfactual dataset of matched question-answer pairs and compare model responses across three settings: no identity context, disability disclosed in prior conversational context, and disability disclosed via a short query prefix. We introduce two composite metrics, the Infantilization Bias Index (IBI) and the Epistemic Accessibility Response Score (EARS), which capture retention of mathematical and formal content, domain terminology, reasoning coverage, and tone signals such as simplification markers and unsolicited offers to adjust the level. Across five open-weight model families, we find consistent evidence that disability disclosure reduces epistemic access by replacing formal explanations with higher-level summaries, with Physics and Mathematics most affected. Using question-clustered inference that respects the repeated-measures structure of the data, the effect remains reliable after accounting for correlated observations. These findings suggest an inclusion tax, where disabled users must request rigor more explicitly than non-disabled users. We conclude by arguing that accessibility should mean format adaptation rather than content simplification.

papers.title: AI Cannot Review What Humans Catch: A First Look at the Reviews of Agent Instruction Files
papers.abstract: Agents increasingly shape software, and instruction files steer them. Files such as this http URL , this http URL , .cursorrules, and this http URL act as executable policy: prose that a machine reads and acts on. Unlike ordinary documentation, a single edit to one of these files can silently redirect how an agent behaves across an entire repository. Natural-language rules have no per-change oracle, so they slip past the compilers, type-checkers, and test suites that guard code. Review is therefore the only quality gate, but no prior work has studied how that review happens. We analyzed 2,870 instruction-file pull requests across 2,246 repositories. The gate is largely broken: over 70% of instruction-file changes receive no substantive review. When an AI reviewer substitutes for a human, it is structurally blind to the concerns that most need human judgment. It catches surface structure but misses factual errors, necessity questions, and staleness problems. We contribute the first taxonomy of instruction-file review concerns (16 categories), which exposes this sharp human/AI divergence, and a benchmark of 1,962 human-checked concerns across 468 PRs. We ran three widely-used agents (Codex, OpenCode, and Claude Code) against the benchmark, giving each reviewer the full repository at review time. They recovered only 1.3-3.9% of the concerns humans raise. Even the strongest current agents cannot substitute for human attention on these files.

papers.title: Automatic techniques for security bug report identification: A systematic mapping study
papers.abstract: Several studies have investigated the use of automated techniques to help practitioners identify security bug reports early in the defect management process. However, currently there is no comprehensive overview of this research area. Such an overview will help identify future research directions and consolidate the potentially relevant existing solutions. This study aims to provide a comprehensive overview of automated techniques for identifying security bug reports. To achieve this, we conducted a systematic mapping study and identified 28 primary studies. The study's findings show that the literature has evaluated various automatic techniques for identifying security bug reports, including traditional machine learning, deep learning, and more advanced large language models. The two main challenges identified are the lack of labeled data and data imbalance. Furthermore, we observe that existing studies lack evaluations in real industrial settings and rely mostly on archival data from open-source repositories. The most commonly used data sources in these studies include Wicket, Ambari, Camel, and Derby. Overall, the literature appears fragmented, highlighting the need for future work to focus on comprehensive evaluations of the most promising techniques.

papers.title: Model-Driven Approaches for DevOps: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: DevOps integrates tools and methodologies aimed at optimizing software development, building, deployment, and monitoring by automating and reducing the development lifecycle and improving software quality. However, despite its many advantages, it presents notable challenges, particularly in terms of usability and migration. On the other hand, model-driven engineering (MDE) offers a way to abstract from specific technologies and implementation details, which can be leveraged to improve these aspects, as happens in software development. In this paper, we present the first systematic literature review aiming to understand the current MDE approaches for supporting DevOps development. We focus on categorizing the works based on computing domains, the phases of the DevOps process to which they contribute, and the reengineering steps they propose. Our findings highlight a dominant focus on cloud computing, while some studies propose domain-agnostic approaches. We also observe that the deployment and integration phases are the most explored. This reveals research opportunities regarding both the domains and DevOps phases addressed. We also found limited use of text-to-model transformations, while nearly half of the papers employed model-to-model transformations. Text-to-model transformations were more prevalent overall. Most notably, we discovered that no study proposed a complete reengineering process, which represents an exciting avenue for future research.

papers.title: Uncertainty in Cyber-Physical Systems: A Literature Survey
papers.abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) operate in dynamic, dependable environments where sensing, communication, decision-making, control, and assurance are affected by uncertainty. This paper characterizes CPS uncertainty through a literature survey comprising 186 primary studies. We (i) characterize uncertainty types, (ii) identify uncertainty sources, (iii) relate uncertainty to life-cycle phases in which they occur, and (iv) overview the possible uncertain mitigation strategies. The findings show that uncertainty is most often conceptualized as an assurance issue. Safety and specification uncertainty is the most prevalent category, followed by environmental and model/epistemic uncertainty. Domain mapping reveals broad cross-domain engagement, while safety-critical sectors such as autonomous systems, energy systems, and robotics CPSs display domain-specific uncertainty patterns. The life-cycle analysis indicates that uncertainty is not limited to the development or testing phases but also arises during runtime operation, underscoring the need for continuous assurance approaches. Mitigation strategies primarily include runtime monitoring, robust and adaptive control, and probabilistic reasoning. In summary, this survey contributes to a thorough characterization of CPS uncertainty and provides a discussion of articles on this topic.

papers.title: VidEngram: Agentic Long-Term Video Understanding via Structured Hierarchical Memory
papers.abstract: Long-video question answering is wasteful and lossy when a multimodal model must re-encode the same video for every query: context limits force sparse sampling or truncation, and no reusable representation remains for later questions. We present VidEngram, an agentic video QA system that builds a persistent hierarchical memory once at ingest and answers later questions from that memory. VidEngram captions video and audio jointly with Qwen2.5-Omni, consolidates segment memories into episode and entity layers, and uses a text-only agentic planner with specialized retrieval tools to produce grounded answers. The web interface makes this process inspectable: users can watch memory formation, inspect retrieval traces, verify cited evidence in the video player, and explore entity relationships. On the full OmniVideoBench, VidEngram with a GPT-5-mini planner outperforms a strong single-pass Qwen2.5-Omni baseline (37.0% vs. 32.3%), with gains concentrated on longer videos where single-pass coverage becomes sparse. Because perception is paid once, subsequent queries use low-cost text-only planning.

papers.title: Formal Modeling in Software Engineering with LLMs: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: Formal verification provides strong correctness guarantees for software systems but remains hindered by the substantial expertise and manual effort required to construct and maintain formal models. The recent rise of Large Language Models (LLMs) has prompted growing interest in whether their natural language understanding and generation capabilities can be leveraged to automate labor-intensive modeling activities. This paper presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) examining how LLMs have been applied to automate model checking and the generation of formal and semi-formal models within software engineering. The review follows established SLR methodologies and a PICOC-driven search strategy across four major digital libraries. From an initial search of 1,193 articles, 34 peer-reviewed conference, journal, and workshop articles published between 2022 and April 2026 were selected and analyzed using a structured data extraction form. The review identifies six recurring trends in the literature, including the automated generation of formal models for model checking, LLM-assisted downstream formal verification, iterative and repair-based generation pipelines, and the generation of semi-formal UML and SysML artifacts whose underlying techniques are transferable to formal modeling contexts. Across these trends, LLMs are generally found to perform well on syntactic generation and repair tasks but struggle with semantic correctness, motivating widespread use of counterexample-guided repair loops, intermediate representations, and human-in-the-loop validation. Notably, this review finds that the use of LLMs specifically to automate model checking remains a largely unexplored area, with comparatively little research published on this narrower task.

papers.title: Measuring and Optimizing Energy Efficiency in ICT: A Multi-vocal Literature Review on Data Centers, Cloud Computing, and LLM-Driven Code Optimization
papers.abstract: Rapid growth in Information and Communication Technology (ICT) increases electricity use and environmental impact. Addressing this challenge requires a systematic, software-centric view of how energy and related sustainability attributes are measured, reported, and improved. We present a comprehensive Multi-vocal Literature Review (MLR) integrating peer-reviewed and gray literature to map current practice in measuring and optimizing energy use in ICT software, with emphasis on data centers and cloud computing environments (DCCCEs). First, we synthesize how sustainability is measured across ICT by proposing a taxonomy organized along metric domains (power/energy, energy efficiency, environmental impact) and component granularity (from applications, to containers/VMs, and system-of-systems levels). We summarize measurement approaches and the tooling landscape that implements them. Second, we review optimization strategies at the software and system levels, covering dynamic power and resource management, VM/container consolidation, energy-aware software and system design, and cross-layer, system-wide methods relevant to DCCCEs. Third, we examine how large language models (LLMs) are applied to code generation and transformation for resource-efficient software, noting that most studies target code generation (predominantly in Python) and evaluate runtime and memory, with fewer works directly reporting energy. Hardware- and network-level telemetry are treated as data sources for software-level analysis. We identify gaps in vendor-neutral telemetry, consistent measurement and reporting practices, network-level metrics, and unified, cross-layer optimization frameworks, and outline directions for improving reproducibility and comparability. We screened 635 records (2010-2025) and included 181 sources (122 peer-reviewed, 59 gray).

papers.title: A Survey of Image-to-Code Generation for Software Engineering
papers.abstract: A large fraction of software intent is expressed visually before it is implemented. A designer hands a screenshot or a Figma mockup to a front-end engineer, an architect sketches a UML diagram or a flowchart, and a bug report ships with a picture of what went wrong. Turning such visual artifacts directly into executable software has therefore become an active problem at the intersection of computer vision and software engineering. The present survey organizes the literature on image-to-code generation for software engineering, defined as the family of methods whose input contains a visual modality and whose output is software an engineer would otherwise write by hand. We deliberately scope the survey to software-engineering code, namely user-interface and front-end code, code recovered from software diagrams such as UML and flowcharts, program repair and test code driven by visual signals, and general software-code targets, and we exclude adjacent code-generation domains whose home communities lie elsewhere, such as chart plotting scripts, vector-graphics programs, hardware description languages, and robot policies. Rather than cataloguing systems in isolation, we introduce a unified processing pipeline of visual understanding, component recognition, layout reasoning, code planning, code generation, and verification, and organize the survey around its stages. We trace five overlapping eras from rule-based reverse engineering to agentic generation, survey each pipeline stage and each software-engineering task in depth grounded in what individual systems actually do, consolidate the datasets, benchmarks, and metrics, and lay out the open challenges of design-system generalization, long-horizon and interactive generation, cross-framework deployment, accessibility, hallucinated components, and unreliable evaluation.

papers.title: Predictive Test Optimization Without Historical Failure Data
papers.abstract: As software systems grow in size and complexity, their test suites become increasingly expensive to execute, delaying feedback and wasting resources. State-of-the-art predictive test optimization methods use machine learning to select tests relevant to a change, typically trained on historical failures. This depends on failure histories and is susceptible to label noise from flaky tests. We introduce the novel method of co-evolution labeling for predictive test optimization, deriving test relevance from tests and code changing together in the version history. These data are widely available and less noisy. We train and evaluate models with failure and co-evolution labels on three large projects---from industry and open source; each with thousands of tests and more than 1M LOC. Co-evolution labeling nearly matches the failure detection capabilities of failure-based models, with an overall Average Percentage of Faults Detected of 0.88, while being more resistant to label noise and requiring no test result history. Co-evolution labeling offers a practical, immediately deployable path to faster pipelines and reliable predictive test optimization.

papers.title: LoopSkill: Evidence-Bound Lifecycle Control and the Safety-Liveness Tradeoff in Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents can edit repositories and announce completion, but conversational claims do not prove that artifacts, dispatches, state versions, and authority still agree. LoopSkill is an evidence-bound lifecycle control plane with a schema-validated sole writer, durable outbox routing, artifact-bound reports, recovery, independent review, and heartbeat-gated finalization. We evaluate a locally frozen v3.3.12 integration under a common 1,800-second budget on a selected subset of SWE-bench Lite. The original 140-cell plan was administratively truncated after interim outcomes were visible, so the 60-cell analysis is exploratory and nonconfirmatory. Of 58 scored cells, blind artifact success was 7/19 for LoopSkill, 11/19 for implementation plus independent review, and 14/20 for an ordinary coding agent; two cells were apparatus null. Across 18 complete LoopSkill-versus-review pairs, the descriptive risk difference was -0.222 with exact McNemar p=0.125. No scored LoopSkill workflow finalized. The results expose a safety-liveness and fixed-budget cost tradeoff. They do not establish comparative superiority, long-horizon efficacy, or a false-accept rate.

papers.title: Where AI Use Is Normalized, Author Seniority but Not AI Disclosure Biases Code Review
papers.abstract: Code-review tools increasingly display whether an author used AI when preparing pull requests. Recent studies report that AI disclosure makes reviewers rate otherwise identical work as less competent, with the penalty falling hardest on already-marginalized authors. In a within-subjects experiment in an AI-normalized organization, 447 software engineers each reviewed the same four code snippets under an AI-use disclosure embedded in the commit message and author-seniority labels. AI disclosure did not bias perceptions of code effectiveness or author competence, whereas a seniority label significantly biased both. Together, these findings show no detected penalty for disclosed AI use in this setting, while confirming that the author information shown in code review can still bias evaluations.

papers.title: Loop Engineering: Version-Bound, Evidence-Gated Coordination for Production Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents can edit repositories and execute tests, yet production software work extends far beyond code generation. It requires durable task context, scoped authority, version-aware approval, source-independent verification, interruption recovery, and accountable handoffs between humans and automated workers. We present Loop Engineering, a method for operating multiple asynchronous agent loops over shared, auditable repository state without relying on private conversational handoffs. Each loop is specified by six elements: a trigger, a context projection, an authority boundary, a verifier, a stop condition, and a write-back rule. Versioned procedural contracts, called Skills, encode reusable operating policy; a Harness bounds the available action surface and collects evidence; human gates authorize high-consequence transitions against exact artifact versions. We report a design-and-experience study from MewDesign, a revenue-generating commercial AI design product. Five specialized loops cover planning, scoped implementation, review, test release, and reconciliation. A cross-sectional audit contains 50 durable marker records across 26 GitHub work items. Five pull requests reached a version-bound test lock: three proceeded to test releases with runtime evidence from sources distinct from the deployment request, and two stopped before merge. A detailed drift episode shows one observed fail-closed path: a new commit invalidated prior approval and evidence, and the workflow refused to reuse stale continuous-integration results. The study is not a controlled benchmark and does not establish causal productivity or general safety. It provides early evidence of feasibility, traceability, and bounded progression in one production setting.

papers.title: Towards Sustainable Large Language Model Inference: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference is becoming a significant contributor to both operational cost and environmental impact in modern AI deployments. Energy consumption during inference depends on multiple factors across the pipeline, including input and output length, model design, system-level decisions, and hardware characteristics. This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of energy-efficient and sustainable LLM inference. We analyze selected primary studies to identify techniques proposed to reduce energy consumption across different levels of the inference pipeline, including input, model, system, and hardware. We further examine the trade-offs between energy consumption, latency, and accuracy, highlighting inconsistencies in how these relationships are evaluated. In addition, we review the tools, datasets, and metrics used for energy measurement, covering both software-based and hardware-based approaches. This survey provides a comprehensive synthesis of existing literature, offering insights into the effectiveness of different techniques in terms of energy savings and their associated impact on accuracy. It highlights the trade-offs between energy efficiency and performance and identifies limitations in current evaluation practices. Overall, this work aims to support future research toward more efficient and environmentally responsible deployment of LLMs. Our repository of relevant references is maintained on GitHub.

papers.title: Knowledge-Centric Automated Issue Resolution: A Systematic Survey and Taxonomy
papers.abstract: Automated issue resolution is a knowledge-intensive software maintenance task in which LLM-based agents must acquire, represent, use, and update knowledge from repositories, execution environments, historical artifacts, documents, tools, and prior repair processes. This paper presents a systematic survey of 133 studies on automated issue resolution from a knowledge-centric perspective. We introduce a three-layer taxonomy that organizes issue-resolution knowledge into the Background Knowledge Layer, the Repository Knowledge Layer, and the Procedural Knowledge Layer, and analyze the knowledge lifecycle along six dimensions: knowledge types, sources and extraction methods, representation formats, usage methods, workflow stages, and temporal evolution. Our analysis shows that current systems primarily rely on Existing Code Knowledge and Development Tool Knowledge, while Repository Evolution Knowledge and Experiential Knowledge are increasingly adopted, indicating a shift toward history-informed, feedback-aware, and experience-oriented issue resolution. In contrast, Design Architecture Knowledge and explicitly modeled Background Knowledge remain comparatively underexplored. These findings suggest that future systems should move beyond temporary context construction toward reusable, traceable, and evolvable software knowledge infrastructures that support more controllable, verifiable, and generalizable software engineering agents. The surveyed studies and related resources are maintained at this https URL .

papers.title: Use of Peer Code Review to Identify Potential Security Vulnerabilities in Open Source Software: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: Context: Security vulnerabilities in OSS can have severe consequences. OSS project participants widely use peer code review to improve quality and prevent security flaws. However, despite mandatory reviews, OSS projects still contain vulnerabilities, highlighting the need to evaluate code review effectiveness for security. Objectives: This SLR synthesizes evidence on vulnerability types identified or missed, security practices, tool support, reviewer challenges, and factors that improve detection. Method: Searches of five digital libraries yielded 1,067 studies, of which 20 were included. Vulnerabilities were categorized using the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) framework. Results: Peer code reviews effectively detect localized, well-known vulnerabilities (e.g., buffer overruns, race conditions, crashes, XSS) but often miss subtle, complex, context-dependent issues (e.g., input validation weaknesses, access control weaknesses, resource lifecycle weaknesses). Effective security practices are associated with reviewer expertise, code familiarity, frequent small changes, and organizational support. Security analysis tools, especially Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools, reduce reviewer effort and improve detection but cannot replace human judgment. Reviewers continue to face limitations in security knowledge, experience, time, and understanding of complex systems. Effectiveness improves through security training, domain expertise, contextual familiarity, formalized review processes, and supportive review environments. Conclusion: Peer code review contributes to OSS security but is insufficient on its own. Improving effectiveness requires structured review processes and checklists, security training, organizational incentives, and lightweight automated tool support to help reviewers detect subtle vulnerabilities while reinforcing secure development practices.

papers.title: Software Engineering Practice in the Virtual Reality/Augmented Reality Software Life Cycle: A Systematic Survey
papers.abstract: Leveraging diverse virtual reality (VR) technologies, VR provides users with an immersive experience in a computer-generated 3D virtual environment. In contrast, augmented reality (AR) superimposes virtual objects (such as images, text, animations, etc.) onto users' real scenes. Both VR and AR have received increasing attention due to the maturity of computer graphics, computer vision, and artificial intelligence. VR and AR have gained rapid market growth in both hardware and software. In the early stages, VR/AR-related research mainly focused on hardware (e.g., head-mounted displays and sensor-equipped controllers). Recently, VR/AR software has become a hot topic due to the mature VR/AR ecosystem. However, there is no comprehensive work to summarize software engineering practices in VR/AR. To bridge this gap, this paper aims to provide a systematic survey summarizing the state-of-the-art research on VR/AR from the perspective of software engineering practices. Considering the general VR/AR software life cycle, we categorize the relevant research based on the VR/AR software life cycle, including requirement engineering and planning, software design, software development, software testing, software deployment, software maintenance and updates, and software evaluation and feedback. As for each stage above, we summarize relevant research on VR/AR for this stage, including the design of technical routes, the construction of datasets, and the design of evaluation metrics. We also enumerate existing empirical studies and make comparisons with conventional software (e.g., mobile/desktop application development). In summary, our article can help researchers gain a comprehensive understanding of the achievements of the existing software development techniques in the VR/AR field and also provide insights, which may facilitate the benign development of VR/AR software ecosystem in the future.

papers.title: Mining Architectural Models in the Wild: A Curated Dataset of AADL Models
papers.abstract: Empirical research on software architecture maintenance and evolution is hindered by the scarcity of large-scale, validated, and richly annotated model datasets. Existing benchmarks are limited in scale, provide only model-level annotations, or lack alignment with reference architectures, thereby restricting reproducible studies of architectural reuse, conformance, and AI-driven analysis. To address this gap, we present A3D, a curated dataset of 1,115 Architecture Analysis and Design Language (AADL) models mined from public GitHub repositories and validated with the OSATE tool. The dataset spans 7 generic domains and 52 specific-problem clusters, and provides two annotation layers: (i) domain- and problem-level labels, which capture different model aggregation criteria, and (ii) component-level mappings to three reference architectures, which have been externally validated through a user study. Models are released in AADL and JSON formats with full provenance, a reproducible mining pipeline, and the validation protocol.

papers.title: More Secure Software Development via Cultural Analysis: How could Log4Shell happen?
papers.abstract: There is little progress avoiding vulnerabilities. Cultural analysis may help: For a given team, find the specific cultural values that led to a past vulnerability, then modify the values accordingly for the future. After enough such studies, patterns will likely emerge that are useful for the development community at large.

papers.title: Check Token: Real-Time Self-Verification and Precise Truncation in LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: ECC memory embeds 8 parity bits for every 64 data bits and automatically detects and corrects errors on each read. The parity bits carry no data and only safeguard integrity, at ~12.5% overhead. Yet the reasoning chains of large language models lack such built-in self-verification: once an error occurs it propagates along the chain, and existing methods can only verify externally after generation completes. We propose the check token, establishing built-in self-verification for language model generation streams for the first time: a functional marker <CHECK> is added to the vocabulary, and the model triggers self-checking (analysis, localization, truncation, rewriting) by outputting it at any position. The check token carries no reasoning content (discarded after triggering) and only safeguards reasoning correctness, directly corresponding to the role of ECC parity bits, also at only ~13% overhead. Speculative forking further eliminates false-positive latency, and segmented reward makes trigger timing end-to-end learnable. Experiments (Qwen3-32B / Qwen3-Next) show that the check token achieves +10.8 pp improvement on HMMT25 at 1.13x overhead, with token efficiency 88x that of Best-of-8, and the precise truncation advantage monotonically increases with chain length.

papers.title: The Klein-Gordon equation in projective geometry
papers.abstract: We discuss a geometric method by which Hörmander's result on the asymptotics of a Klein-Gordon field, on an asymptotically flat spacetime, can be related to some partial peeling, à la Penrose, along an extended projective boundary, embedded in a spacetime with one dimension higher.

papers.title: DecompJSCC: Joint Source-Channel Coding With Decoupled SNR and Rate Adaptation
papers.abstract: Deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) for image transmission must adapt to changes in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and available transmission resources. However, some existing joint-adaptive methods condition the encoder on the requested rate, while others apply static masks after encoding. The former couples latent formation to the rate request, whereas the latter cannot adapt channel selection to image content. To address these limitations, we propose DecompJSCC, which decomposes joint adaptation into SNR-conditioned latent formation and post-encoding rate control within a single model. The encoder applies SNR-conditioned block attention residuals across all stages, aggregating intra-stage and cross-stage semantic representations. At the receiver, an adapter performs SNR-conditioned affine correction. We introduce a post-encoding rate-adaptive channel semantic budgeting (RCSB) module whose shared gate selects channels of the formed latent by image content, adjusts their gains, and keeps exactly the requested count. This keeps the encoder output independent of the rate request for a fixed image and SNR. Experimental results show that DecompJSCC outperforms SwinJSCC and SA-RA-JSCC in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) across a range of SNR and rate settings, by 0.64 dB and 1.00 dB over SwinJSCC and by 0.97 dB and 0.96 dB over SA-RA-JSCC on Kodak and CLIC2021, while using only 7.5% of SwinJSCC's Adaptive ModNet parameters.

papers.title: Bäcklund transformations of the fifth Painlevé equation
Zeeman-Doppler imaging of V889 Her: Surface spots and magnetic field topology 2017 - 2023
papers.abstract: The surface magnetic field of the young solar analogue V889 Her is studied using Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI). This well-studied star has previously been reported to have an exceptionally high differential rotation and show abrupt changes in the surface magnetic field and spot configuration. Our aim is to study the evolution of the magnetic field topology in V889 Her. This will contribute to understanding dynamo action in young solar-type stars. We also want to constrain the surface differential rotation curve of the target star. We employ the ZDI method on observations collected with the SOFIN spectropolarimeter mounted at the Nordic Optical Telescope. We test differential rotation parameters previously reported in studies of the star. We observe significant changes in the radial field near the rotational pole throughout the whole span of the observations. Specifically, the polarity of the radial field is reversed around 2021. The large-scale magnetic field also contains a persistent strong azimuthal component at high latitudes. We detect abrupt changes in the spot configuration in June 2018 on the time scale of a week. The observations favour a solar type differential rotation. The different rotation parameters influence the brightness map more than the magnetic field topology. We cannot link the observed changes in the magnetic field topology with the evolution of the long-term spot activity. The abrupt changes observed in 2018 confirm previous reports that the surface magnetic field and spot configuration may undergo rapid evolution on short time scales. This complicates the estimation of the surface differential rotation.

papers.title: Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras
The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
An Incomplete-Preference Quantum Anscombe--Aumann Representation
Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
Hybrid Uncertainty in the Real Forms of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)$
An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
An AI-enabled high-resolution chlorophyll-a forecasting model that outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system
papers.abstract: Surface chlorophyll-a concentration is a key indicator of marine phytoplankton variability, and short-term forecasts of its distribution provide advance information for marine ecosystem monitoring and management. However, interactions between physical transport and biological processes complicate chlorophyll-a forecasting, and simulating these coupled processes with conventional numerical models imposes substantial computational demands. Here we introduce ChlCast, an AI model that generates daily forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a concentration over a 10-day horizon at approximately 4-km resolution between 60$^\circ$S and 60$^\circ$N. ChlCast combines factorized spatiotemporal convolutions with a multiscale architecture to learn from historical chlorophyll-a fields and climatological information. Compared with the operational 0.25$^\circ$ Copernicus global ocean biogeochemical forecasting system, ChlCast reduces mean absolute error and root mean square error by 70.74% and 47.63%, respectively, against satellite-derived Level-4 chlorophyll-a fields, and by 35.03% and 13.07% against independent BGC-Argo in situ observations. Coastal case studies further show that the 4-km forecasts retain coastal gradients and localized concentration maxima that are weakened by coarse-grid averaging. These results demonstrate the potential of observation-driven deep learning for high-resolution forecasting of surface chlorophyll-a variability at the near-global scale.

papers.title: Foundation Tensor Networks Generalize Across Lattice Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: Neural quantum states and tensor networks have emerged as leading techniques for simulating quantum many-body systems. However, disordered systems remain extremely challenging in both frameworks as they require computation of the ground state for every realization of the disorder. Recently, neural quantum states have been used to construct foundation models that generate the ground state directly from the Hamiltonian. Still, they are hindered by the need to perform extensive sampling to estimate observables. To address these difficulties, we introduce the foundation tensor network (FTN), which uses a neural network to generate the tensor network representation of the ground-state wavefunction from the Hamiltonian. To accelerate training, we develop a technique, called \texttt{GridBP}, based on iterated one-dimensional belief propagation that reduces the cost of computing the energy expectation value to just two tensor contractions. We use FTNs to calculate the critical parameters of the glass transition in the quantum Edwards-Anderson model via finite-size scaling analysis. To facilitate rapid averaging, we use a moment-generating function to evaluate the order parameter, lowering the cost to a single tensor contraction. We obtain high-fidelity estimates for the critical parameters by averaging over 500,000 disorder realizations.

papers.title: DART ejecta reveal the recoil momentum budget of a kinetic impact
papers.abstract: Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) demonstrated that ejecta recoil enhances asteroid deflection, but the ejecta processes generating and distributing this recoil remained unclear. We reconstruct three-dimensional ejecta evolution from time-resolved morphology and brightness observations, recovering previously missing constraints on momentum transfer and material transport. Integrating reconstructed momentum yields momentum enhancement factors $\beta_\mathrm{D}=2.13 \pm 0.19 (1{\sigma})$ for Dimorphos and $\beta_\mathrm{sys}=2.04 \pm 0.19 (1{\sigma})$ for the Didymos system. Combined with the measured deflection, the reconstructed recoil constrains Dimorphos's bulk density to $1435.18_{-153.71}^{+112.59} \mathrm{kg m^{-3}}$ without assuming its mass. By linking observed orbital deflection to the released material, this reconstruction provides ejecta-based constraints for assessing kinetic-impact effectiveness and investigating how natural collisions drive mass loss and debris transport among small Solar System bodies.

papers.title: The retarded interaction and non-scattering for 3D Maxwell--Dirac system
Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
QuantumInputOutput.jl: A Julia framework for input-output theory with quantum pulses and the SLH formalism
Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
papers.abstract: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $\Omega(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

papers.title: Microcausality Bounds on Dispersion Laws
papers.abstract: Microcausality holds in any state, including those that spontaneously break Lorentz invariance, and requires the poles (and other singularities) of the retarded Green's function to satisfy $\mathrm{Im}\,\omega \le |\mathrm{Im}\,k|$ throughout the complex plane. Building on the work of Heller, Serantes, Spaliński and Withers, we study its consequences for dispersion relations that are linear at small $k$, like Goldstone bosons, assuming tree-level, non-dissipative dynamics. We show that microcausality is equivalent to requiring that $k \pm \omega(k)$ be typically real functions. This yields two-sided bounds on all higher-order coefficients of $\omega(k)$ in units of its radius of convergence $R$, the scale at which the linear Goldstone description breaks down. The optimal constraints are characterised by an infinite hierarchy of Toeplitz determinants. We derive analogous bounds on $\omega^2(k)$, whose radius of convergence $\tilde R$ marks the scale at which new states must appear. The bounds shrink to zero as the sound speed $c_s$ approaches 1: for a fixed higher-derivative correction, both $R$ and $\tilde R$ become parametrically smaller than naive dimensional analysis suggests. In particular, in the EFT of Inflation all higher-derivative quadratic operators must vanish as $c_s \to 1$. We test the bounds in several models: a $U(1)$ superfluid, light in a dielectric medium, photon propagation in a strong magnetic field, colour-flavour-locked quark matter, and a homogeneous solid. Finally, we extend the bounds to gapped modes.

papers.title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets with Minimum 2
Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
papers.abstract: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a $2+2$ arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector $\qv$ proportional to the charge contrast $\Delta\abaralpha_{AB}$ between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor $\K_{\ULDM}(t)=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of $m_\phi$. The axis of $\qv$ is fixed in advance by the material assignment, so the response obeys the null condition $\K_{\ULDM}(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$ at every instant, for any $\gv_\phi$ including a virialized field with a stochastic gradient---an exact tensor discriminator against gravitational-wave signals; for a single composition $\qv=0$. With the gravitational-wave noise model, the coupling sensitivity for copper and lead test masses reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$ for the baseline instrument and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers. The rank-one factorization and the null condition are summarized in a companion Letter; the present paper gives the derivations and the detector-level analysis.

papers.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
papers.abstract: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. The wavefunction exhibits a strongly coupled core, as well as an asymptotic power-law tail where the D0-branes are well separated. The coefficient of this power-law decay is the three-graviton coupling, previously computed by Herderschee and Maldacena, which our numerical solution reproduces with high accuracy. We also show that this coupling is protected by supersymmetry in the matrix model, and derive its value from the non-renormalized one-loop interaction of the two D0-branes. Lastly, we provide a simple representation-theoretic argument regarding the recently proposed excited bound states of the model.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$α$ Forest at the Field Level
papers.abstract: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly-$\alpha$) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%. Exploiting cosmic-variance cancellation in the field-level approach, we carry out precision measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest bias parameters from the CAMELS simulation suite. We use these measurements to analytically predict the shifts in the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) scaling parameters induced by nonlinearities in the three-dimensional Lyman-alpha forest clustering as a function of cosmological parameters. We find sub-percent shifts in both the radial and transverse directions with a noticeable dependence on cosmology and redshift. Finally, from the field-level fits we construct simulation-based priors that can be used for cosmological analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest with the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). In addition, our cubic model captures the connected four-point function (trispectrum) of the forest, which opens up novel opportunities for accurate covariance matrix estimation for DESI and its successor, DESI-II.

papers.title: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe a superposition of gravitational-wave signals, requiring joint inference of an unknown number of sources, parameters, and instrumental noise. To disentangle these contributions, that overlap in both time and frequency, a Global Fit (GF) analysis is needed. We present samsara++, a C++/CUDA sampler designed to address this trans-dimensional GF problem. Building on the continuous-time MCMC framework of samsara, the algorithm combines birth-death processes for adding and removing sources, with mutation moves for parameter estimation. Birth and death are selected through posterior-dependent rates. Shared-memory parallelism, incremental likelihood updates, and indexed storage reduce the computational and memory costs, while parallel tempering improves the exploration of multimodal posteriors. We assess the performance using simulated one-year LISA datasets containing Galactic double white dwarf binaries and stationary Gaussian instrumental noise. Analyses of populations containing 143 and 866 binaries start from empty source models, without preliminary searches or proposals tailored to the injected population. These tests demonstrate source reconstruction and catalog generation, highlighting, at the same time, the importance of source-count, overlapping signals, and incomplete mixing on joint source and noise inference. Then we perform a separate stress test, initialized at the injected parameters, exploring a population of 16,435 binaries, corresponding to 131,480 source parameters. This run completes 15 million iterations in approximately 16 hours using about 3 GB of RAM. All together, these benchmarks show the computational feasibility of birth-death sampling for large Galactic-binary populations, and provide a foundation for extending samsara++ toward a comprehensive LISA global fit.

papers.title: Gauge aspects of teleparallel gravity and Noether's second theorem
papers.abstract: We examine the gauge structure of the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity (TEGR) from the perspective of Noether's second theorem. We show that diffeomorphisms and local Lorentz transformations are the gauge symmetries of TEGR, as these are the only variational symmetries that give rise to Noether identities. We then discuss the distinct roles of these two symmetries and their implications for the gauge-theoretic interpretation of gravity. Finally, we discuss consequences of these observations for the role of translations in gauge theories of gravity and the coupling of matter in TEGR. In particular, we demonstrate that the matter coupling prescription is uniquely determined and coincides with that of general relativity, including in the case of spinor fields.

papers.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
UV and deep-UV ultrafast harmonic generation enhanced by resonant gold nano-pillar metasurface
papers.abstract: We report experimental observations and full-vector numerical simulations of second and third-harmonic generation from a two-dimensional periodic gold nano-pillar metasurface, for efficient ultrafast light conversion from near-infrared to the UV and deep-UV spectral ranges. The metasurface is designed to support an angle-tunable plasmonic resonance in the near-infrared spectral range, with its resonance wavelength shifting as a function of the pump angle of incidence. Under resonant conditions, strong electromagnetic-field confinement near the nano-pillar corners enhances the nonlinear light-matter interactions. Compared with a flat gold mirror, the nanostructured metal exhibits enhanced nonlinear frequency conversion, with conversion efficiencies of second and third-harmonic generation increased by two and three orders of magnitude, respectively. Full-wave theoretical modeling of linear and nonlinear light-matter interaction in nanoscale structures validates the experimental results. We demonstrate that periodically arranged square gold pillars can be engineered to achieve enhanced second and third-harmonic generation at wavelengths that can be tailored through the structural design, without requiring complex geometries or hybrid structures that pose fabrication challenges. The close agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements further advances our understanding of surface-mediated nonlinear optical processes in metals and highlights the potential of metallic nanostructures as ultrafast light sources in the UV and deep-UV.

papers.title: Temporal Regularized Learning: Self-Supervised Learning Local in Space and Time
papers.abstract: Self-supervised objectives such as VICReg learn representations by making related inputs similar, while variance and covariance penalties prevent collapse. These penalties are statistics over a batch of samples, so layer-local variants, too, are typically local in space but not in time. We introduce Temporal Regularized Learning (TeReL), which optimizes a VICReg-style objective one sample at a time with purely local updates: each update uses only the current activity of its own and the preceding layer and a fixed-size running state. Temporally adjacent inputs serve as positive pairs, which makes the objective a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis (SFA). Running estimates of each neuron's mean and variance, together with one lateral matrix per layer, replace the batch statistics; held fixed during differentiation, they turn the gradient into a Hebbian feedforward update and an anti-Hebbian lateral update. We show that a two-layer network trained with batch size one on an MNIST stream of class-homogeneous chunks reaches 96.48% linear-probe accuracy, above random features (95.09%) and classical SFA, and that the temporal order and each loss term contribute to this result. With both locality constraints relaxed, the same objective matches supervised backpropagation. TeReL thus shows that the collapse-preventing statistics of modern self-supervised learning can be held as running state at each neuron, which brings these objectives closer to what brains and neuromorphic hardware can implement.

papers.title: Real log canonical thresholds and real log canonical thresholds with signs
Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
Numerical tests of chiral fermion weights with $η$-invariant phases in the 3450 model
papers.abstract: We test numerically a recently proposed prescription for coupling continuum chiral fermions to interpolated lattice gauge fields, in which the fermion weight has a Pauli-Villars (PV) regularized magnitude and a phase given by an Atiyah-Patodi-Singer (APS) $\eta$-invariant in one higher dimension. We use the anomaly-free two-dimensional $U(1)$ theory with left-handed charges $3,4$ and right-handed charges $5,0$, whose torus determinant is known exactly. At zero magnetic flux, with gauge fields interpolated from lattice links, the Polyakov loops evaluated on a $16\times16$ grid of flat connections agree with the exact values within $0.04\%$, whereas omitting the APS phase substantially reduces them to about $3\%$ of the exact result. The vacuum-polarization response yields an induced mass $m/e=2.82089$, close to $5/\sqrt{\pi}=2.82095$. At unit flux, where zero modes make the determinant vanish, we calculate a twelve-point correlator on a cylinder with the generalized APS boundary condition. For three smooth backgrounds its magnitude agrees with the exact result within $0.8\%$. Without the $\eta$-invariant its phase deviates by $1.8$-$3.0$ mrad, and with it by $0.2$-$0.5$ mrad. The phase of each charged fermion changes by $15$-$46$ mrad when the gauge field is extended differently into the third dimension, but the change cancels to below $0.2$ mrad in the anomaly-free combination.

papers.title: Uniqueness of addition in Schrödinger algebras
Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space
Boundary Actuation of a Chain Fountain - Physically Admissible Tracking, Stochastic Limits and Zero-Gravity Circulation
Near-Threshold Kink Trapping Enhances Defect Healing in an Adaptive $\boldsymbol{ϕ^4}$ Chain
papers.abstract: We study the scattering of topological kinks in a discrete $\phi^4$ chain with a localized, adaptive defect, motivated by autonomous self-healing mechanisms in fibrous and polymeric chains. The defect represents damaged flanking bonds whose coupling stiffness evolves dynamically via an internal healing variable, driven by the local energy density and moderated by a viscoelastic relaxation rate $\beta$. Using high-resolution numerical simulations, we identify a sharp transition at a critical impact velocity $v_c$ separating kink reflection from transmission ($v_c \simeq 0.4183$ for the benchmark initial defect stiffness $C_{\min} = 0.2$). While subcritical kinks ($v_i < v_c$) bounce back with little energy deposition and supercritical ones ($v_i > v_c$) cross the defect too quickly to induce noticeable recovery, kinks near the threshold ($v_i \simeq v_c$) undergo resonant trapping. This prolonged dwell time transfers substantial vibrational energy into the defect, driving the healing variable to nearly full restoration ($h_{\max} \approx 0.98$). Notably, while $v_c$ and the peak defect energy $E_{d,\max}$ depend strongly on $C_{\min}$ and are largely unaffected by $\beta$, non-zero relaxation ($\beta > 0$) shortens the trapping window and reduces the final recovery efficiency. Our results show that energy-driven self-healing in discrete lattices is controlled by the cumulative dwell time and time-integrated energy excitation rather than the instantaneous impact peak alone.

papers.title: On the Difficulty of Sequence-Level Supervised Learning for Autoregressive Language Models
papers.abstract: During the supervised learning phase, autoregressive language models are typically trained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood of the training data, which decomposes as a sum of token-level cross-entropies via teacher forcing. This objective is simple and efficient but potentially suffers from so-called exposure bias: a mismatch between the way the model is trained and the way it is used at inference time. Can we instead design sequence-level loss functions that incorporate inference-time decoding procedures, such as greedy decoding or autoregressive sampling? We show that two natural attempts lead to loss functions that are fundamentally flawed: unbounded below. We further show that these two flawed loss functions are intimately connected: using autoregressive Gumbel tricks, the sampling based loss is the expected greedy loss under Gumbel perturbations. Since the pathology stems from the dependence of the decoded sequence on the model parameters, we analyze the update direction obtained by applying a stop gradient on the sampling procedure, leading to a moment matching direction. While it is not the gradient of any loss function, we prove that it defines a valid descent direction in function space for the autoregressive negative log-likelihood. Despite these theoretical insights, the moment matching direction suffers from high variance. We conclude that teacher forcing may well be ``all you need'' for supervised learning of autoregressive models.

papers.title: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the $K$-User Gaussian Case
Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case
Dynamics and Statistical Mechanics of Born-Oppenheimer Auxiliary Velocities
papers.abstract: In Born-Oppenheimer (BO) dynamics, auxiliary variables such as electron densities, induced polarization and electrode charges follow stationarity conditions, yet their time derivatives, such as currents, are physical observables. Using Mass-Zero constrained dynamics, we interpret these derivatives as explicit dynamical variables and derive the invariant measure giving their equilibrium statistical properties. We illustrate the framework in constant-potential molecular dynamics, where the electrode-charge velocities reproduce BO current fluctuations and the frequency-dependent admittance.

papers.title: Low-lying doubly charmed strange baryons via QCD sum rules
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the masses of the low-lying doubly heavy baryons and their $B^*(3/2^+)\to B(1/2^+)\gamma$ radiative transitions within QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules (LCSR). By constructing mixed interpolating currents, we obtain $M_{\Xi_{cc}}=3.62^{+0.14}_{-0.15}$ GeV, $M_{\Xi_{cc}^*}=3.72^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ GeV, $M_{\Omega_{cc}}=3.72^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, and $M_{\Omega_{cc}^*}=3.82^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, together with their doubly bottom partners around $10.27$--$10.34$ GeV. The extracted masses are compatible with the observed $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ states and predict hyperfine splittings of about $101^{+27}_{-11}$ MeV and $99^{+11}_{-12}$ MeV for the $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ systems, respectively. Using these inputs, we derive the LCSR for the electromagnetic form factors and obtain radiative widths $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*++}\to\Xi_{cc}^{++}\gamma)=5.25^{+8.57}_{-3.62}$ keV, $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*+}\to\Xi_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.31^{+0.84}_{-0.25}$ keV, and $\Gamma(\Omega_{cc}^{*+}\to\Omega_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.41^{+0.67}_{-0.30}$ keV, while the corresponding doubly bottom widths are at the $0.002$--$0.01$ keV level. We find that the magnetic-dipole contribution dominates, whereas the electric-quadrupole form factor is numerically small. The light- and heavy-quark photon-emission terms can interfere or enhance significantly, and the heavy-quark contribution cannot be neglected in radiative transitions. These results provide useful theoretical guidance for future searches for spin-$3/2$ doubly heavy baryons through radiative decay modes at LHCb, Belle II, and other experimental facilities.

papers.title: TAPES: Terminal Adjoint-Propagated Error Scheduling for Financial Diffusion Samplers
papers.abstract: Financial diffusion samplers are often reused with a small number of function evaluations (NFE) inside scenario and risk pipelines, where numerical time-grid error can distort terminal quantities such as covariances, tails, and drawdown proxies. We study offline grid construction for a frozen probability-flow ODE: the score network, conditioning, Euler solver, report normalization, and deployment NFE remain fixed. TAPES (Terminal Adjoint-Propagated Error Scheduling) estimates signed local defects by Richardson comparisons, transports them through the remaining discrete flow and a terminal-report adjoint, and optimizes the squared norm of their sum before a capped direct refinement. We show that this transported signed sum is the first-order terminal-report error and quantify, under an aligned-defect model, the inefficiency of diagonal criteria. Across six budgets on a regime-switching simulation and chronologically held-out Mag7 contexts, TAPES gives the lowest design- and audit-report errors in all 24 dataset--budget--report rows within the reported five-pipeline panel. Cross-budget mean relative audit-error reductions are about 10--11% on Regime-SV and about 1% on Mag7, with Bonferroni intervals excluding zero; all displayed winners persist under a doubled-resolution reference, and a small Regime-SV Heun probe preserves the TAPES-first audit ordering. TAPES changes only the offline schedule and retains the prescribed deployment NFE; claims concern numerical fidelity to frozen generators.

papers.title: Why "quantum spin liquids" are quantum singlet liquids
papers.abstract: The last couple of decades have seen enormous theoretical and experimental research efforts aimed at finding quantum spin liquids (QSLs) in geometrically frustrated (GF) magnetic materials. Experimental demonstrations of QSLs are challenging due to the indirect character of possible QSL signatures and the presence of impurities in materials, which may destroy or obscure a QSL. At the same time, the theoretical literature often lacks consensus about the ground states of quantum spins on even the simplest GF magnetic lattices. We summarize experimental evidence that in the impurity-free limit, available GF magnetic materials that do not develop magnetic order at low temperatures would form {\it a quantum singlet liquid}, i.e. a disordered state of non-magnetic excitations. We further confirm with theoretical arguments the existence of such a singlet liquid and its gapless character in materials with half-integer spins per primitive magnetic cell. Such a liquid manifests itself in the thermodynamics of GF magnets while having no magnetic features at low temperatures.

papers.title: No Convergence in Learned Eavesdropping-Detection Dynamics for BB84 Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abstract: In prior work we showed that a reinforcement-learning eavesdropper can intercept BB84 quantum key distribution while holding the quantum bit error rate below the abort threshold and keeping a usable distillable key. In this paper we ask whether an equally adaptive learning detector can close this stealth window. We cast the interaction as an alternating best-response game between a tabular eavesdropper and a tabular threshold-adapting detector. We measure exploitability, which is the detection rate and distillable key fraction achieved by a fresh attacker best-responding to the final detector. Across three learning rules (Q-Learning, SARSA, Double Q-Learning), three channel-noise levels, and a uniform false-alarm discipline, the dynamics do not settle out to twenty rounds. The exploitability does not approach a fixed point, and its round-to-round swings do not decay. Two controls, one retraining the attacker against a frozen defender and one retraining the defender against a frozen attacker, show that the swings on each side match the variance of the best-response procedure itself. The dynamics fluctuate at the scale of best-response variance rather than converging, with neither player settling to a fixed response. The behavior is noise-dependent, and the stealth window stays open at the low noise where practical QKD operates. The defender contains the attacker on average at intermediate noise without the contest settling, and at high noise the channel rather than the learned policy suppresses the attack. As a candidate mechanism we examine a last-mover information asymmetry, supported by significant anti-persistence at intermediate noise and consistent with best-response noise at low noise. The results suggest that a learned detector cannot be certified from any single round, and that closing the window calls for breaking the information structure rather than out-adapting the attacker.

papers.title: Polynomial Swap Coboundary Expansion with Applications to LTCs and PCPs
papers.abstract: Swap coboundary expansion, introduced independently by Bafna--Minzer and Dikstein--Dinur, is a local-to-global property that underlies agreement tests in the low-acceptance regime and recent constructions of succinct PCPs. Previous works obtained bounds of $\exp(-O(\sqrt{r}))$ for the $r$-swap coboundary expansion of Chapman--Lubotzky complexes. We establish the first inverse-polynomial bounds for bounded-degree complexes: suitable skeleta of Kac--Moody--Steinberg (KMS) complexes have $r$-swap coboundary expansion at least $r^{-O(1)}$. Our theorem supplies a key ingredient in forthcoming work of Ben Yaacov--Dikstein--Liu, which obtains local tests for sparse algebraic codes with guarantees even at arbitrarily small acceptance probability. These tests use $\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))$ queries and guarantee that any word accepted with probability at least $\varepsilon$ agrees with a codeword on an $\varepsilon^{O(1)}$ fraction of coordinates. Separately, substituting our bound into the existing analysis of Bafna--Minzer--Vyas--Yun improves the soundness dependence of their two-query PCP construction, giving perfect completeness, soundness $\varepsilon$, and proof length $n(\log n)^{\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))}$. Our proof exploits the product structure of the groups arising in KMS complexes. The main new ingredient is a decomposition lemma for Dehn functions, which separates the analysis of group relations into independent problems on much smaller factors, with only polynomial overhead.

papers.title: Integral Exponential Series: Fibonacci Weights and Implicit Equations
Learning memory forces and bounding frequency errors in fractional Kuramoto grids
papers.abstract: Missing history creates two different demands on a forecaster for a fractional grid: predicting frequency accurately and reconstructing memory well enough to bound the prediction error. We connect these demands through the hereditary force that remains after an integral observation correction. A compact decoder retains the directions most relevant to that force, and an exact decomposition separates omitted directions from coefficient error. A response-trained linear predictor and neural refinement learn the coefficients for frequency prediction. A separate force reconstruction supplies the reference for a nonlinear energy bound for the specified finite relaxation model, accounting for numerical propagation defects and the difference between the reference and point forecasts. For the outage transients studied here, refinement improves on the linear predictor across the time steps and memory parameters tested. Replacing the noisy origin states reveals why this gain can coexist with greater memory reconstruction error: the learned correction partly compensates for observation error. Separating prediction from reconstruction enables frequency bounds in cases where the point predictor alone cannot support them. A critical radius compares calibrated uncertainty with the angle margin available along the reference trajectory, explaining both issuance and abstention. Under jointly exchangeable calibration and test events, the calibrated guarantee bounds the marginal probability of issuing an invalid envelope. Together, these results connect uncertainty about history outside the observation window to frequency forecasts and explicit conditions for bounding their errors.

papers.title: Chimera states in a network of firefly oscillators
papers.abstract: We investigate chimera-like states in a network of identical firefly oscillators with nonlocal delayed coupling. For a uniform communication delay, the network exhibits a breathing phase-frequency chimera, characterized by the coexistence of frequency-locked and frequency-drifting populations and an oscillating incoherent-domain width. We then introduce heterogeneous pairwise communication delays to investigate a numerical analogue of the Sarfati-Peleg phenomenon observed in natural firefly swarms. In this regime, a recurring collective chorus coexists with character oscillators that flash persistently before or after the chorus. Cycle-resolved delay maps, role rasters, character probabilities, and spatial covariance diagnostics demonstrate the persistence and collective organization of these chorus-character roles. Although the uniform-delay and heterogeneous-delay states represent different forms of partial synchronization, the same firefly-oscillator framework supports both regimes. Finally, we construct a reduced analytical description in terms of a chorus-relative delay field and a memory field. The local dynamics is organized around a saturated subcritical pitchfork structure, producing a stable chorus equilibrium together with two stable character equilibria. The reduced model therefore provides a phenomenological description of the tri-stable chorus-character organization and its characteristic delay scale. Our results show that heterogeneous delayed interactions among identical relaxation oscillators can generate persistent temporal identities analogous to those reported in synchronous firefly swarms.

papers.title: Connecting Electroweak Fine-Tuning, Tens-of-GeV Dark Matter, and Exotic Higgs Decays in the GNMSSM
papers.abstract: In the general next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model (GNMSSM), we connect electroweak fine-tuning, a singlino dark matter candidate with mass around tens of GeV, and Exotic Higgs Decays, identifying a natural region characterized by the mass hierarchy $m_{\tilde{S}}<m_{\tilde{B}}<m_{\tilde{H}}$ and $\mu_{\rm tot}\in [200, 500]$ GeV. For fine-tuning measure $\Delta \leq 40$, the branching ratio $\mathrm{Br}(h\to a_sa_s)$ falls in the range 7\%$-$25\%, with the pseudoscalar mass $m_{a_s}$ lying mostly between 10 and 20 GeV. This region splits into two viable scenarios consistent with LZ 2024 direct detection: one where the lightest CP-even Higgs $h_1$ is SM-like ($h_1$ case), and another where the second-lightest $h_2$ is SM-like ($h_2$ case). LHC searches for $h\to a_sa_s \to b\bar{b}\tau^+\tau^-$ exclude 12\% (10\%) of samples with 12 GeV $\leq m_{a_s} \leq$ 15.5 GeV in the $h_1$ ($h_2$) case, while a substantial fraction remains accessible at the HL-LHC in the $h_2$ case. Our analysis unifies naturalness, dark matter, and observable exotic Higgs decays, yielding concrete targets for future experiments.

papers.title: Congruence density under sublattice inclusion
The limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of erdős problem 521
A Probabilistic Characterization of the Ideals of Resolvent Algebras
Pyramidal Columns Acting as Attention Heads
papers.abstract: Can the functional architecture of a Transformer attention head be given a biological construction? More specifically, could a suitable group of pyramidal columns in posterior temporal language regions (PTLRs) constitute the biological construction of a neuromorphic mechanical realization of an attention head, under a mathematical instantiation that need not coincide with its standard Transformer instantiation? This paper investigates this hypothesis by examining possible correspondences between the functional organization of attention heads and neurophysiological mechanisms operating within and across pyramidal columns involved in human language processing. Our analysis builds on a mechanical-structural description of Transformer attention heads as systems of simple neural networks linked through output-input and output-weight interconnections. We examine the functional organization of an attention head and the input-dependent transformations it produces, and ask how the corresponding processing relations could be constructed in biological neural tissue. We then identify candidate neural mechanisms of signal transmission and modulation within and across pyramidal columns that may jointly support such a construction. On this basis, we propose that a suitably organized group of pyramidal columns in PTLRs could constitute a biological construction of a neuromorphic mechanical realization of an attention head. Whether the required functional organization actually exists in PTLRs remains an open empirical question. The hypothesis does not require the biological system to reproduce the standard mathematical instantiation of Transformer attention: the same functional architecture may be mechanically realized and mathematically instantiated in a different way, consistent with its biological construction.

papers.title: Improved Elastic Weight Consolidation as an Optimization Constraint for Continual Learning
