Independent five-rater validation ($\alpha=0.961$) preserves the ordering; identical continuations and affect/formality controls confirm scale-related variation beyond generated wording. The axis is also behaviorally causal: positive steering moves Llama from $2.00$ to $3.17$ on a five-point macro scale for prompts admitting local responses. Steering strength and stability depend on the model's default operating regime. Together, these findings establish social granularity as a representational primitive: a continuous, ordered, causally manipulable direction organizing role-conditioned generation across model families.

papers.title: Hugoniot Relation for Multi-Temperature Euler Equations of Compressible Plasma Flows
Steering Visual Generation in Unified Multimodal Models with Understanding Supervision
papers.abstract: Unified multimodal models are envisioned to bridge the gap between understanding and generation. Yet, to achieve competitive performance, state-of-the-art models adopt largely decoupled understanding and generation components. This design, while effective for individual tasks, weakens the connection required for mutual enhancement, leaving the potential synergy empirically uncertain. We propose to explicitly restore this synergy by introducing Understanding-Oriented Post-Training (UNO), a lightweight framework that treats understanding not only as a distinct task, but also a direct supervisory signal to steer generative representations. By incorporating objectives that encode semantic abstraction (captioning) and structural details (visual regression), we enable effective gradient flow from understanding to generation. Extensive experiments on image generation and editing demonstrate that understanding can serve as an effective catalyst for generation.

papers.title: EgoEMG: A Multimodal Egocentric Dataset with Bilateral EMG and Vision for Hand Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Hand pose estimation from egocentric video is challenging under adverse visual conditions, such as occlusion. Wrist-worn surface electromyography (sEMG) measures muscle activity without requiring visual access to the hand, offering a wearable complement to egocentric cameras. Evaluating their combined use requires synchronized physiological and visual recordings with continuous pose annotations, which existing EMG-based hand pose datasets do not jointly provide. We introduce EgoEMG, a multimodal dataset pairing bilateral wrist sEMG with egocentric video and motion-capture-derived hand poses, supplemented by external multi-view RGB-D recordings. EgoEMG contains 25.9 hours of recordings from 68 participants, covering 60 bare-hand gesture classes and interactions with 10 everyday objects. We establish EMG-only, vision-only, and fusion benchmarks with shared 22-dimensional pose targets and evaluations on unseen users, gestures, and objects. For EMG-only estimation, EMGFormer achieves the lowest overall MAE among the compared methods on EgoEMG and competitive results on EMG2Pose. Our residual fusion model combines ViT and EMGFormer features. Adding EMG reduces error for both single-frame and temporal vision models, with MAE decreasing from $7.39^\circ$ to $7.06^\circ$ for ViT-L. The largest absolute reduction occurs when evaluating interactions with an unseen object. Generalization to unseen users remains challenging. Project page: this https URL .

papers.title: The First Token Knows: Single-Decode Confidence for Hallucination Detection
papers.abstract: Sampling-based uncertainty methods detect hallucinations by generating multiple answers and measuring agreement, often with additional semantic clustering. We study whether uncertainty is already visible in the first content-bearing answer token of a single greedy decode. We define first-token confidence, phi_first, as one minus the normalized entropy of the top-K first-token distribution. Across PopQA and TriviaQA with three 7-8B instruction-tuned models, phi_first matches or modestly exceeds semantic self-consistency while requiring only one decode instead of one greedy decode plus ten sampled generations and NLI clustering. A subsumption analysis shows that phi_first is moderately to strongly correlated with semantic agreement, and combining both signals yields only small additional AUROC gains. We position phi_first as a cheap deployment-oriented baseline for factual QA uncertainty estimation, while noting its limits for high-confidence falsehoods and long-form generation.

papers.title: Exact SU(2) Yang-Mills Waves from a Simple Ansatz
papers.abstract: We use an ansatz based on rotations of the Pauli basis to construct exact propagating solutions of the sourceless SU(2) Yang--Mills equations in $(3+1)$ dimensions. By examining and extending this ansatz, we obtain two wave families with nontrivial transverse structures and a family of finite-amplitude waves on a self-similar non-Abelian background. These solutions can retain a genuinely non-Abelian structure while admitting arbitrary wave profiles propagating at the speed of light and carrying the corresponding longitudinal electric or magnetic fields. We also investigate the parameter conditions for their non-Abelian character and their energy transport. For the self-similar family, we study the structure of its singular plane and construct suitable sources to replace the singular region while preserving wave propagation in the remaining regions. This offers a possible interpretation of these solutions as propagating fields outside sources.

papers.title: Training-Time Batch Normalization Reshapes Local Partition Geometry in Piecewise-Affine Networks
papers.abstract: The effect of batch normalization (BN) on the function realized during training is less understood than its effect on optimization. We study training-time BN in continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) networks through the affine regions they induce in local $\ell_\infty$ windows around the data. Conditioned on a mini-batch, every switching hyperplane of a BN layer with learned parameters and a general CPA activation is a translate of a hyperplane through the batch centroid, at an offset given by a standardized quantity times the batch spread, independent of the raw bias. We prove an exact formula, valid under general position, for the number of regions in a window in terms of window cuts and interior intersections. For a BN layer it gives a lower bound on the local count in terms of the standardized offsets; the bound depends on the batch only through its spread and not on the biases or the batch location. Without BN the best such bound is $1$: for any weights and batch, some biases leave the window as a single region. We prove that the formula holds in deeper layers, inside parent affine regions of any rank. By the exact formula, BN increases the expected local count whenever it increases the expected numbers of window cuts and of interior intersections, which we examine empirically. Offset distributions of networks trained on synthetic data, MNIST, CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet show higher window-cut rates under BN, and exact enumeration in two dimensions attributes most of the additional BN regions to interior intersections.

papers.title: PAIR-CI: Calibrated Conditional Independence Testing for Causal Discovery with Incomplete Data
papers.abstract: The standard constraint-based paradigm for causal discovery with incomplete data -- impute first, test second -- is frequently miscalibrated: any consistent conditional independence (CI) test rejects a true null with probability approaching 1 when imputation error induces spurious conditional dependence. We introduce PAIR-CI, a nonparametric CI test that restores calibration by integrating multiple imputation directly into the inferential procedure via a paired permutation design. PAIR-CI compares cross-validated models that include and exclude the candidate variable while receiving the same imputed conditioning set, so that imputation error cancels in their loss difference rather than contaminating the test statistic. A variance estimator that nests a provably consistent cross-validation estimator inside Rubin's rules yields inference that is asymptotically valid in the many-imputation limit and conservative by a derived, sign-definite mechanism -- to our knowledge, the first formal result combining these two inferential frameworks. In simulations, existing imputation-based CI tests exhibit false positive rates of 28-45% when data are missing not at random (MNAR), whereas PAIR-CI's pooled rate is at most 3.6%, exceeding the nominal 5% only in some cells with five or more conditioning variables. Integrated into the PC algorithm, PAIR-CI is stable across functional forms and missingness mechanisms, whereas every parametric pipeline we consider, including missing-value PC, has a regime in which it fails badly. On nonlinear network benchmarks it reduces structural Hamming distance by 18% (ALARM) and 11% (HAILFINDER) relative to missing-value PC and by 31-48% relative to test-wise deletion and imputation-based Fisher-$Z$ pipelines, while attaining the highest skeleton F1; when relationships are linear, a well-specified parametric pipeline remains preferable.

papers.title: Reentrant value fields as delayed coupled reaction-diffusion systems on finite graphs
Dante: An Open Source Model Pre-Training and Fine-Tuning Tool for the Dafne Federated Framework for Medical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Adapting pre-trained deep learning segmentation models to new clinical domains is a persistent challenge in medical image analysis, particularly when annotated data at the target site are scarce. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies offer a principled solution by selectively updating a controlled subset of model parameters, preserving previously acquired representations while reducing the risk of overfitting on small datasets. This paper introduces DAfNe TrainEr (Dante), an open-source module integrating with the Dafne federated segmentation ecosystem as a dedicated training and fine-tuning backend. Dante supports training from scratch with automatic architecture configuration, configurable layer freezing schedules, and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) extended to N-dimensional convolutional layers through channel-wise factorization. To validate the module, Gradual Unfreezing (GU) and LoRA are assessed across realistic cross-domain MRI transfer scenarios covering abdominal organ segmentation and brain white matter lesion segmentation, under full-data and few-shot conditions. GU reduced the epochs required to reach 85% of peak performance by up to 63.6% compared to training from scratch, while LoRA achieved Dice Similarity Coefficients up to 0.957 in data-rich scenarios. Both strategies outperformed the baseline across all tested domains, with gains amplified by richer pre-training datasets. These results suggest that Dante can support the adaptation of medical image segmentation models across the evaluated anatomical and imaging domains when annotated target data are limited. Dante code is available at this https URL while Dafne ecosystem project is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Calculating extremely high energy bremsstrahlung in matter
papers.abstract: Ultra-relativistic electrons initiate electromagnetic showers in ordinary matter that evolve through bremsstrahlung and pair production. At very high energy, the quantum mechanical duration of bremsstrahlung becomes longer than the mean free time to elastically scatter from the medium, leading to a significant suppression known at the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect. For some ranges of bremsstrahlung photon and initial electron energies $(k_\gamma,E)$, the duration becomes so long that it will also overlap with subsequent pair production by the bremsstrahlung photon, disrupting LPM suppression and drastically changing LPM predictions. We have previously calculated this change for extremely high energies ($k_\gamma \gg 2$ TeV or more, depending on the medium), for which the electron mass and medium-induced photon mass could be ignored. In this paper, we extend that analysis to lower (but still ultra-relativistic) energy by accounting for those masses, leading to a rich map of behavior in different regions of $(k_\gamma,E)$.

papers.title: Fuzzy Fingerprinting Encoder Pre-trained Language Models for Emotion Recognition in Conversations: Human Assessment and Validity Study
papers.abstract: In Emotion Recognition in Conversations (ERC), model decisions should align with nuanced human perception and ideally provide insights on the classification process. Standard encoder pre-trained language models (PLMs) are the state-of-the-art at these tasks but offer little insight into why a certain prediction is made. This is especially problematic in imbalanced datasets, where most utterances are labeled as neutral, making these models frequently misclassify minority emotions as the majority neutral class. To tackle this issue, we introduced a novel, interpretable approach to ERC by combining PLMs with Fuzzy Fingerprints (FFPs). FFP provide class-specific prototypes that reflect the characteristic class activation patterns in the PLM's latent space. They are derived by ranking and fuzzifying the activations of the pooled conversational context-dependent embeddings across training instances for each emotion. At inference time, each input utterance is similarly fuzzy fingerprinted and matched to the emotion prototypes using a fuzzy similarity function based on the aggregation of the intersection of the fuzzy sets that define each FFP. Experimental results show that FFP integration reduces overclassification into the neutral class and human evaluation further supports the adequacy of FFP predictions. Our proposed method thus bridges the gap between deep neural inference and human perception, performing at state-of-the-art level while simultaneously offering valuable insights into the classification procedure.

papers.title: ProS2T: Progressive Fusion with Structure-Shape Transformations for Source-Free Domain Adaptation from Scratch
papers.abstract: Most Vision-Language (ViL)-guided works for source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) still rely on source-trained models. In those methods, we observe that different source models yield close final performance on the same target domain, suggesting the source initialization may has limited impact. Motivated by this, we propose ViL-guided Fully-Source-Free Domain Adaptation (VF-SFDA) setting, which trains a target model from scratch using only unlabeled target data and a pretrained ViL model. Reliable ViL supervision is therefore critical, however, resizing and cropping during pre-processing can distort object shape or remove important structural cues, leading to inaccurate predictions. To address this, we propose Progressive Fusion with Structure-Shape Transformations (ProS2T). Its S2 module constructs complementary views: Structure Priority retains more image content, while Shape Priority largely preserves object proportions. Guided by our analysis of adaptation dynamics, ProS2T progressively fuses each view's ViL prediction with the same target model prediction to form two candidates, then selects the more confident one to generate hard pseudo-labels to supervise the target model, whose predictions guide ViL prompt updates. Experiments on Office-Home, VisDA-C, and DomainNet-126 demonstrate that ProS2T achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance compared to existing SFDA methods, despite operating under a stricter setting. Moreover, S2T improves ViL zero-shot classification and existing ViL-guided SFDA methods as a plug-and-play module.

papers.title: SplitZip: Ultra Fast Lossless KV Compression for Disaggregated LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Contemporary systems serving large language models (LLMs) have adopted prefill-decode disaggregation to load-balance between the compute-bound prefill phase and the memory-bound decode phase. Under this design, prefill workers generate a KV cache that must be transferred to decode workers before generation can begin. With these workers residing on different physical systems, this transfer becomes a significant bottleneck to serving LLMs at scale, especially for long-input and agentic workloads. Existing lossless codecs are unsuitable here as they primarily target offline weight compression, run on CPUs, or use variable-length coding whose compression cannot keep up with KV production during prefill. We introduce SplitZip, a GPU-friendly lossless compressor for KV cache transfer that preserves KV tensors bitwise and integrates into existing serving frameworks without modifying model execution. SplitZip exploits redundancy in floating-point exponents of KV activations, encoding frequent exponent values with fixed-length codes and routing rare exponents through a sparse escape stream of (position, value). A calibrated top-16 exponent codebook eliminates online histogramming, while the regular dense path and sparse escape correction make both encoding and decoding efficient on GPUs. On real BF16 activation tensors, SplitZip achieves $613.3$ GB/s compression throughput and $2181.8$ GB/s decompression throughput, outperforming prior lossless compressors on the critical codec path. End-to-end transfer experiments show up to $1.32\times$ speedup for BF16 KV cache transfer, $1.30\times$ speedup for TTFT, and $1.23\times$ increase in Request Throughput. The same approach extends to FP8 KV caches, providing up to $1.14\times$ compression over native E5M2. Code is available at this https URL

papers.title: Toward Fair Speech Technologies: A Comprehensive Survey of Bias and Fairness in Speech AI
papers.abstract: Speech technologies are deployed in high-stakes settings, yet fairness concerns remain fragmented across tasks and disciplines. Existing surveys either adopt a general machine-learning perspective that overlooks speech-specific properties or focus on a single task, missing failure patterns shared across the speech domain. Synthesizing over 400 studies spanning generation and perception tasks and emerging speech-language models, this survey presents a unified framework that links formal fairness definitions to evaluation, diagnosis, and mitigation. We formalize seven fairness definitions adapted to the speech modality and organize the field's conceptual expansion through three paradigms: Robustness, Representation, and Governance. We then ground evaluation metrics in the mathematical cores of these definitions, organizing them into six families and mapping each family back to the definitions it operationalizes. We diagnose bias sources along the speech processing pipeline, surfacing speech-specific mechanisms such as channel bias as a demographic proxy and annotation subjectivity in emotion labels. We systematize mitigation strategies across four intervention stages, mapping each to the diagnosed sources. Finally, we identify open challenges and propose directions for future research.

papers.title: Comparison of OpenAlex and Scopus coverage of German institutions' publications in top-tier journals
papers.abstract: OpenAlex has recently emerged as a leading alternative to proprietary bibliometric sources. However, concerns remain regarding the quality of its metadata, especially the institutional profiles which are crucial for evaluating organizations. This study assesses the quality of affiliation data in OpenAlex using German research institutions. Publications from top-tier journals were analyzed and institutional publication counts in OpenAlex were systematically compared with counts in Scopus. The results show that OpenAlex generally contains more publications at the journal level, reflecting its broader coverage. However, institutional publication counts in OpenAlex are consistently lower; it contained 6.8% fewer institution-paper links in the analyzed sample. Aggregate institutional counts nevertheless showed very high rank correlation and concordance with Scopus. Discrepancies varied substantially across fields, publishers and journals. Detailed investigation identified missing affiliation information, differences in institutional boundaries, and divergent year and journal assignments, while errors present in both databases. These findings suggest that OpenAlex is suitable for comparative institutional analyses in academic research but requires further improvement in affiliation metadata before it can be used for evaluation contexts that rely on absolute publication counts.

papers.title: Exploring Multivariate Data Using Median Absolute Deviation Depth
papers.abstract: This paper studies the moving median absolute deviation as a functional description of half mass concentration in univariate and multivariate distributions. Its minimizing location defines the median radius center. Because the original radius profile need not increase outward, a radial running maximum envelope is constructed. Under continuity and unique minimizer assumptions, normalization yields a continuous centrality score with maximality, outward monotonicity, and vanishing values at infinity. Euclidean distance provides similarity invariance, and a univariate derivative identity characterizes local boundary imbalance. Empirical constructions and numerical illustrations distinguish concentration geometry from centre-outward ordering and clarify the interpretation of central regions under asymmetric and multimodal distributions.

papers.title: A gravity interpretation for the complex saddles of the ABJM and spindle indices
papers.abstract: The superconformal index is a grand-canonical partition function that counts the 1/16-BPS states in the theory, and its Legendre transform with respect to reduced chemical potentials accounts for the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of electrically charged rotating black holes in anti-de Sitter spacetime. However, the superconformal index of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory appears to allow shifts in chemical potentials, and the contributions of the shifted terms diverge exponentially. We resolved this puzzle by showing the instability of wrapped D3-branes corresponding to shifts in the gravitational on-shell action. Analogously, we study the M5-brane instability criterion of the ABJM index and the spindle index.

papers.title: DeGenTWeb: A First Look at MGT-dominant Websites
papers.abstract: Many news reports have claimed that machine-generated text (MGT) from large language models (LLMs) is taking over the web. However, these claims are typically not based on a representative sample of the web, and the methodology underlying them is often opaque. Consequently, we lack an understanding of the true prevalence and characteristics of MGT on the web. We describe DeGenTWeb, which systematically identifies MGT-dominant websites: sites whose informational prose content is mostly MGT, with little human input. We show how to adapt detectors of MGT for use on web pages, and how to aggregate detection results from multiple pages on a site for accurate site-level categorization. DeGenTWeb mislabels only 0.12% of human-authored sites as MGT-dominant. We find that 20.9% of the sites archived by Common Crawl between January and July 2026 and 13.6% of the sites linked from Bing's search results in 2025 are MGT-dominant. These figures are lower bounds on the prevalence of MGT-dominant sites. We also find that the fraction of MGT-dominant sites is growing over time, and that many such sites share the same owner. We will release all of our code and data after publication.

papers.title: Quantum-Geometric Spin Magnetization and Spin Currents Across Altermagnetic Symmetry Classes
papers.abstract: Altermagnets host spin-split band structures despite vanishing equilibrium spin magnetization, making field-induced responses a direct probe of their quantum geometry. Based on symmetry, altermagnets can be classified into M-, S-, A-, and S/A-type according to the presence or absence of inversion and time-reversal symmetries. We develop a unified framework using a generalized quantum geometric tensor that captures both momentum translations and spin rotations of Bloch states. In particular, we introduce the Zeeman counterpart of the conventional spin quantum geometric tensor, whose real and imaginary parts define the Zeeman spin quantum metric and Zeeman spin Berry curvature, respectively. Using this framework, we study linear spin magnetization and spin currents induced by electric and magnetic fields. We show that M- and S-type altermagnets support intrinsic electric-field-induced spin currents and magnetic-field-induced spin magnetization, while A-type altermagnets exhibit both electric and magnetic field induced spin current and spin magnetization. For S/A-type altermagnets, neither inversion nor time-reversal symmetry alone determines the allowed responses. Applying our theory to the S-type $d$-wave altermagnet $\mathrm{FeSb}_2$ and a Rashba-coupled S/A-type $d$-wave altermagnet, we find complete agreement with the symmetry constraints. The predicted responses are sizable and within reach of magnetometry and spin-transport experiments. Our results establish a symmetry based quantum geometric framework for spin responses in altermagnets and highlight their potential for experimental detection and spintronic applications.

papers.title: LZn : Robust LoRa Frame Synchronization Under Frame Collisions and Ultra-Low SNR Conditions
papers.abstract: LoRa has become a widely adopted wireless modulation scheme in LPWANs due to its low cost, long range, and minimal transmission power. However, collisions between frames of the same spreading factor -- common in dense LoRa deployments -- prevent conventional LoRa receivers from detecting and correctly decoding frames. Recent work has introduced methods to improve recovery, yet their detection stage degrades sharply under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and high collision rates. In this work, we introduce LZn, a synchronization scheme driven by a minimum-based spectral intersection across consecutive symbols. While preamble search incurs a modest overhead, LZn reduces the cost of fine synchronization by two to three orders of magnitude compared to existing collision-tolerant receivers. Our method enables robust frame synchronization even under multiple packet overlaps or extremely low SNR conditions. We evaluate LZn on simulations and three independent, real-world LoRa datasets. LZn improves detection sensitivity by up to 10 dB and increases detection probability by up to 1.54x. In real-world datasets, LZn improves decoding by 3.46x in the most challenging single-user scenario and up to 1.22x in collision scenarios compared to the second best collision-tolerant scheme (TnB). These results demonstrate that LZn substantially improves the frame recovery of LoRa receivers, while remaining compatible with real-time requirements.

papers.title: Quantum Gromov--Hausdorff Convergence of Spectral Truncations for Compact Quantum Groups with Proper Length Functions
Multirate characterization of relaxation mechanisms for two nonequivalent nuclear spins 1/2 in a liquid using maximally entangled pseudo-pure quantum states
papers.abstract: Multirate characterization of spin responses in nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a promising approach to fingerprinting complex molecules in the presence of multiple relaxation mechanisms. Here we present experimental and theoretical investigations simultaneously accessing 8 relaxation rates describing the density matrix of two adjacent non-equivalent nuclear spins 1/2 (1H and 13C) belonging to a molecule in a liquid. The selected nuclear pair is stable with respect to chemical exchange. Some of the rates are obtained from conventional measurements of inversion recovery and nuclear Overhauser effect, while other, less conventional ones, are extracted from the relaxation initialized by the maximally entangled pseudo-pure Bell states (Bell PPSs) of the spin pair. The Bell PPSs are created using a hereby introduced method based on a detuned Hartmann-Hahn double resonance condition. Microscopic theory behind the measured relaxation rates is presented, and its consistency is demonstrated by several parameter-free tests. In particular, it is shown both theoretically and experimentally, that the eigenmodes of the off-diagonal relaxation of the two-spin density matrix can be selectively initialized using Bell PPSs. Our multirate analysis suggests that the measured off-diagonal relaxation is partly due to an unconventional mechanism arising from very weak J-couplings of the spin pair with fluctuating distant nuclear spins. Furthermore, we identify a dimensionless ratio of diagonal relaxation rates, which is determined exclusively by intra-pair magnetic dipolar interaction and hence possesses a universal value for a broad class of nuclear spin pairs. This value is consistent with both our experiments and other experiments reported in the literature.

papers.title: LLM-Flax: LLM-Generated Rules and Object Guidance for Neuro-Symbolic Task Planning
papers.abstract: Adapting a neuro-symbolic task planner to a new domain can require hand-authored symbolic rules and solved training instances for a learned object scorer. This paper presents LLM-Flax, which applies large language models (LLMs) to offline rule generation, failure recovery, and object scoring within the Flax planning pipeline. Generated rules undergo validation and corrective feedback before reuse, while runtime guidance operates within a shared planning budget. Experiments on MazeNamo and two additional domains show that the evaluated rule configuration improves planning success over manually authored rules while retaining the trained object scorer. Across eight MazeNamo settings, the mean success rate increases by approximately three percentage points. Controlled comparisons distinguish the effects of rule content from the choice of generator. Runtime recovery and object scoring do not establish an overall performance advantage under the evaluated planning budgets. These findings demonstrate the value of reusable LLM-generated rules and identify information quality and inference efficiency as central challenges for runtime guidance.

papers.title: A Novel Reinforcement Learning Based Framework for Scalable MIMO Interference Alignment
papers.abstract: Interference alignment (IA) is a widely recognized approach for mitigating inter-cell interference in multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks. Despite its effectiveness, practical deployment remains constrained by two major challenges, i.e., the need for global channel state information (CSI) at each transmitter and the complexity of deriving closed-form solutions for intricate MIMO systems. This work aims to maximize network throughput by effectively mitigating interference using an IA-inspired learning algorithm that addresses its aforementioned challenges. First, we propose a predictive, transformer-based IA framework that estimates CSI to reduce signaling overhead in small-scale MIMO systems. Next, we formulate the IA problem as a multi-objective optimization problem based on subspace coordination and develop two reinforcement learning-based algorithms to enhance the scalability of IA in large-scale MIMO systems. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methods significantly outperform conventional baselines with up to 30% average user throughput gains over the best performing baseline.

papers.title: Structure-Aware Tensorial Model Reduction
papers.abstract: This work investigates a two-stage method for constructing projection-based reduced-order models (ROMs) of parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs). Based on established tensorial ROM methodology, the proposed approach reduces dimensionality offline by encoding solution snapshots using a multi-linear Tucker factorization, so that a reduced basis which varies nonlinearly with PDE parameters can be rapidly constructed online and used in a Galerkin ROM. Two novel extensions of this strategy, tailored to the cases of structured PDEs and sparse parameter sampling, are presented: the construction of reduced bases orthonormalized with respect to a general discrete inner product, and the interpolation of encoded states via radial basis functions. Basic representation and ROM error estimates are presented demonstrating the validity of these modifications, and the approach is challenged on state-linear examples where monolithic-basis ROMs are known to struggle, including a realistic instance of Maxwell's equations in 3D. Results suggest that the proposed nonlinear basis ROM can effectively mitigate linear restrictions on Kolmogorov $n$-width while improving upon previous tensorial ROM technology, particularly in the highly nonlinear and data-limited regimes characteristic of practical use cases.

papers.title: On submersions with definite folds of manifolds with boundary into Euclidean spaces
Seeing Is No Longer Believing: Frontier Image Generation Models, Synthetic Visual Evidence, and Real-World Risk
papers.abstract: Image generation systems can produce plausible photographs, readable documents, and consistent depictions of people and places. Presented as records of real events, these outputs can influence decisions in news, finance, identity verification, medicine, and law. This narrative review examines public model documentation, incident reports, empirical studies, governance materials, and illustrative English and Chinese practitioner commentary available through 1 October 2026. We separate vendor capability claims, documented incidents, experimental findings, and prospective harm pathways. Realism, text rendering, reference consistency, conversational editing, search grounding, and low generation cost shape the conditions under which synthetic images acquire evidentiary weight. Documented episodes show how fabricated visuals enter public and institutional workflows, although public reporting cannot measure misuse prevalence for current releases. Comparing provider safeguards, provenance credentials, watermarks, platform labels, and statutory duties shows that origin signals do not verify a depicted event or transaction. Our framework matches artifact types and decision stakes to specific controls. Consequential decisions require authenticated source records, independent channel corroboration, and proportionate review before action.

papers.title: Regret-Optimal Control for Finite-State Systems
Marginal-Contribution Policy Gradients under Filtered Feedback for Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.abstract: We develop a unified treatment of credit assignment for RL training in multi-agent LLM systems. In these systems, several agents produce outputs, a mechanism such as a router deploys one, and only that output is rewarded. How should each agent learn from this one reward? Giving every agent the shared reward follows the right gradient but is noisy, because each agent's update carries every other agent's luck. We prove that rewarding only the selected agent (winner-take-all) is biased: it maximizes the agent's own expected reward from being selected, and the bias equals the reward it takes from its competitors. Between the two lie contribution signals, which subtract from the reward a baseline that ignores the agent's own output. We prove that once agents interact, an agent's contribution must depend on which other agents are present; that contribution signals keep the system's gradient, so they can help only by lowering noise; and that their noise splits into three terms, which determine when one beats shared reward. We show how to learn contributions from ordinary training data and, under routing, how to estimate them without extra generation. On GSM8K with Llama-3.2-3B agents, measured gradient noise matches these predictions and shows how to fix a noisy estimator. In pre-registered training with nine agents, a contribution signal learns faster than shared reward ($p=7.5\times10^{-5}$) and tolerates twice the learning rate.

papers.title: Presheaves and cocompletions in formal category theory
Koopman Operator Analysis of EEG Microstate Dynamics Reveals a Cross-Dataset, Hearing-Level Adjusted Signature of Tinnitus
papers.abstract: While major progress has been made in identifying EEG biomarkers for chronic Tinnitus, hearing loss remains as a major confound that must be accounted for in the identified effect. These markers have rarely been tested across independent datasets, a further test of robustness. We analyzed resting-state EEG microstate statistics, and developed a Koopman-operator description of the same microstate signal, carry a tinnitus-related difference that replicates across sites and survives adjustment for hearing level. Three public resting-state datasets (335 subjects; 234 tinnitus, 101 controls) were projected onto a fixed seven-map microstate template. Pooled across datasets, 2/56 microstate statistics differed consistently, and after adjustment for pure-tone average (PTA) none remained significant after FDR correction. Tinnitus subjects had a larger fraction of fast-decaying Koopman modes in all three datasets, and this difference survived PTA adjustment (pooled r=0.26, p=0.002). Microstate differences in tinnitus are substantially explained by hearing level; operator-level dynamics of the same signal retain a hearing-adjusted difference that generalizes across sites.

papers.title: Thermalization Regimes in a Chaotic Tavis-Cummings Model
AAC: Admissible-by-Architecture Differentiable Landmark Compression for ALT
papers.abstract: We introduce the Architecturally Admissible Compressor (AAC), which adapts landmark-based A* heuristics to query demand under a fixed label-memory budget. AAC provides two continuous relaxations of ALT (A*, Landmarks, and Triangle inequality) selection. With exact landmark distances, every parameter value defines a lower bound on shortest-path distance. Both relaxations deploy ALT using only the selected labels. The row-stochastic relaxation takes convex combinations of landmark distances. We characterize the maximal admissibility-preserving linear classes and prove that the relaxed and discrete optima coincide. The fractional relaxation mixes subset heuristics and supports continuous greedy (AAC-CG) with exact gradients and an entropy-regularized oracle for differentiable selection. For expected heuristic value, we prove an approximation guarantee with finite-step, oracle-error, and finite-sample terms. The limiting $1-1/e$ factor is optimal for arbitrary supplied pools and query distributions unless P${=}$NP. At matched label memory, AAC-CG reduces A* expansions by $1.9$-$22.7$% relative to farthest-point ALT (FPS-ALT) in all $19$ tested combinations of graph and memory budget across six road networks and two synthetic graphs. Each combination uses one $500$-query test split; all methods share distance tables when distances are symmetric. Canonical greedy also expands fewer nodes than FPS-ALT in all $19$ graph-budget pairs. AAC-CG achieves $99.6$% of canonical greedy's mean heuristic value on test queries, averaged over these pairs. AAC makes admissibility independent of training success, while its analysis and experiments distinguish selection quality from search efficiency.

papers.title: G-birationally rigid cubic threefolds
Scalable Hessian-vector products for tensor networks with application to quantum circuit compression
papers.abstract: Optimizing tensor networks with standard first-order methods often leads to slow convergence and getting trapped in local minima. Although second-order optimization offers enhanced robustness, explicitly constructing the full Hessian matrix is computationally prohibitive for large-scale systems. In this work, we bypass this bottleneck by introducing an analytical Hessian-vector product kernel designed for arbitrary compositions of linear maps. This two-pass algorithm leverages a recursive tangent-state propagation with a bounded virtual bond dimension to guarantee scalability. We demonstrate its use within a Riemannian trust-region method for quantum circuit compression. For time-evolution circuits with up to 17 layers, our method reproduces previous results in substantially fewer iterations, reducing wall-time by up to an order of magnitude. For deeper quantum circuits, incorporating second-order derivative information yields a better solution, reducing the final error to less than half that of the first-order result.

papers.title: A Loewner-Nirenberg phenomena for Ricci flow on compact manifolds with boundary.II
A Loewner-Nirenberg phenomenon for Ricci flow on compact manifolds with boundary
Layer-wise Geometric Approximation Rates for Deep Networks
papers.abstract: Depth is widely viewed as a central contributor to the success of deep neural networks, yet standard approximation results typically give error bounds only for the final output of a network. Inspired by classical multiscale expansions and multigrade deep learning, we give depth a scale-dependent interpretation by constructing a single network whose intermediate readouts approximate the target at successively finer scales. For any $f\in L^p([0,1]^d)$ with $1\le p <\infty$ and any integer $N\ge2$, we construct a single network of width $3dN+2d+4$ with the same activation pattern in every hidden layer, using sine in the first two neurons and $\mathtt{ReLU}$ in the rest. For every $\ell\ge0$, the $L^p$ approximation error of the readout $\Phi_\ell$ at layer $\ell+4$ is bounded by $(2d+1)\omega_{f,p}(N^{-\ell})$, where $\omega_{f,p}$ denotes the $L^p$ translation modulus of $f$. Under the Hölder condition $\omega_{f,p}(t)\le Ct^\alpha$ with $C>0$ and $0< \alpha \le 1$, this estimate yields the geometric bound $(2d+1)C N^{-\alpha\ell}$. More generally, if $\omega_{f,p}(t)$ has a known upper bound that tends to zero as $t\downarrow0$, we obtain a stopping rule for adaptive depth selection. We can stop at the first depth where the error bound meets the desired tolerance and later append layers to meet a tighter tolerance while keeping all earlier maps and readouts fixed.

papers.title: Debiased neural operators
papers.abstract: Neural operators are widely used to approximate solution maps of complex physical systems. In many applications, however, the goal is not to recover the full solution trajectory, but to summarize the solution trajectory via a scalar target quantity (e.g., a functional such as time spent in a target range, time above a threshold, accumulated cost, or total energy). In this paper, we introduce DOPE (debiased neural operator): a semiparametric estimator for such target quantities of solution trajectories obtained from neural operators. DOPE is broadly applicable to settings with both partial and irregular observations and can be combined with arbitrary neural operator architectures. We make three main contributions. (1) We show that, in contrast to DOPE, naive plug-in estimation can suffer from first-order bias. (2) To address this, we derive a novel one-step, Neyman-orthogonal estimator that treats the neural operator as a high-dimensional nuisance mapping between function spaces, and removes the leading bias term. For this, DOPE uses a weighting mechanism that simultaneously accounts for irregular observation designs and for how sensitive the target quantity is to perturbations of the underlying trajectory. (3) To learn the weights, we extend automatic debiased machine learning to operator-valued nuisances via Riesz regression. We demonstrate the benefits of DOPE across various numerical experiments.

papers.title: Verbal tics in frontier language models: A critical review of current releases, research evidence, and public discussion
papers.abstract: Repeated praise, canned reassurance, formulaic contrasts, and conspicuous vocabulary figure prominently in discussions of large language models. Context governs how these habits should be read. A conventional phrase can orient a reader, whereas a fluent answer can reinforce a false belief. This critical review examines linguistic habits and sycophancy across eight developer families. We verify public offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, ByteDance, Moonshot AI, DeepSeek, and Xiaomi against official release and API documentation through 1 October 2026. We then synthesize empirical research on lexical overrepresentation, stylistic variation, social warmth, and agreement alongside benchmark methods and dated public discussions in English and Chinese. Published studies document recurring linguistic patterns and agreement that distorts human judgment, but comparable measurements for the newest releases remain sparse in the retrieved material. Current user accounts report both persistent complaints and clearer prose, and experiences vary by task and prompt design. We propose separate measures for recurrence, contextual appropriateness, and belief distortion paired with exact service records and language-specific annotation. This framework keeps claims about writing quality and conversational reliability testable as model services change.

papers.title: Distributivity, affineness, and the structure sheaf
Minimax optimal dual control -- The single input case
Kill-Probability-Maximization Guidance: Breaking from the Miss-Distance-Minimization Paradigm
papers.abstract: Classical guidance laws aim at minimizing the miss distance, thus implicitly determining the minimum warhead lethality radius required against nominal targets. However, nonnominal targets or scenarios might render the designed warhead insufficient, causing a significant degradation in the single-shot kill probability (SSKP). We propose a guidance methodology that shifts the interceptor's objective from minimizing the miss distance to directly maximizing the SSKP, while taking into account the warhead's probabilistic lethality model. Complying with the generalized separation theorem, the paradigm presented here modifies deterministic differential-game-based guidance laws using Bayesian decision theory. For this purpose, we obtain the saddle-point solution of the deterministic differential game whose objective is the SSKP. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate substantial SSKP improvement over the standard and recently introduced estimation-aware guidance laws, when tested against nominal and nonnominal evasively maneuvering targets.

papers.title: Multilinear embedding theorem for fractional sparse operators
The Stability of Wasserstein Shadow Projection and its Application to Transfer Learning
Analog Resonant Recurrent Neural Networks via Metacircuits
papers.abstract: Physical neural networks offer a promising route to fast and energy-efficient edge intelligence by embedding computation in the intrinsic dynamics of materials and devices. However, processing temporal signals requires recurrent networks with memory, whose trained dynamics are hard to reproduce faithfully in physical systems. Here we present an analog resonant recurrent neural network (R$^2$NN) implemented as a metacircuit of coupled local resonators. A reformulated mechanical-electrical analogy based on frequency-dependent negative resistances maps a trained network one-to-one onto the metacircuit, with every trainable parameter realized as a resistance. Training tunes local resonances and global resistive couplings so that past responses persist as recurrent memory and interfere with incoming inputs, and the resulting impedance landscape routes different frequencies to distinct outputs. Exploiting this recurrent memory, the metacircuit solves a temporal-parity task whose output depends on the entire input history. Building on the learned frequency selectivity, stand-alone R$^2$NN systems classify raw tactile, acoustic and vibration signals in real time and directly drive downstream hardware. This work establishes engineered locally resonant dynamics as a physical substrate for recurrent neural computation and opens a route to compact, low-latency neural hardware for machine intelligence at the edge.

papers.title: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
Representation Before Training: A Practical Benchmark for Generative Medical Event Model Tokenization
papers.abstract: Generative medical event models use tokenized sequences of patient timelines as input, but practical guidance on the many decisions around tokenization is limited because most studies keep the tokenizer fixed while scaling architecture or data. We benchmark quantization granularity, reference-range anchoring, code--value fusion, numeric and temporal encodings, and schema harmonization across 156 models. Using both Llama-3.2-style and Qwen3-style architectures, all models were trained on full MIMIC-IV hospitalizations from three initialization seeds under a shared training recipe, and linear probes evaluated frozen 24-hour representations across eight binary and regression outcome families during hours 24--48. Fused tokens pairing codes with value deciles produced statistically significant gains in six of eight families over unfused deciles, including all four regression families ($+0.032$ to $+0.114$ Spearman correlation) and vital-signs classification ($+0.033$ AUROC), with 38 of 48 comparisons significant across all six quantization schemes (seven of eight families). Next-token training organized unfused and fused centile embeddings into ordered trajectories and made clinical reference ranges linearly decodable in unfused centiles (93--97\% accuracy). Neither reference-range anchoring nor finer quantization consistently improved 24-hour probes. Event order and admission-relative RoPE shortened inputs while marginally raising all eight family means over explicit time tokens (five and four statistically significant). Mapping native input to the Common Longitudinal Intensive Care Unit Data Format (CLIF) cut training tokens by 71.4\% and vocabulary size by 97.8\%, with statistically significant gains in four of eight families. These findings show that compact, expert-curated tokenizations can outperform more granular and continuous alternatives under a shared training recipe.

papers.title: Debate as Reward: A Multi-Agent Reward System for Scientific Ideation via RL Post-Training
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated potential in automating scientific ideation, yet current approaches relying on iterative prompting or complex multi-agent architectures often suffer from hallucination or computational inefficiency. A critical bottleneck in applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to this open-ended domain is reward hacking---where models exploit imperfect evaluation proxies to maximize scores without producing genuine scientific innovation. To address these limitations, we propose an RL framework explicitly tailored for high-quality scientific idea generation. We propose the first multi-agent reward function designed to serve as a judge, decoupling methodological validation from implementation details while providing strict binary rewards that are robust to reward hacking. To effectively optimize against this sparse signal, we utilize an unbiased variant of Group Relative Policy Optimization to mitigate artificial length bias. We ground our training in a curated dataset of problem-solution pairs extracted from ICLR 2024 and NeurIPS 2025 proceedings. Experiments demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across expert-evaluated metrics of novelty, feasibility, and effectiveness.

papers.title: The hydrodynamical response of cold circumgalactic clouds to quasar radiation
papers.abstract: Recent simulations increasingly resolve the small-scale structure of the circumgalactic medium (CGM), but the dynamical impact of ionising radiation on its cold $10^4$ K component remains poorly understood. We investigate the evolution of cold gas structures exposed to quasars' EUV radiation. We develop an analytical framework to describe the evolution of such clouds, introducing a new threshold that defines when a cloud becomes radiation-shielded. The framework is validated using radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of single static clouds. It predicts three evolutionary paths: (i) an optically thin regime, in which radiation uniformly ionises the cloud; (ii) a radiation-shielded regime, where the cloud remains largely unaffected; and (iii) a rocket-effect regime, in which the propagation of the ionisation front ionises the illuminated side while compressing the opposite side, later accelerating the surviving cold clump. In the latter regime, the cloud's Ly$\alpha$ luminosity can be up to one order of magnitude higher than the optically thin case. Such luminosities are as high as $70\%$ of the values obtained from a fluorescent regime without considering hydrodynamical response. Unless the cloud is shielded, at least $\sim 50$-$60\,\%$ of Ly$\alpha$ emission arises from recombination. Applying this framework to both a ray crossing a population of clouds, and a ray propagating inside a cold stream, we find that the cold CGM around bright quasars ($L_{\mathrm{\nu,LL}} \sim 10^{31.6} \, \mathrm{erg\, s^{-1}\, Hz^{-1}}$) is likely fully ionised, whereas the one around faint quasars ($L_{\mathrm{\nu,LL}} \sim 10^{28.6} \, \mathrm{erg\, s^{-1}\, Hz^{-1}}$) predominantly experiences a rocket-effect regime. These results imply that the hydrodynamical response of cold CGM structures to quasar radiation must be considered when deriving their physical properties, particularly for faint quasars.

papers.title: Subliminal Transfer of Unsafe Behaviors in AI Agent Distillation
papers.abstract: Recent work on subliminal learning has shown that language models can transmit semantic traits through data with no apparent connection to those traits. Whether this phenomenon extends to agentic systems, where policies are learned from trajectories rather than static text, remains an open question with critical safety implications. We present the first empirical evidence that unsafe agent behaviors transfer subliminally through model distillation, demonstrated across several settings. In the primary setting, we construct a teacher agent with a deletion bias, a tendency to perform destructive file-system actions through an API-style tool interface, and distill it into a student using only trajectories from ostensibly safe tasks, with all explicit deletion keywords filtered. In the secondary setting, we replicate the threat model with shell commands, replacing API calls with shell commands and operationalizing the bias as a preference for chmod over semantically equivalent alternatives (e.g., chown, setfacl) when issuing the first permission-related command. Despite sanitation, students inherit measurable biases. Over 1,500 trials per configuration, the API student chooses a destructive action first on 35.5% of ambiguous tasks (vs. 1.2% baseline), and the Bash student's chmod-first rate reaches 30-55% (vs. 0-10% baseline). In a multi-turn environment where tool calls execute, 33.9% of student episodes end with a resource irreversibly destroyed (vs. 6.4% baseline). On TerminalBench we observe a smaller effect (7.7% vs. 0% baseline). Explicit data sanitation is therefore insufficient as a defense; mitigating behavioral bias transfer in agentic systems will require fundamentally new strategies.

papers.title: Structural interpretability in SVMs with truncated orthogonal polynomial kernels
Beyond Visual Cues: Semantic-Driven Token Filtering and Expert Routing for Anytime Person ReID
papers.abstract: Any-Time Person Re-identification (AT-ReID) necessitates the robust retrieval of target individuals under arbitrary conditions, encompassing both modality shifts (daytime and nighttime) and extensive clothing-change scenarios, ranging from short-term to long-term intervals. However, existing methods are highly relying on pure visual features, which are prone to change due to environmental and time factors, resulting in significantly performance deterioration under scenarios involving illumination caused modality shifts or cloth-change. In this paper, we propose Semantic-driven Token Filtering and Expert Routing (STFER), a novel framework that leverages the ability of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to generate identity consistency text, which provides identity-discriminative features that are robust to both clothing variations and cross-modality shifts between RGB and IR. Specifically, we employ instructions to guide the LVLM in generating identity-intrinsic semantic text that captures biometric constants for the semantic model driven. The text token is further used for Semantic-driven Visual Token Filtering (SVTF), which enhances informative visual regions and suppresses redundant background noise. Meanwhile, the text token is also used for Semantic-driven Expert Routing (SER), which integrates the semantic text into expert routing, resulting in more robust multi-scenario gating. Extensive experiments on the Any-Time ReID dataset (AT-USTC) demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art results. Moreover, the model trained on AT-USTC was evaluated across 5 widely-used ReID benchmarks demonstrating superior generalization capabilities with highly competitive results. Our code will be available soon.

papers.title: AgentGA: Evolving Code Solutions in Agent-Seed Space
papers.abstract: We present AgentGA, a framework that evolves autonomous code-generation runs by optimizing the agent seed: the task prompt plus optional parent archives that initialize a fresh workspace. The outer loop searches over reusable starting conditions rather than editing code directly. Each generation launches a fresh autonomous run in an isolated workspace, while selected parent archives provide inherited artifacts that descendants can inspect and reuse. AgentGA couples a population-level genetic algorithm with long-horizon agents, deterministic 1:1 elite tournaments, and online operator allocation through a modified Hedge controller. We evaluate the approach for tabular AutoML on the 16-competition Weco-Kaggle Lite benchmark, including model-matched AIDE and AutoGluon comparisons. AgentGA with DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731) achieves 71.13% mean Exceeds % of Human, compared with 57.61% for model-matched AIDE and 57.89% for AutoGluon, outranking AIDE on 14/16 tasks. A control that removes inheritance, in which every agent starts from scratch, reaches 65.76% under AgentGA's stopping rule and 67.25% at the full budget, above a single long-lived agent (61.20%) and below AgentGA. These descriptive results support agent-seed optimization as a practical design choice for autonomous code-search systems, without isolating the causal contribution of inheritance.

papers.title: VoxSafeBench: Not Just What Is Said, but Who, How, and Where
papers.abstract: As speech language models (SLMs) transition from personal devices into shared, multi-user environments, their responses must account for far more than the words alone. Who is speaking, how they sound, and where the conversation takes place can each turn an otherwise benign request into one that is unsafe, unfair, or privacy-violating. Existing benchmarks, however, largely focus on basic audio comprehension, study individual risks in isolation, or conflate content that is inherently harmful with content that only becomes problematic due to its acoustic context. We introduce VoxSafeBench, among the first benchmarks to jointly evaluate social alignment in SLMs across three dimensions: safety, fairness, and privacy. VoxSafeBench adopts a Two-Tier design: Tier1 evaluates content-centric risks using matched text and audio inputs, while Tier2 targets audio-conditioned risks in which the transcript is benign but the appropriate response hinges on the speaker, paralinguistic cues, or the surrounding environment. To validate Tier2, we include intermediate perception probes and confirm that frontier SLMs can successfully detect these acoustic cues yet still fail to act on them appropriately. Across 22 tasks with bilingual coverage, we find that safeguards appearing robust on text often degrade in speech: safety awareness drops for speaker- and scene-conditioned risks, fairness erodes when demographic differences are conveyed vocally, and privacy protections falter when contextual cues arrive acoustically. Together, these results expose a pervasive speech grounding gap: current SLMs frequently recognize the relevant social norm in text but fail to apply it when the decisive cue must be grounded in speech. Code and data are publicly available at: this https URL

papers.title: Quantification and Regulation of Energy Reserves for Distributed Frequency and Voltage Control of Cyber-Physical Microgrids
papers.abstract: The introduction of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) has led to the formation of cyber-physical Microgrids (MGs) and Networks of MGs (NMGs). MGs and NMGs can operate in islanded mode, transforming the grid into a more distributed system. This has led to extensive studies in the literature on distributed hierarchical control strategies. Previous works have proposed distributed secondary level frequency and voltage regulation control schemes for Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)- based Grid-Forming (GFM) inverters with State of Charge (SoC) balancing. However, control applications in terms of service-based reserves and local resource adequacy in MGs are largely unexplored. Therefore, this paper proposes a BESS-based GFM inverter energy reserves framework, to quantify reserves for hierarchical control operation. Additionally, to partially regulate the proposed energy reserves, we propose the formulation of a modified Distributed-Averaging Proportional-Integral (DAPI) controller with regulation energy reserve consensus. Modal analysis is performed to demonstrate the stability guarantees of energy consensus under simplified assumptions. Cyber-physical Controller Hardware-In-the-Loop (CHIL) simulation is performed on an MG topologically based on the IEEE 13 bus test feeder system in MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed scheme results illustrate effective frequency and voltage regulation along with improved power and energy sharing across droop-controlled and Virtual Synchronous Machine (VSM) controlled inverters

papers.title: AI-Enabled Qubit Loss Detection and Replenishment Strategy for Atom Array Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: Qubit loss is a major source of error in atom-array quantum computing and invalidates the algebraic structure of the standard stabilizer formalism for quantum error-correcting codes. On the one hand, it complicates decoding; on the other hand, it introduces tochastic flicker patterns in stabilizers as a hallmark of qubit loss. Here, we develop an artificial-intelligence-enabled decoder based on a spatiotemporal graph neural network (STGNN) architecture to extract spatial and temporal correlations from syndrome histories. Our decoder performs a dual-head task, simultaneously correcting standard Pauli errors and identifying the locations of qubit loss. Our decoder achieves significantly higher logical accuracy than both the traditional minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) algorithm and even delayed-erasure MWPM decoders that use qubit-loss information from the final round as input. Furthermore, we integrate the decoder into a sliding-window framework for dynamic qubit replenishment. We emphasize that our approach does not involve any additional physical measurements beyond stabilizer measurements, and detects qubit loss and determines its replacement strategy through a purely software-based AI policy. We demonstrate that our approach bounds the accumulation of lost qubits and fully restores the fault-tolerant scaling behavior. For realistic near-term error rates, this work provides a robust and scalable framework for correcting qubit-loss errors, paving the way for more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

papers.title: On the Rokhlin lemma for infinite measure-preserving bijections
Stabilization of finite-energy grid states of a quantum harmonic oscillator by reservoir engineering with two dissipation channels
Phase transition in compressed sensing using log-sum penalty and adaptive smoothing
papers.abstract: In many real-world problems, recovering sparse signals from underdetermined linear systems remains a fundamental challenge. Although $\ell_1$ norm minimization is widely used, it suffers from estimation bias that prevents it from reaching the Bayes-optimal reconstruction limit. Nonconvex alternatives, such as the log-sum penalty, have been proposed to promote stronger sparsity. However, maintaining their algorithmic stability is challenging. To address this challenge, we introduce an adaptive smoothing strategy within an approximate message passing framework to mitigate algorithmic instability. Furthermore, we evaluate the typical exact-recovery threshold for Gaussian measurement matrices using the replica method and state evolution. The results indicate that the adaptive method achieves exact recovery over a broader region than $\ell_1$-norm minimization, although metastable states hinder the attainment of the information-theoretic limit.

papers.title: Estimating Continuous Treatment Effects with Two-Stage Kernel Ridge Regression
papers.abstract: We study the problem of estimating the effect function for a continuous treatment, which maps each treatment value to a population-averaged outcome. A central challenge in this setting is confounding: treatment assignment often depends on covariates, creating selection bias that makes direct regression of the response on treatment unreliable. To address this issue, we propose a two-stage kernel ridge regression method. In the first stage, we learn a model for the response as a function of both treatment and covariates; in the second stage, we use this model to construct pseudo-outcomes that correct for distribution shift, and then fit a second model to estimate the treatment effect. Although the response varies with both treatment and covariates, the induced effect function obtained by averaging over covariates is typically much simpler, and our estimator adapts to this structure. Our optimal learning bounds are achieved without estimating the conditional treatment density, thereby bypassing a major bottleneck in existing methods. Furthermore, we introduce a fully data-driven model selection procedure that achieves provable adaptivity to both the unknown degree of overlap and the spectral decay of the underlying kernel.

papers.title: AffectAgent: Collaborative Multi-Agent Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: LLM-based multimodal emotion recognition relies on static parametric memory and often hallucinates when interpreting nuanced affective states. In this paper, given that single-round retrieval-augmented generation is highly susceptible to modal ambiguity and therefore struggles to capture complex affective dependencies across modalities, we introduce AffectAgent, an affect-oriented multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation framework that leverages collaborative decision-making among agents for fine-grained affective understanding. Specifically, AffectAgent comprises three jointly optimized specialized agents, namely a query planner, an evidence filter, and an emotion generator, which collaboratively perform analytical reasoning to retrieve cross-modal samples, assess evidence, and generate predictions. These agents are optimized end-to-end using Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) with a shared affective reward to ensure consistent emotion understanding. Furthermore, we introduce Modality-Balancing Mixture of Experts (MB-MoE) and Retrieval-Augmented Adaptive Fusion (RAAF), where MB-MoE dynamically regulates the contributions of different modalities to mitigate representation mismatch caused by cross-modal heterogeneity, while RAAF enhances semantic completion under missing-modality conditions by incorporating retrieved audiovisual embeddings. Extensive experiments on MER-UniBench demonstrate that AffectAgent achieves superior performance across complex scenarios. Our code will be released at: this https URL .

papers.title: Asymptotically Stable Gait Generation and Instantaneous Walkability Determination for Planar Almost Linear Biped with Knees
papers.abstract: A class of planar bipedal robots with unique mechanical properties has been proposed, where all links are balanced around the hip joint, preventing natural swinging motion due to gravity. A common property of their equations of motion is that the inertia matrix is a constant matrix, there are no nonlinear velocity terms, and the gravity term contains simple nonlinear terms. By performing a Taylor expansion of the gravity term and making a linear approximation, it is easy to derive a linearized model, and calculations for future states or walkability determination can be performed instantaneously without the need for numerical integration. This paper extends the method to a planar biped robot model with knees. First, we derive the equations of motion, constraint conditions, and inelastic collisions for a planar 6-DOF biped robot, design its control system, and numerically generate a stable bipedal gait on a horizontal plane. Next, we reduce the equations of motion to a 3-DOF model, and derive a linearized model by approximating the gravity term as linear around the expansion point for the thigh frame angle. Through numerical simulations, we demonstrate that calculations for future states and walkability determination can be completed in negligible time. By applying control inputs to the obtained model, performing state-space realization, and then discretizing it, instantaneous walkability determination through iterative calculation becomes possible. Through detailed gait analysis, we discuss how the knee joint flexion angle and the expansion point affect the accuracy of the linear approximation, and the issues that arise when descending a small step.

papers.title: Dynamic Multi-Robot Task Allocation under Uncertainty and Communication Constraints: A Game-Theoretic Approach
papers.abstract: We study dynamic multi-robot task allocation under uncertain task completion, time-window constraints, and incomplete information. Tasks arrive online over a finite horizon and must be completed within specified deadlines, while agents operate from distributed hubs with limited sensing and communication. We model incomplete information through hub-based sensing regions that determine task visibility and a communication graph that governs inter-hub information exchange. Using this framework, we propose Iterative Best Response (IBR), a decentralized policy in which each agent selects the task that maximizes its marginal contribution to the locally observed welfare. We compare IBR against three baselines: Earliest Due Date first (EDD), Hungarian algorithm, and Stochastic Conflict-Based Allocation (SCoBA), on a city-scale package-delivery domain with up to 100 drones and varying task arrival scenarios. Under full and sparse communication, IBR achieves competitive task-completion performance with lower computation time.

papers.title: A Mechanistic Analysis of Looped Reasoning Language Models
papers.abstract: Reasoning has become a central capability in large language models. Recent research has shown that reasoning performance can be improved by looping an LLM's layers in the latent dimension, resulting in looped reasoning language models. Despite promising results, few works have investigated how the internal dynamics and computation of looped models differ from that of standard feedforward models. In this paper, we conduct a mechanistic analysis of latent states and layer behavior in looped language models. We analyze cyclic recurrence and show that for many of the studied models each layer in the cycle converges to a distinct fixed point; consequently, the recurrent block follows a consistent cyclic trajectory in the latent space. We provide evidence that as these fixed points are reached, attention-head behavior stabilizes, leading to constant behavior - stages of inference - across recurrences. Empirically, we discover that recurrent blocks tend to organize their computation such that it closely mirrors that of feedforward models, repeating this behavior in depth with each iteration. We study how architectural choices influence the emergence and stability of these cyclic fixed points and stages of inference, providing practical guidance for looped language model design.

papers.title: An analogue of irreducible cuspidal representations for the group $PGL(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
TEMPER: Reducing Attribute Leakage from Face Recognition Embeddings
papers.abstract: Face recognition embeddings encode soft-biometric attributes such as gender and ethnicity, which can be inferred from templates. This paper proposes TEMPlate Entropy Regularisation (TEMPER), a post-hoc method that removes an attribute. TEMPER learns a linear map of the embedding in a split-latent variational autoencoder. The map is initialised at the principal component analysis (PCA) solution of the embeddings and trained to maximise the predictive entropy of an auxiliary attribute classifier. A relational term keeps the similarities of mated pairs close to the embedding similarities. We evaluate the removal of gender and a four-group ethnicity label from ArcFace embeddings against ten prior post-hoc methods and two label-free controls. Every method is trained on VGGFace2 and tested on IJB-C and RFW at false match rates down to $10^{-4}$. Leakage is the balanced accuracy of the strongest of four attacker families trained on transformed VGGFace2 templates. TEMPER retains the highest IJB-C true match rate at a false match rate of $10^{-3}$ at every leakage threshold for both attributes. TEMPER retains a true match rate of 82.4% at a gender leakage of at most 52.5%, close to chance, against 76.7% for the best prior method. In the ablation, this improvement comes from the PCA initialisation and the relational term.

papers.title: Entanglement inequalities for timelike intervals within dynamical holography
papers.abstract: This paper extends our previous work ( arXiv:2504.14313 ) of a single timelike subregion to two, in the framework of AdS$_3$-Vaidya holography. We confirm the positivity of timelike mutual information and the statement of weak monotonicity when the subregions are non-overlapping. We also study entanglement inequalities such as Araki-Lieb inequality and strong subadditivity when the intervals start to overlap. In line with the recent findings in the literature, we provide explicit working examples showing that the timelike version of the strong subadditivity is generally violated in these setups, even though the statements of subadditivity and Araki-Lieb inequality hold true.

papers.title: Information-theoretic bound on thermodynamic efficiency and the generalized Carnot theorem
papers.abstract: We derive a bound on the efficiency of thermal engines that can be sharper than Carnot's limit. It is a function of statistical correlations between the engine internal state and Hamiltonian, can be saturated even in finite-time cycles, and applies to both classical and quantum engines. Specifically, the bound establishes the exact maximal efficiency of engines operating with multiple baths, tightening the upper limit set by Carnot's theorem. Then, we show that an engine made of a quantum dot coupled with fermionic baths can achieve the bound, even when operating beyond the quasistatic regime. The bound relates thermodynamic efficiency to statistical correlations of the working medium and identifies conditions for its saturation in classical and quantum cycles.

papers.title: On the Structure of Risk Contribution: A Leave-One-Out Decomposition into Inherent and Correlation Risk
papers.abstract: Risk Contribution (RC) is a widely used risk attribution metric that assigns each position a share of portfolio volatility, with contributions that sum to total portfolio volatility. This paper proposes a leave-one-out decomposition of RC into two interpretable components at the position level: an inherent term (position's own scaled variance) and a correlation term (covariance with the other holdings). Unlike the X-sigma-rho framework, which uses the position's correlation with the full portfolio, ICD uses covariance with the other holdings, yielding qualitatively different diagnostic signals when a position is large relative to the portfolio. The contribution is the interpretive framing and an exact identity linking the components to incremental volatility (iVol), which allows the discrete condition under which a position reduces portfolio volatility to be stated in closed form. That condition differs from the marginal condition and the two can disagree for over-hedged or levered positions. The decomposition also inherits RC's strict additivity. Empirical illustrations on three multi-asset portfolios show the components shift differently across regimes, distinguishing stand-alone volatility spikes from correlation breakdown, and demonstrate value for risk reporting, stress testing, and attribution.

papers.title: Spectral Softening and the Structural Breakdown of Thermodynamic Equilibrium
papers.abstract: Reversible quasistatic thermodynamics requires normalizable instantaneous equilibrium states and dynamics allowing their attainment or tracking. We examine these requirements in a driven two-dimensional quadratic Hamiltonian with an angular-momentum coupling and a spatially uniform momentum shift $p_c(t)$, representable by a time-dependent vector potential. Its undriven part has normal-mode frequencies $\omega_\pm=\omega_1\pm\omega_2$ and the Fock--Darwin structure of a charged oscillator in a perpendicular magnetic field. At the exact soft-mode endpoint $\omega_-=0$, confinement is lost in one normal-mode sector. For every strictly positive $\omega_-$, the canonical Gibbs state remains normalizable; only at the endpoint does the canonical trace cease to be finite. In the quasi-soft regime, where $\omega_-\to0^+$, exact adjacent-level couplings yield a dimensionless adiabatic parameter proportional to $|\dot p_c|/\omega_-^2$. The standard adiabatic criterion requires this parameter to remain much smaller than unity. At a fixed occupation and a fixed nonzero driving rate, however small, this parameter grows without bound as $\omega_-\to0^+$, eventually violating this criterion. In an open system, thermal tracking additionally depends on relaxation relative to the driving timescale. An explicit linear system--bath coupling illustrates why the relaxation rate cannot be inferred from the soft-mode spacing alone. Finally, the thermal Wigner function and its classical limit show that phase-space confinement is lost in both descriptions at the soft-mode endpoint. Taken together, our results show that canonical equilibrium is lost at $\omega_-=0$. For $\omega_->0$, the Gibbs state exists, while the ability to track it dynamically depends on the driving and dissipation.

papers.title: TinyNeRV: Compact Neural Video Representations via Capacity Scaling, Distillation, and Low-Precision Inference
papers.abstract: Neural Representations for Videos (NeRV) encode video sequences within neural decoder parameters, enabling direct frame reconstruction from temporal indices. Deploying NeRV in resource-constrained settings remains challenging because reconstruction quality, model capacity, decoding cost, and numerical precision are tightly coupled.
